    Exchangeable μ X ↔
      ∀ n (i : Fin n),
        blockLaw μ X (fun j : Fin (n + 1) => (Equiv.swap i.castSucc i.succ j).val) =
          prefixLaw μ X (n + 1)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.Exchangeable.of_forall_adjacent_swap
decls.doc: The introduction form of `Exchangeable.iff_forall_adjacent_swap`.
decls.statement:
theorem of_forall_adjacent_swap {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α}
    (hX : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ)
    (h :
      ∀ n (i : Fin n),
        blockLaw μ X (fun j : Fin (n + 1) => (Equiv.swap i.castSucc i.succ j).val) =
          prefixLaw μ X (n + 1)) :
    Exchangeable μ X

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.blockLaw
decls.doc:
The finite-dimensional law of a family along a coordinate selection `k`.

The index type is arbitrary: nothing about a finite selection needs the indices to be natural
numbers, and `ExchangeableFamily` selects from an arbitrary type. Sequence-level users get the
`ι = ℕ` case by unification.
decls.statement:
def blockLaw (μ : Measure Ω) (X : ι → Ω → α) {m : ℕ} (k : Fin m → ι) :
    Measure (Fin m → α)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.prefixLaw
decls.doc: The law of the first `n` coordinates of a process.
decls.statement: def prefixLaw (μ : Measure Ω) (X : ℕ → Ω → α) (n : ℕ) : Measure (Fin n → α)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.pathLaw
decls.doc: The law of the whole process as a measure on path space.
decls.statement: def pathLaw (μ : Measure Ω) (X : ℕ → Ω → α) : Measure (ℕ → α)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.prefixProj
decls.doc: Projection from path space to the first `n` coordinates.
decls.statement: def prefixProj (α : Type*) (n : ℕ) (x : ℕ → α) : Fin n → α

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.shift
decls.doc: The left shift on one-sided path space.
decls.statement: def shift (α : Type*) (x : ℕ → α) : ℕ → α

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.permReindex
decls.doc: Reindex a one-sided path by a permutation of time.
decls.statement: def permReindex (π : Equiv.Perm ℕ) (x : ℕ → α) : ℕ → α

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.ExchangeableAt
decls.doc: Finite exchangeability at `n`: the first `n` coordinates have permutation-invariant law.
decls.statement: def ExchangeableAt (μ : Measure Ω) (X : ℕ → Ω → α) (n : ℕ) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.Exchangeable
decls.doc: Finite exchangeability at every length.
decls.statement: def Exchangeable (μ : Measure Ω) (X : ℕ → Ω → α) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.FullyExchangeable
decls.doc: Full exchangeability: the path law is invariant under every permutation of `ℕ`.
decls.statement: def FullyExchangeable (μ : Measure Ω) (X : ℕ → Ω → α) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.Contractable
decls.doc:
Contractability, or spreadability: finite-dimensional laws are invariant under strictly
increasing finite subsequences.
decls.statement: def Contractable (μ : Measure Ω) (X : ℕ → Ω → α) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.blockLaw_def
decls.statement:
theorem blockLaw_def (μ : Measure Ω) (X : ι → Ω → α) {m : ℕ} (k : Fin m → ι) :
    blockLaw μ X k = μ.map (fun ω i => X (k i) ω)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.blockLaw_apply_of_measurable
decls.statement:
theorem blockLaw_apply_of_measurable (μ : Measure Ω) (X : ι → Ω → α) {m : ℕ} (k : Fin m → ι)
    (hXk : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X (k i)) μ) {S : Set (Fin m → α)} (hS : MeasurableSet S) :
    blockLaw μ X k S = μ ((fun ω i => X (k i) ω) ⁻¹' S)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.blockLaw_apply_rectangle
decls.doc:
The block law of `X` along `k`, evaluated on a measurable rectangle `Set.univ.pi B`, is the
measure of the coordinate-wise preimage `{ω | ∀ i, X (k i) ω ∈ B i}` — the rectangle specialization
of `blockLaw_apply_of_measurable`.

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.prefixLaw_def
decls.statement:
theorem prefixLaw_def (μ : Measure Ω) (X : ℕ → Ω → α) (n : ℕ) :
    prefixLaw μ X n = blockLaw μ X (fun i : Fin n => i.val)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.pathLaw_def
decls.statement:
theorem pathLaw_def (μ : Measure Ω) (X : ℕ → Ω → α) :
    pathLaw μ X = μ.map (fun ω i => X i ω)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.prefixProj_apply
decls.statement:
theorem prefixProj_apply (n : ℕ) (x : ℕ → α) (i : Fin n) :
    prefixProj α n x i = x i.val

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.shift_apply
decls.statement: theorem shift_apply (x : ℕ → α) (n : ℕ) : shift α x n = x (n + 1)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.permReindex_apply
decls.statement:
theorem permReindex_apply (π : Equiv.Perm ℕ) (x : ℕ → α) (n : ℕ) :
    permReindex π x n = x (π n)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.permReindex_permReindex
decls.doc: Composing `permReindex π` after `permReindex σ` reindexes by `σ * π`.
decls.statement:
theorem permReindex_permReindex (π σ : Equiv.Perm ℕ) (x : ℕ → α) :
    permReindex (α := α) π (permReindex (α := α) σ x) =
      permReindex (α := α) (σ * π) x

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.measurable_prefixProj
decls.doc: The prefix projection is measurable.
decls.statement: theorem measurable_prefixProj (n : ℕ) : Measurable (prefixProj α n)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.measurable_shift
decls.doc: The one-sided path-space shift is measurable.
decls.statement: theorem measurable_shift : Measurable (shift α)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.map_prefixProj_pathLaw
decls.doc: The prefix law is the pushforward of the path law by `prefixProj`.

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.map_blockLaw
decls.doc: A coordinatewise measurable map sends block laws to block laws.
decls.statement:
theorem map_blockLaw (μ : Measure Ω) {X : ι → Ω → α} {m : ℕ} (k : Fin m → ι)
    {f : α → β} [MeasurableSpace β] (hf : Measurable f)
    (hXk : ∀ i : Fin m, AEMeasurable (X (k i)) μ) :
    (blockLaw μ X k).map (fun x : Fin m → α => fun i => f (x i)) =
      blockLaw μ (fun n ω => f (X n ω)) k

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.map_prefixLaw
decls.doc: A coordinatewise measurable map sends prefix laws to prefix laws.
decls.statement:
theorem map_prefixLaw (μ : Measure Ω) {X : ℕ → Ω → α}
    {f : α → β} [MeasurableSpace β] (hf : Measurable f)
    (n : ℕ) (hX : ∀ i : Fin n, AEMeasurable (X i.val) μ) :
    (prefixLaw μ X n).map (fun x : Fin n → α => fun i => f (x i)) =
      prefixLaw μ (fun n ω => f (X n ω)) n

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.map_pathLaw
decls.doc: A coordinatewise measurable map sends path laws to path laws.
decls.statement:
theorem map_pathLaw (μ : Measure Ω) {X : ℕ → Ω → α}
    {f : α → β} [MeasurableSpace β] (hf : Measurable f)
    (hX : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ) :
    (pathLaw μ X).map (fun x : ℕ → α => fun i => f (x i)) =
      pathLaw μ (fun n ω => f (X n ω))

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.map_blockLaw_reindex
decls.doc:
Push a block law forward along a coordinate reindexing: selecting the coordinates of
`blockLaw μ X k` through `g : Fin p → Fin n` yields the block law along `k ∘ g`.
decls.statement:
theorem map_blockLaw_reindex (μ : Measure Ω) {X : ι → Ω → α} {n p : ℕ}
    (k : Fin n → ι) (g : Fin p → Fin n) (hXk : ∀ j : Fin n, AEMeasurable (X (k j)) μ) :
    (blockLaw μ X k).map (fun x : Fin n → α => fun i : Fin p => x (g i)) =
      blockLaw μ X (k ∘ g)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.measurable_reindex
decls.doc: Reindexing the coordinates of path space along `φ` is measurable.
decls.statement:
theorem measurable_reindex (φ : ℕ → ℕ) :
    Measurable (fun x : ℕ → α => fun k => x (φ k))

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.map_reindex_pathLaw
decls.doc: Reindexing a path law gives the path law of the reindexed process.
decls.statement:
theorem map_reindex_pathLaw (μ : Measure Ω) {X : ℕ → Ω → α}
    (hX : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ) (φ : ℕ → ℕ) :
    (pathLaw μ X).map (fun x : ℕ → α => fun k => x (φ k)) =
      pathLaw μ (fun k ω => X (φ k) ω)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.map_reindex_prefixProj_pathLaw
decls.doc:
Projecting the `φ`-reindexed path law onto its first `n` coordinates gives the law of the
block `(X (φ 0), …, X (φ (n-1)))`.
decls.statement:
theorem map_reindex_prefixProj_pathLaw (μ : Measure Ω) {X : ℕ → Ω → α}
    (hX : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ) (φ : ℕ → ℕ) (n : ℕ) :
    ((pathLaw μ X).map (fun x : ℕ → α => fun k => x (φ k))).map (prefixProj α n) =
      blockLaw μ X (fun i : Fin n => φ i.val)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.map_prefixLaw_castLE
decls.doc:
Projecting the prefix law on `Fin n` onto its first `m ≤ n` coordinates (via `Fin.castLE`)
gives the prefix law on `Fin m`.
decls.statement:
theorem map_prefixLaw_castLE (μ : Measure Ω) {X : ℕ → Ω → α} {m n : ℕ} (hmn : m ≤ n)
    (hX : ∀ i : Fin n, AEMeasurable (X i.val) μ) :
    (prefixLaw μ X n).map (fun x : Fin n → α => fun i : Fin m => x (Fin.castLE hmn i)) =
      prefixLaw μ X m

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.Exchangeable.exchangeableAt
decls.statement:
theorem Exchangeable.exchangeableAt {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α}
    (h : Exchangeable μ X) (n : ℕ) : ExchangeableAt μ X n

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.ExchangeableAt.permute
TauCeti.Probability.FullyExchangeable.permute
TauCeti.Probability.ConditionallyIIDWith
decls.doc:
Conditional i.i.d.-ness with a specified directing measure `ν`: the random measure `ν` is
measurable, and along every finite selection `k` of **distinct** coordinates the *joint* law of
`(ν, block)` is the `ν`-disintegration `∫ δ_{ν ω} ⊗ (ν ω)^{⊗m} dμ(ω)`.

Constraining the joint law, rather than just the block's marginal, is exactly what makes this the
conditional statement: see `MixedIIDWith` for the marginal-only version and
`mixedIIDWith_of_conditionallyIIDWith` for the arrow between them.
decls.statement: def ConditionallyIIDWith (μ : Measure Ω) (X : ι → Ω → α) (ν : Ω → ProbabilityMeasure α) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.ConditionallyIIDWith.intro
decls.doc: Constructor: a measurable directing measure together with the joint-law disintegration.
decls.statement:
theorem ConditionallyIIDWith.intro {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ι → Ω → α}
    {ν : Ω → ProbabilityMeasure α}
    (hν : Measurable ν)
    (h : ∀ (m : ℕ) (k : Fin m → ι), Function.Injective k →
      μ.map (fun ω => (ν ω, fun i : Fin m => X (k i) ω)) =
        μ.bind fun ω =>
          (Measure.dirac (ν ω)).prod (ProbabilityMeasure.pi fun _ : Fin m => ν ω).toMeasure) :
    ConditionallyIIDWith μ X ν

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.conditionallyIIDWith_iff
decls.doc: Simp normal form for `ConditionallyIIDWith`.
decls.statement:
theorem conditionallyIIDWith_iff {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ι → Ω → α}
    {ν : Ω → ProbabilityMeasure α} :
    ConditionallyIIDWith μ X ν ↔
      Measurable ν ∧
        ∀ (m : ℕ) (k : Fin m → ι), Function.Injective k →
          μ.map (fun ω => (ν ω, fun i : Fin m => X (k i) ω)) =
            μ.bind fun ω =>
              (Measure.dirac (ν ω)).prod
                (ProbabilityMeasure.pi fun _ : Fin m => ν ω).toMeasure

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.ConditionallyIID
decls.doc: Conditional i.i.d.-ness: existence of a directing measure.
decls.statement: def ConditionallyIID (μ : Measure Ω) (X : ι → Ω → α) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.ConditionallyIID.of_directing
decls.doc: Constructor from a directing measure together with its witness.
decls.statement:
theorem ConditionallyIID.of_directing {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ι → Ω → α}
    {ν : Ω → ProbabilityMeasure α} (h : ConditionallyIIDWith μ X ν) : ConditionallyIID μ X

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.conditionallyIID_iff
decls.doc: Simp normal form for the existential wrapper `ConditionallyIID`.
decls.statement:
theorem conditionallyIID_iff {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ι → Ω → α} :
    ConditionallyIID μ X ↔ ∃ ν : Ω → ProbabilityMeasure α, ConditionallyIIDWith μ X ν

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.ConditionallyIIDWith.measurable_directing
decls.doc: The directing measure of a `ConditionallyIIDWith` witness is measurable.
decls.statement:
theorem ConditionallyIIDWith.measurable_directing {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ι → Ω → α}
    {ν : Ω → ProbabilityMeasure α} (h : ConditionallyIIDWith μ X ν) : Measurable ν

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.ConditionallyIIDWith.jointLaw_eq_disintegration
decls.doc: The defining joint-law disintegration of a `ConditionallyIIDWith` witness.
decls.statement:
theorem ConditionallyIIDWith.jointLaw_eq_disintegration {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ι → Ω → α}
    {ν : Ω → ProbabilityMeasure α} (h : ConditionallyIIDWith μ X ν)
    {m : ℕ} (k : Fin m → ι) (hk : Function.Injective k) :
    μ.map (fun ω => (ν ω, fun i : Fin m => X (k i) ω)) =
      μ.bind fun ω =>
        (Measure.dirac (ν ω)).prod (ProbabilityMeasure.pi fun _ : Fin m => ν ω).toMeasure

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.ConditionallyIID.exists_directing
decls.doc: A `ConditionallyIID` family has a directing measure.

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.ConditionallyIIDWith.comp_injective
decls.doc:
Conditional i.i.d.-ness with a named directing measure is preserved by reindexing along an
injection. The directing measure is unchanged.
decls.statement:
theorem ConditionallyIIDWith.comp_injective
    {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ι → Ω → α} {ν : Ω → ProbabilityMeasure α}
    (h : ConditionallyIIDWith μ X ν) {f : κ → ι} (hf : Function.Injective f) :
    ConditionallyIIDWith μ (fun j => X (f j)) ν

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.ConditionallyIID.comp_injective
decls.doc: Conditional i.i.d.-ness is preserved by reindexing along an injection.
decls.statement:
theorem ConditionallyIID.comp_injective
    {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ι → Ω → α} (h : ConditionallyIID μ X)
    {f : κ → ι} (hf : Function.Injective f) :
    ConditionallyIID μ fun j => X (f j)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.mixedIIDWith_of_conditionallyIIDWith
decls.doc:
**The easy arrow.** A directing measure is in particular a mixing representative: the mixture
identity is the joint disintegration with the `ν` coordinate integrated out.

Taking the second marginal of both sides does exactly that. On the left, `Measure.snd_map_prodMk₀`
discards the `ν` coordinate needing only measurability of `ν` itself — which the predicate
supplies — so no hypothesis on the coordinates of `X` is required. On the right, naturality of
`bind` pushes the marginal inside the mixture, where each `δ_{ν ω}` factor integrates away.
decls.title: The easy arrow
decls.statement:
theorem mixedIIDWith_of_conditionallyIIDWith {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α}
    {ν : Ω → ProbabilityMeasure α} (h : ConditionallyIIDWith μ X ν) : MixedIIDWith μ X ν

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.mixedIID_of_conditionallyIID
decls.doc: The existential form of the easy arrow.
decls.statement:
theorem mixedIID_of_conditionallyIID {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α}
    (h : ConditionallyIID μ X) : MixedIID μ X

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.coinKernel
decls.doc:
**The two-point kernel.** `coinKernel p` is the law of one `Bool`-valued flip of a coin that
comes up `true` with probability `p`.

Phrasing the example through this kernel — rather than through a `Bernoulli` random variable —
keeps it independent of any particular parametrized-distribution API: all it needs is that the
family is measurable in the bias.
decls.title: The two-point kernel
decls.statement: def coinKernel (p : I) : ProbabilityMeasure Bool

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.coinKernel_toMeasure
decls.doc: The measure underlying `coinKernel p` is Mathlib's Bernoulli measure on `Bool`.
decls.statement:
theorem coinKernel_toMeasure (p : I) :
    (coinKernel p : Measure Bool) = bernoulliMeasure true false p

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.coinKernel_apply_true
decls.doc: The bias is read back off the coin: `coinKernel p` gives mass `p` to `{true}`.
decls.statement:
theorem coinKernel_apply_true (p : I) :
    (coinKernel p : Measure Bool) {true} = (toNNReal p : ℝ≥0∞)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.measurable_coinKernel
decls.doc: The two-point kernel is measurable in the bias, so it can direct a mixture.
decls.statement: theorem measurable_coinKernel : Measurable coinKernel

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.conditionallyIIDWith_coinFlips
decls.doc:
**The worked example.** Draw a bias from `π`, then flip i.i.d. coins with that bias: the
resulting `Bool`-valued sequence is conditionally i.i.d. with directing measure
`ω ↦ coinKernel ω.1`.

This is the sharp conditional statement, not just the mixture identity: the generating construction
puts the sequence and its directing measure on one space and pins their joint law.
decls.title: The worked example
decls.statement:
theorem conditionallyIIDWith_coinFlips :
    ConditionallyIIDWith (iidMixtureLaw π coinKernel) (fun n ω => ω.2 n)
      fun ω => coinKernel ω.1

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.conditionallyIID_coinFlips
decls.doc: The coin-flip sequence is conditionally i.i.d. (existential form).
decls.statement:
theorem conditionallyIID_coinFlips :
    ConditionallyIID (iidMixtureLaw π coinKernel) fun n ω => ω.2 n

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.exchangeable_coinFlips
decls.doc: The coin-flip sequence is exchangeable.
decls.statement:
theorem exchangeable_coinFlips :
    Exchangeable (iidMixtureLaw π coinKernel) fun n ω => ω.2 n

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.contractable_coinFlips
decls.doc: The coin-flip sequence is contractable.
decls.statement:
theorem contractable_coinFlips :
    Contractable (iidMixtureLaw π coinKernel) fun n ω => ω.2 n

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.exists_map_toNNReal_eq_dirac_of_iIndepFun_coinFlips
decls.doc:
**Independent flips force a deterministic bias.** If the coordinates of the coin-flip sequence
are independent, then the law of the bias — pushed forward along `toNNReal` — is a Dirac
measure.
decls.title: Independent flips force a deterministic bias
decls.statement:
theorem exists_map_toNNReal_eq_dirac_of_iIndepFun_coinFlips [IsProbabilityMeasure π]
    (h : iIndepFun (fun n (ω : I × (ℕ → Bool)) => ω.2 n) (iidMixtureLaw π coinKernel)) :
    ∃ c : ℝ≥0∞, π.map (fun p : I => (toNNReal p : ℝ≥0∞)) = Measure.dirac c

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.toNNReal_ennreal_injective
decls.doc:
The bias-to-mass map `I → ℝ≥0∞` is injective, so a degenerate image law means a degenerate
bias law.
decls.statement:
theorem toNNReal_ennreal_injective :
    Function.Injective fun p : I => (toNNReal p : ℝ≥0∞)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.not_iIndepFun_coinFlips
decls.doc:
**Exchangeable but not independent.** With the bias itself drawn from a nondegenerate two-point
law `Ber(a, b, r)` — two distinct biases `a ≠ b`, each of positive probability — the coin flips are
exchangeable (`exchangeable_coinFlips`) yet dependent.

So `ConditionallyIID` is strictly wider than i.i.d., and the directing measure the construction
supplies is genuinely random rather than an a.e. constant.
decls.title: Exchangeable but not independent
decls.statement:
theorem not_iIndepFun_coinFlips {a b r : I} (hab : a ≠ b) (hr₀ : r ≠ 0) (hr₁ : r ≠ 1) :
    ¬ iIndepFun (fun n (ω : I × (ℕ → Bool)) => ω.2 n)
      (iidMixtureLaw (bernoulliMeasure a b r) coinKernel)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.conditionallyIIDWith_const_of_mixedIIDWith
decls.doc:
**At a constant `ν` the conditional identity is free.** The joint law of `(p, block)` is the
block law pushed forward by `Prod.mk p`, and the disintegration `δ_p ⊗ p^{⊗m}` is the product law
pushed forward by the same map, so the mixture identity already gives the joint one.
decls.title: At a constant `ν` the conditional identity is free

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.conditionallyIIDWith_const_iff_mixedIIDWith
decls.doc:
**The two de Finetti predicates agree at a constant witness.** In general only
`mixedIIDWith_of_conditionallyIIDWith` is available and the two need not agree; at a constant `ν`
the converse holds too, so they coincide.
decls.title: The two de Finetti predicates agree at a constant witness

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.conditionallyIIDWith_const_iff_iIndepFun_and_map_eq
decls.doc:
**A constant directing measure means plain i.i.d.**: `fun _ => p` witnesses
`ConditionallyIIDWith` exactly when the coordinates are independent and each has law `p`.
decls.title: A constant directing measure means plain i.i.d

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.ConditionallyIIDWith.of_iIndepFun_identDistrib
decls.doc:
**An i.i.d. sequence is conditionally i.i.d.**, with the constant directing measure
`ω ↦ μ.map (X 0)`. This is the sharp form of the roadmap's first worked example: the constant
random measure is a genuine *directing measure*, not merely a mixing representative.
`MixedIIDWith.of_iIndepFun_identDistrib` is the mixture form it projects down to.
decls.title: An i.i.d. sequence is conditionally i.i.d

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.ConditionallyIID.of_iIndepFun_identDistrib
decls.doc: **An i.i.d. sequence is conditionally i.i.d.** (existential directing-measure form).
decls.title: An i.i.d. sequence is conditionally i.i.d

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.iidMixtureLaw
decls.doc:
**The canonical conditionally i.i.d. law.** Draw a parameter `t` from `π`, then sample the
coordinates i.i.d. from `P t`, keeping `t` as the first coordinate of the sample space
`T × (ℕ → α)`.

Retaining the parameter is what makes this a *conditional* construction rather than only a mixture
of i.i.d. laws: the sequence and its directing measure live on the same space, so the joint law of
the two can be compared with the disintegration `ConditionallyIIDWith` demands.
decls.title: The canonical conditionally i.i.d. law
decls.statement: def iidMixtureLaw (π : Measure T) (P : T → ProbabilityMeasure α) : Measure (T × (ℕ → α))

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.iidMixtureLaw_def
decls.doc: The canonical law unfolded as the `π`-mixture of the parameter-tagged countable powers.
decls.statement:
theorem iidMixtureLaw_def (π : Measure T) (P : T → ProbabilityMeasure α) :
    iidMixtureLaw π P =
      π.bind fun t => (Measure.dirac t).prod (Measure.infinitePi fun _ : ℕ => (P t : Measure α))

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.isProbabilityMeasure_iidMixtureLaw
decls.doc:
The canonical law is a probability measure. Measurability of `P` is needed, not decorative:
`Measure.bind` against a non-measurable kernel is the zero measure.
decls.statement:
theorem isProbabilityMeasure_iidMixtureLaw [IsProbabilityMeasure π] (hP : Measurable P) :
    IsProbabilityMeasure (iidMixtureLaw π P)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.iidMixtureLaw_map_fst
decls.doc: The parameter coordinate of the canonical law is distributed as `π`.
decls.statement:
theorem iidMixtureLaw_map_fst (hP : Measurable P) :
    (iidMixtureLaw π P).map Prod.fst = π

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.iidMixtureLaw_map_directing
decls.doc: The directing measure of the canonical law has the prescribed mixing law `π.map P`.
decls.statement:
theorem iidMixtureLaw_map_directing (hP : Measurable P) :
    (iidMixtureLaw π P).map (fun ω => P ω.1) = π.map P

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.conditionallyIIDWith_iidMixtureLaw
decls.doc:
**The canonical process is conditionally i.i.d.** For a measurable family `P`, the coordinate
process of `iidMixtureLaw π P` is conditionally i.i.d. with directing measure `ω ↦ P ω.1`: along
every finite selection of distinct coordinates, the joint law of the directing measure and the
selected block is the disintegration `∫ δ_{P ω.1} ⊗ (P ω.1)^{⊗ Fin m}`.

This is the sharp conditional conclusion — the directing measure is pinned to the process, not
merely to the block laws — which is what makes `iidMixtureLaw` a realization of `P` as a directing
measure rather than only as a mixing representative.
decls.title: The canonical process is conditionally i.i.d
decls.statement:
theorem conditionallyIIDWith_iidMixtureLaw (hP : Measurable P) :
    ConditionallyIIDWith (iidMixtureLaw π P) (fun n ω => ω.2 n) (fun ω => P ω.1)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.conditionallyIID_iidMixtureLaw
decls.doc: The canonical process is conditionally i.i.d. (existential form).
decls.statement:
theorem conditionallyIID_iidMixtureLaw (hP : Measurable P) :
    ConditionallyIID (iidMixtureLaw π P) fun n ω => ω.2 n

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.mixedIIDWith_iidMixtureLaw
decls.doc: The prescribed family is in particular a mixing representative of the canonical process.
decls.statement:
theorem mixedIIDWith_iidMixtureLaw (hP : Measurable P) :
    MixedIIDWith (iidMixtureLaw π P) (fun n ω => ω.2 n) fun ω => P ω.1

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.exchangeable_iidMixtureLaw
decls.doc: The canonical process is exchangeable.
decls.statement:
theorem exchangeable_iidMixtureLaw (hP : Measurable P) :
    Exchangeable (iidMixtureLaw π P) fun n ω => ω.2 n

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.contractable_iidMixtureLaw
decls.doc: The canonical process is contractable.
decls.statement:
theorem contractable_iidMixtureLaw (hP : Measurable P) :
    Contractable (iidMixtureLaw π P) fun n ω => ω.2 n

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.pathLaw_iidMixtureLaw
decls.doc:
The path law of the canonical process is the `π.map P`-mixture of infinite product measures —
the de Finetti mixture representation, here with the mixing law prescribed in advance.
decls.statement:
theorem pathLaw_iidMixtureLaw [IsProbabilityMeasure π] (hP : Measurable P) :
    pathLaw (iidMixtureLaw π P) (fun n ω => ω.2 n)
      = (π.map P).bind fun Q => Measure.infinitePi fun _ : ℕ => (Q : Measure α)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.exists_map_eq_dirac_of_iIndepFun_iidMixtureLaw
decls.doc:
**The construction is genuinely richer than i.i.d.** If the canonical process happens to have
independent coordinates, then its mixing law `π.map P` is a point mass — so a nondegenerate `π.map
P` produces an exchangeable sequence that is *not* independent, and the directing measure the
construction supplies is genuinely random rather than an a.e. constant.
decls.title: The construction is genuinely richer than i.i.d
decls.statement:
theorem exists_map_eq_dirac_of_iIndepFun_iidMixtureLaw [IsProbabilityMeasure π]
    (hP : Measurable P) (h : iIndepFun (fun n (ω : T × (ℕ → α)) => ω.2 n) (iidMixtureLaw π P)) :
    ∃ Q : ProbabilityMeasure α, π.map P = Measure.dirac Q

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.ConditionallyIIDWith.exchangeable
decls.doc: A sequence with a named directing measure is exchangeable.
decls.statement:
theorem ConditionallyIIDWith.exchangeable {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α}
    {ν : Ω → ProbabilityMeasure α} (h : ConditionallyIIDWith μ X ν) : Exchangeable μ X

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.ConditionallyIID.exchangeable
decls.doc: A conditionally i.i.d. sequence is exchangeable.
decls.statement:
theorem ConditionallyIID.exchangeable {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α}
    (h : ConditionallyIID μ X) : Exchangeable μ X

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.ConditionallyIIDWith.contractable
decls.doc: A sequence with a named directing measure is contractable.
decls.statement:
theorem ConditionallyIIDWith.contractable {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α}
    {ν : Ω → ProbabilityMeasure α} (h : ConditionallyIIDWith μ X ν) : Contractable μ X

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.ConditionallyIID.contractable
decls.doc: A conditionally i.i.d. sequence is contractable.
decls.statement:
theorem ConditionallyIID.contractable {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α}
    (h : ConditionallyIID μ X) : Contractable μ X

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.ConditionallyIIDWith.of_pathLaw
decls.doc:
**Path-law transfer, at a named directing measure.** If the coordinate process is conditionally
i.i.d. under the path law of `X` with directing measure `ν`, then `X` is conditionally i.i.d. with
directing measure `ν ∘ (ω ↦ fun i => X i ω)`.

Both sides of the disintegration identity move along the path map: the joint law by
`Measure.map_map`, the mixture by `bind_map`.
decls.title: Path-law transfer, at a named directing measure

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.conditionallyIID_of_conditionallyIID_pathLaw
decls.doc:
**Path-law transfer for the conditional predicate**, existential form. The roadmap names this
`conditionallyIID_transfer`; the name here matches its mixture counterpart
`mixedIID_of_mixedIID_pathLaw`.
decls.title: Path-law transfer for the conditional predicate
decls.statement:
theorem conditionallyIID_of_conditionallyIID_pathLaw {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α}
    (hX_meas : ∀ n, Measurable (X n))
    (h : ConditionallyIID (pathLaw μ X) fun n p => p n) :
    ConditionallyIID μ X

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.ConditionallyIIDWith.lintegral_mul_indicator_iInter
decls.doc:
**The weighted block identity.** Integrating the joint-law disintegration of
`ConditionallyIIDWith` against a weight `g (ν ω)` times the indicator of the event that a block of
`m` distinct coordinates lands in `B` replaces the block by the power `(ν ω) B ^ m`.

Taking `g = 1` recovers the block probabilities that `MixedIIDWith` already determines; the content
of the conditional predicate is that an arbitrary weight in the directing measure may be carried
along.
decls.title: The weighted block identity
decls.statement:
theorem ConditionallyIIDWith.lintegral_mul_indicator_iInter
    (h : ConditionallyIIDWith μ X ν) (hX : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ)
    {m : ℕ} {k : Fin m → ℕ} (hk : Function.Injective k)
    {g : ProbabilityMeasure α → ℝ≥0∞} (hg : Measurable g) (hB : MeasurableSet B) :
    ∫⁻ ω, g (ν ω) * (⋂ i : Fin m, X (k i) ⁻¹' B).indicator (1 : Ω → ℝ≥0∞) ω ∂μ
      = ∫⁻ ω, g (ν ω) * (ν ω : Measure α) B ^ m ∂μ

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.ConditionallyIIDWith.lintegral_mul_indicator_single
decls.doc: One-coordinate form of the weighted block identity.
decls.statement:
theorem ConditionallyIIDWith.lintegral_mul_indicator_single
    (h : ConditionallyIIDWith μ X ν) (hX : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ) (i : ℕ)
    {g : ProbabilityMeasure α → ℝ≥0∞} (hg : Measurable g) (hB : MeasurableSet B) :
    ∫⁻ ω, g (ν ω) * (X i ⁻¹' B).indicator (1 : Ω → ℝ≥0∞) ω ∂μ
      = ∫⁻ ω, g (ν ω) * (ν ω : Measure α) B ∂μ

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.ConditionallyIIDWith.lintegral_mul_indicator_pair
decls.doc: Two-coordinate form of the weighted block identity, at distinct indices.
decls.statement:
theorem ConditionallyIIDWith.lintegral_mul_indicator_pair
    (h : ConditionallyIIDWith μ X ν) (hX : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ) {i j : ℕ} (hij : i ≠ j)
    {g : ProbabilityMeasure α → ℝ≥0∞} (hg : Measurable g) (hB : MeasurableSet B) :
    ∫⁻ ω, g (ν ω) * (X i ⁻¹' B ∩ X j ⁻¹' B).indicator (1 : Ω → ℝ≥0∞) ω ∂μ
      = ∫⁻ ω, g (ν ω) * (ν ω : Measure α) B ^ 2 ∂μ

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.integral_toReal_eq_of_lintegral_eq
decls.doc:
Transfer of an `ℝ≥0∞` integral identity between finite integrands to the Bochner integrals of
their real parts. Private: a bookkeeping step of the moment computation.
decls.statement:
theorem integral_toReal_eq_of_lintegral_eq {F G : Ω → ℝ≥0∞}
    (hF : AEMeasurable F μ) (hG : AEMeasurable G μ)
    (hFtop : ∀ ω, F ω ≠ ∞) (hGtop : ∀ ω, G ω ≠ ∞)
    (hFG : ∫⁻ ω, F ω ∂μ = ∫⁻ ω, G ω ∂μ) :
    ∫ ω, (F ω).toReal ∂μ = ∫ ω, (G ω).toReal ∂μ

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.integrable_mul_of_nonneg_of_le_one
decls.doc:
A product of two `[0, 1]`-valued functions is integrable on a finite measure space, being
bounded by `1`. Every summand of the covariance expansion below is of this shape.
decls.statement:
theorem integrable_mul_of_nonneg_of_le_one [IsFiniteMeasure μ] {u v : Ω → ℝ}
    (hu : AEMeasurable u μ) (hv : AEMeasurable v μ)
    (hu01 : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, 0 ≤ u ω ∧ u ω ≤ 1) (hv01 : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, 0 ≤ v ω ∧ v ω ≤ 1) :
    Integrable (fun ω => u ω * v ω) μ

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.integral_sub_mul_sub
decls.doc:
**Expanding a centred product.** Whenever the four products are integrable, the integral of
`(u - q)(v - q)` splits into the four moments of the product expansion.
decls.title: Expanding a centred product
decls.statement:
theorem integral_sub_mul_sub {u v q : Ω → ℝ}
    (hi1 : Integrable (fun ω => u ω * v ω) μ) (hi2 : Integrable (fun ω => q ω * u ω) μ)
    (hi3 : Integrable (fun ω => q ω * v ω) μ) (hi4 : Integrable (fun ω => q ω ^ 2) μ) :
    ∫ ω, (u ω - q ω) * (v ω - q ω) ∂μ
      = ∫ ω, u ω * v ω ∂μ - ∫ ω, q ω * u ω ∂μ - ∫ ω, q ω * v ω ∂μ
        + ∫ ω, q ω ^ 2 ∂μ

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.integral_sq_average_sub
decls.doc:
The abstract second-moment computation behind the `L²` rate: if the centred variables
`eᵢ - q` are uncorrelated with common variance `c`, then their average over `Fin n` has mean
square `c / n`. Private: it is an algebraic repackaging with no probabilistic content of its own.
decls.statement:
theorem integral_sq_average_sub [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {e : ℕ → Ω → ℝ} {q : Ω → ℝ}
    {c : ℝ} (he : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (e i) μ) (hq : AEMeasurable q μ)
    (heb : ∀ i ω, |e i ω| ≤ 1) (hqb : ∀ ω, |q ω| ≤ 1)
    (hcov : ∀ i j, ∫ ω, (e i ω - q ω) * (e j ω - q ω) ∂μ = if i = j then c else 0)
    {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) :
    ∫ ω, ((n : ℝ)⁻¹ * (∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, e i ω) - q ω) ^ 2 ∂μ = (n : ℝ)⁻¹ * c

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.toReal_indicator_one
decls.doc: The real part of a `{0, 1}`-valued `ℝ≥0∞` indicator is the corresponding real indicator.
decls.statement:
theorem toReal_indicator_one (s : Set Ω) (ω : Ω) :
    (s.indicator (1 : Ω → ℝ≥0∞) ω).toReal = s.indicator (1 : Ω → ℝ) ω

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.indicator_one_ne_top
decls.doc: An `ℝ≥0∞` indicator of `1` is finite.
decls.statement:
theorem indicator_one_ne_top (s : Set Ω) (ω : Ω) :
    s.indicator (1 : Ω → ℝ≥0∞) ω ≠ ∞

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.ConditionallyIIDWith.integral_indicator_single
decls.doc:
**First moment.** The integral of the indicator of `{Xᵢ ∈ B}` equals the integral of the
directing measure's mass on `B`. (`μ` is an arbitrary measure here; under a probability measure
this reads as the two having the same probability.)
decls.title: First moment
decls.statement:
theorem ConditionallyIIDWith.integral_indicator_single
    (h : ConditionallyIIDWith μ X ν) (hX : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ) (hB : MeasurableSet B)
    (i : ℕ) :
    ∫ ω, (X i ⁻¹' B).indicator (1 : Ω → ℝ) ω ∂μ
      = ∫ ω, ((ν ω : Measure α) B).toReal ∂μ

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.ConditionallyIIDWith.integral_indicator_pair
decls.doc:
**Pair moment.** For distinct indices the integral of the product of the two indicators
equals the integral of the squared mass — conditional independence, read at two indices.
decls.title: Pair moment
decls.statement:
theorem ConditionallyIIDWith.integral_indicator_pair
    (h : ConditionallyIIDWith μ X ν) (hX : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ) (hB : MeasurableSet B)
    {i j : ℕ} (hij : i ≠ j) :
    ∫ ω, (X i ⁻¹' B).indicator (1 : Ω → ℝ) ω * (X j ⁻¹' B).indicator (1 : Ω → ℝ) ω ∂μ
      = ∫ ω, ((ν ω : Measure α) B).toReal ^ 2 ∂μ

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.ConditionallyIIDWith.integral_directing_mul_indicator
decls.doc:
**Cross moment.** Weighting one coordinate's indicator by the directing mass integrates to the
same squared quantity — the moment the mixture identity alone does not determine.
decls.title: Cross moment
decls.statement:
theorem ConditionallyIIDWith.integral_directing_mul_indicator
    (h : ConditionallyIIDWith μ X ν) (hX : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ) (hB : MeasurableSet B)
    (i : ℕ) :
    ∫ ω, ((ν ω : Measure α) B).toReal * (X i ⁻¹' B).indicator (1 : Ω → ℝ) ω ∂μ
      = ∫ ω, ((ν ω : Measure α) B).toReal ^ 2 ∂μ

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.ConditionallyIIDWith.integral_indicator_sub_directing_mul_indicator_sub_directing
decls.doc:
**The centred indicators are uncorrelated, with common variance `∫ q - ∫ q²`.** Writing
`q ω = ((ν ω) B).toReal` for the directing mass of `B`, the centred variables
`1_{Xᵢ ∈ B} - q` have vanishing cross moments and common second moment `∫ q - ∫ q²`.

This is the covariance hypothesis of `integral_sq_average_sub`, and it is the only place the
conditional i.i.d. structure enters beyond measurability of the directing map.
decls.title: The centred indicators are uncorrelated, with common variance `∫ q - ∫ q²`
decls.statement:
theorem ConditionallyIIDWith.integral_indicator_sub_directing_mul_indicator_sub_directing
    [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (h : ConditionallyIIDWith μ X ν) (hX : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ)
    (hB : MeasurableSet B) (i j : ℕ) :
    ∫ ω, ((X i ⁻¹' B).indicator (1 : Ω → ℝ) ω - ((ν ω : Measure α) B).toReal)
        * ((X j ⁻¹' B).indicator (1 : Ω → ℝ) ω - ((ν ω : Measure α) B).toReal) ∂μ
      = if i = j then
          (∫ ω, ((ν ω : Measure α) B).toReal ∂μ - ∫ ω, ((ν ω : Measure α) B).toReal ^ 2 ∂μ)
        else 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.ConditionallyIIDWith.integral_empiricalFrequency_sub_sq
decls.doc:
**The `L²` rate for empirical frequencies.** For a conditionally i.i.d. process with directing
measure `ν` and a measurable set `B`, the empirical frequency of `B` among the first `n`
coordinates approximates `ω ↦ (ν ω) B` with mean square error
`(∫ (ν ·) B - ∫ ((ν ·) B) ^ 2) / n`.

This is the second-moment law of large numbers for the conditional predicate, read straight off the
joint-law disintegration: the cross term `∫ (ν ·) B · 1_{Xᵢ ∈ B}` is the one moment that the
mixture identity alone does not determine.
decls.title: The `L²` rate for empirical frequencies
decls.statement:
theorem ConditionallyIIDWith.integral_empiricalFrequency_sub_sq [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    (h : ConditionallyIIDWith μ X ν) (hX : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ) (hB : MeasurableSet B)
    {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) :
    ∫ ω, ((n : ℝ)⁻¹ * (∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, (X i ⁻¹' B).indicator (1 : Ω → ℝ) ω)
          - ((ν ω : Measure α) B).toReal) ^ 2 ∂μ
      = (n : ℝ)⁻¹ * (∫ ω, ((ν ω : Measure α) B).toReal ∂μ
          - ∫ ω, ((ν ω : Measure α) B).toReal ^ 2 ∂μ)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.ConditionallyIIDWith.integral_empiricalFrequency_sub_sq_le
decls.doc:
The mean square error of `ConditionallyIIDWith.integral_empiricalFrequency_sub_sq` is at most
`1 / n`: the variance factor is a difference of moments of a `[0, 1]`-valued variable.
decls.statement:
theorem ConditionallyIIDWith.integral_empiricalFrequency_sub_sq_le [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    (h : ConditionallyIIDWith μ X ν) (hX : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ) (hB : MeasurableSet B)
    {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) :
    ∫ ω, ((n : ℝ)⁻¹ * (∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, (X i ⁻¹' B).indicator (1 : Ω → ℝ) ω)
          - ((ν ω : Measure α) B).toReal) ^ 2 ∂μ ≤ (n : ℝ)⁻¹

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.ConditionallyIIDWith.tendsto_integral_empiricalFrequency_sub_sq
decls.doc:
**Fixed-set empirical frequencies converge in mean square.** For a conditionally i.i.d. process,
the empirical frequency of a fixed measurable set `B` along the first `n` coordinates converges in
`L²` to the directing measure's evaluation `(ν ·) B`.

Indexed at `n + 1` so that no caller carries an `n ≠ 0` side condition.
decls.title: Fixed-set empirical frequencies converge in mean square
decls.statement:
theorem ConditionallyIIDWith.tendsto_integral_empiricalFrequency_sub_sq [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    (h : ConditionallyIIDWith μ X ν) (hX : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ) (hB : MeasurableSet B) :
    Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => ∫ ω, (((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)⁻¹ *
          (∑ i ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), (X i ⁻¹' B).indicator (1 : Ω → ℝ) ω)
        - ((ν ω : Measure α) B).toReal) ^ 2 ∂μ) atTop (nhds 0)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.abs_average_indicator_le_one
decls.doc:
**An average of indicators lies in `[0, 1]`.** Stated with the absolute value because that is
the form the `L²` estimates below consume.
decls.title: An average of indicators lies in `[0, 1]`
decls.statement:
theorem abs_average_indicator_le_one (A : ℕ → Set Ω) (n : ℕ) (ω : Ω) :
    |(n : ℝ)⁻¹ * ∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, (A i).indicator (1 : Ω → ℝ) ω| ≤ 1

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.integrable_sub_sq_of_abs_le_one
decls.doc:
**A squared difference of bounded functions is integrable**, being bounded by `4` on a finite
measure space.
decls.title: A squared difference of bounded functions is integrable
decls.statement:
theorem integrable_sub_sq_of_abs_le_one [IsFiniteMeasure μ] {u v : Ω → ℝ}
    (hu : AEMeasurable u μ) (hv : AEMeasurable v μ)
    (hu1 : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, |u ω| ≤ 1) (hv1 : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, |v ω| ≤ 1) :
    Integrable (fun ω => (u ω - v ω) ^ 2) μ

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.integral_sub_sq_le_two_mul_add_two_mul_of_integral_sub_sq_le_of_integral_sub_sq_le
decls.doc:
**An `L²` triangle bound.** If `q` and `q'` are within `c₁` and `c₂` of a common `Y` in mean
square, then they are within `2c₁ + 2c₂` of each other. The three squared differences are assumed
integrable; `hd` is not implied by `hi1` and `hi2`, which constrain only the squares `(Y - q)²` and
`(Y - q')²` and so do not make `q - q'` measurable.
decls.title: An `L²` triangle bound
decls.statement:
theorem integral_sub_sq_le_two_mul_add_two_mul_of_integral_sub_sq_le_of_integral_sub_sq_le
    {q q' Y : Ω → ℝ}
    (hd : Integrable (fun ω => (q ω - q' ω) ^ 2) μ)
    (hi1 : Integrable (fun ω => (Y ω - q ω) ^ 2) μ)
    (hi2 : Integrable (fun ω => (Y ω - q' ω) ^ 2) μ)
    {c₁ c₂ : ℝ} (h1 : ∫ ω, (Y ω - q ω) ^ 2 ∂μ ≤ c₁) (h2 : ∫ ω, (Y ω - q' ω) ^ 2 ∂μ ≤ c₂) :
    ∫ ω, (q ω - q' ω) ^ 2 ∂μ ≤ 2 * c₁ + 2 * c₂

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.integrable_toReal_directing_sub_sq
decls.doc:
**The squared difference of two directing masses is integrable.** Each evaluation
`ω ↦ ((ρ ω) B).toReal` is measurable and takes values in `[0, 1]`, so the square of the difference
is bounded, hence integrable on a finite measure space.
decls.title: The squared difference of two directing masses is integrable
decls.statement:
theorem integrable_toReal_directing_sub_sq [IsFiniteMeasure μ]
    {ρ ρ' : Ω → ProbabilityMeasure α} (hρ : Measurable ρ) (hρ' : Measurable ρ')
    (hB : MeasurableSet B) :
    Integrable (fun ω =>
      (((ρ ω : Measure α) B).toReal - ((ρ' ω : Measure α) B).toReal) ^ 2) μ

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.ConditionallyIIDWith.integral_directing_sub_sq_le_four_div
decls.doc:
**The `L²` rate between two directing measures.** Two directing measures of the same process
are within `4 / n` of each other in mean square, for every `n ≥ 1`, on each fixed measurable set.
This is the scaffolding for `ae_measure_apply_eq`, which is its `n → ∞` limit. It stays private:
that theorem has the same hypotheses and makes the integrand a.e. zero, so once it is available
this bound is a trivial consequence and carries no independent content.
decls.title: The `L²` rate between two directing measures
decls.statement:
theorem ConditionallyIIDWith.integral_directing_sub_sq_le_four_div
    [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    (hX : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ) (h : ConditionallyIIDWith μ X ν)
    (h' : ConditionallyIIDWith μ X ν') (hB : MeasurableSet B) {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) :
    ∫ ω, (((ν ω : Measure α) B).toReal - ((ν' ω : Measure α) B).toReal) ^ 2 ∂μ ≤ 4 / n

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.ConditionallyIIDWith.ae_measure_apply_eq
decls.doc:
Two directing measures of the same process assign the same mass to each fixed measurable set,
almost everywhere.

Both are approximated in `L²` by the *same* empirical frequencies, at a rate that does not depend
on the witness, so the triangle inequality forces their difference to vanish in `L²`.
decls.statement:
theorem ConditionallyIIDWith.ae_measure_apply_eq [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    (hX : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ) (h : ConditionallyIIDWith μ X ν)
    (h' : ConditionallyIIDWith μ X ν') (hB : MeasurableSet B) :
    (fun ω => (ν ω : Measure α) B) =ᵐ[μ] fun ω => (ν' ω : Measure α) B

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.ae_eq_of_forall_apply_ae_eq
decls.doc:
Almost sure equality of two random probability measures follows from a.e. equality of their
masses on each fixed measurable set, when the σ-algebra is countably generated. Private: the final
promotion step, phrased for the two witnesses at hand.

The countable-set-algebra argument is adapted from `TauCeti.MeasureTheory.Measure.FiniteMeasure`,
where the same `generateSetAlgebra (countableGeneratingSet α)` idiom pins a finite measure down from
its values on a countable set algebra (there, to prove that singletons are measurable).
decls.statement:
theorem ae_eq_of_forall_apply_ae_eq [CountablyGenerated α]
    (h : ∀ s : Set α, MeasurableSet s →
      (fun ω => (ν ω : Measure α) s) =ᵐ[μ] fun ω => (ν' ω : Measure α) s) :
    ν =ᵐ[μ] ν'

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.conditionallyIID_ae_unique
decls.doc:
**The directing measure is almost surely unique.** Two witnesses of `ConditionallyIIDWith` for
the same process agree almost everywhere.

This is the uniqueness statement that belongs to the *conditional* predicate. Its mixture analogue
is false at the level of witnesses: for a nondegenerate mixing law an independent copy of a
directing measure is another mixing representative, and only the mixing law `μ.map ν` is determined
(`mixedIID_mixingLaw_unique`).

`TauCetiRoadmap/Exchangeability/README.md` (Layer 6) states this with `[StandardBorelSpace α]`,
which supplies `[MeasurableSpace.CountablyGenerated α]` through
`countablyGenerated_of_standardBorel`; the extra `[Nonempty α]` is not needed, since no measure on
`α` is constructed here.
decls.title: The directing measure is almost surely unique
decls.statement:
theorem conditionallyIID_ae_unique [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] [CountablyGenerated α]
    (hX : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ) (h : ConditionallyIIDWith μ X ν)
    (h' : ConditionallyIIDWith μ X ν') : ν =ᵐ[μ] ν'

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.Contractable.map
decls.doc:
A contractable process has the same finite-dimensional block law as the corresponding
prefix law along any strictly increasing finite index map.
decls.statement:
theorem Contractable.map {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α} (h : Contractable μ X)
    {m : ℕ} {k : Fin m → ℕ} (hk : StrictMono k) :
    blockLaw μ X k = prefixLaw μ X m

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.Contractable.map_single
decls.doc: The one-coordinate specialization of contractability.
decls.statement:
theorem Contractable.map_single {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α} (h : Contractable μ X)
    (k : Fin 1 → ℕ) :
    blockLaw μ X k = prefixLaw μ X 1

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.Contractable.map_pair
decls.doc: The two-coordinate specialization of contractability.
decls.statement:
theorem Contractable.map_pair {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α} (h : Contractable μ X)
    {i j : ℕ} (hij : i < j) :
    blockLaw μ X ![i, j] = prefixLaw μ X 2

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.Contractable.identDistrib_block
decls.doc:
**Finite blocks of a contractable process are identically distributed.** For a contractable
process `X`, any two strictly increasing finite coordinate selections have the same joint law.
decls.title: Finite blocks of a contractable process are identically distributed
decls.statement:
theorem Contractable.identDistrib_block {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α}
    (hX : Contractable μ X) {m : ℕ} {k l : Fin m → ℕ} (hk : StrictMono k) (hl : StrictMono l)
    (hk_meas : ∀ r, AEMeasurable (X (k r)) μ)
    (hl_meas : ∀ r, AEMeasurable (X (l r)) μ) :
    IdentDistrib (fun ω r => X (k r) ω) (fun ω r => X (l r) ω) μ μ

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.Contractable.identDistrib_coord
decls.doc:
**Coordinates of a contractable process are identically distributed.** For a contractable
process `X`, any two a.e. measurable coordinates `X i` and `X j` have the same law.
decls.title: Coordinates of a contractable process are identically distributed
decls.statement:
theorem Contractable.identDistrib_coord {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α} (hX : Contractable μ X)
    {i j : ℕ} (hi_meas : AEMeasurable (X i) μ) (hj_meas : AEMeasurable (X j) μ) :
    IdentDistrib (X i) (X j) μ μ

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.Contractable.identDistrib_pair
decls.doc:
**Increasing pairs of a contractable process are identically distributed.** For a
contractable process `X`, if the four selected coordinates are a.e. measurable and `i < j`,
`k < l`, then `(X i, X j)` has the same joint law as `(X k, X l)`.
decls.title: Increasing pairs of a contractable process are identically distributed
decls.statement:
theorem Contractable.identDistrib_pair {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α} (hX : Contractable μ X)
    {i j k l : ℕ} (hi_meas : AEMeasurable (X i) μ) (hj_meas : AEMeasurable (X j) μ)
    (hk_meas : AEMeasurable (X k) μ) (hl_meas : AEMeasurable (X l) μ)
    (hij : i < j) (hkl : k < l) :
    IdentDistrib (fun ω => (X i ω, X j ω)) (fun ω => (X k ω, X l ω)) μ μ

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.Contractable.comp
decls.doc: Contractability is preserved by passing to a strictly increasing subsequence.
decls.statement:
theorem Contractable.comp {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α} (h : Contractable μ X)
    {φ : ℕ → ℕ} (hφ : StrictMono φ) :
    Contractable μ (fun n ω => X (φ n) ω)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.Exchangeable.blockLaw_eq_prefixLaw_of_injective
decls.doc:
**An exchangeable sequence has the prefix law along any injective finite selection:**
`blockLaw μ X k = prefixLaw μ X n` for injective `k : Fin n → ℕ`.
decls.title: An exchangeable sequence has the prefix law along any injective finite selection
decls.statement:
theorem Exchangeable.blockLaw_eq_prefixLaw_of_injective {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α}
    (hX : Exchangeable μ X) (hX_meas : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ)
    {n : ℕ} (k : Fin n → ℕ) (hk : Function.Injective k) :
    blockLaw μ X k = prefixLaw μ X n

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.contractable_of_exchangeable
decls.doc:
**Every exchangeable sequence with a.e. measurable coordinates is contractable**: along any
strictly increasing finite selection `k`, `blockLaw μ X k = prefixLaw μ X m`. One direction of the
de Finetti–Ryll-Nardzewski equivalence.
decls.title: Every exchangeable sequence with a.e. measurable coordinates is contractable
decls.statement:
theorem contractable_of_exchangeable {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α}
    (hX : Exchangeable μ X) (hX_meas : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ) : Contractable μ X

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.Exchangeable.contractable
decls.doc:
Every exchangeable sequence with a.e. measurable coordinates is contractable (dot-notation
form of `contractable_of_exchangeable`).
decls.statement:
theorem Exchangeable.contractable {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α}
    (hX : Exchangeable μ X) (hX_meas : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ) : Contractable μ X

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.Contractable.measurePreserving_reindex
decls.doc:
**A contractable process's path law is invariant under strictly monotone time-reindexing:** for
`StrictMono φ`, the reindexing `x ↦ x ∘ φ` preserves `pathLaw μ X`.
decls.title: A contractable process's path law is invariant under strictly monotone time-reindexing
decls.statement:
theorem Contractable.measurePreserving_reindex {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α} [IsFiniteMeasure μ]
    (hX : Contractable μ X) (hX_meas : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ) {φ : ℕ → ℕ} (hφ : StrictMono φ) :
    MeasurePreserving (fun x : ℕ → α => fun k => x (φ k)) (pathLaw μ X) (pathLaw μ X)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.contractable_iff_forall_map_reindex_pathLaw
decls.doc:
Contractability is equivalent to invariance of the path law under every strictly increasing
time-reindexing `ℕ → ℕ`. This is the path-law form of spreadability/contractability.
decls.statement:
theorem contractable_iff_forall_map_reindex_pathLaw {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α}
    [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (hX_meas : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ) :
    Contractable μ X ↔
      ∀ φ : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono φ →
        (pathLaw μ X).map (fun x : ℕ → α => fun k => x (φ k)) = pathLaw μ X

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.contractable_iff_forall_measurePreserving_reindex
decls.doc:
Contractability is equivalent to preservation of the path law by every strictly increasing
time-reindexing `ℕ → ℕ`.
decls.statement:
theorem contractable_iff_forall_measurePreserving_reindex {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α}
    [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (hX_meas : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ) :
    Contractable μ X ↔
      ∀ φ : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono φ →
        MeasurePreserving (fun x : ℕ → α => fun k => x (φ k)) (pathLaw μ X) (pathLaw μ X)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.Contractable.measurePreserving_shift
decls.doc: **A contractable process has a shift-invariant path law:** `shift` preserves `pathLaw μ X`.
decls.title: A contractable process has a shift-invariant path law
decls.statement:
theorem Contractable.measurePreserving_shift {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α} [IsFiniteMeasure μ]
    (hX : Contractable μ X) (hX_meas : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ) :
    MeasurePreserving (shift α) (pathLaw μ X) (pathLaw μ X)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.Contractable.pairLaw_eq
decls.doc:
**Pair-law equality from contractability.** For a contractable process, a strictly increasing
tail selection `g`, and two head indices `j, k` below the tail start `g 0`, the joint law of the
head coordinate `X j` with the tail `(X (g 0), X (g 1), …)` equals the joint law of `X k` with
the **same** tail:
```
μ.map (fun ω => (X j ω, fun n => X (g n) ω)) = μ.map (fun ω => (X k ω, fun n => X (g n) ω)).
```
decls.title: Pair-law equality from contractability
decls.statement:
theorem Contractable.pairLaw_eq {μ : Measure Ω} [IsFiniteMeasure μ] {X : ℕ → Ω → α}
    (hX : Contractable μ X) (hX_ae : ∀ n, AEMeasurable (X n) μ) {g : ℕ → ℕ} (hg : StrictMono g)
    {j k : ℕ} (hj : j < g 0) (hk : k < g 0) :
    μ.map (fun ω => (X j ω, fun n => X (g n) ω))
      = μ.map (fun ω => (X k ω, fun n => X (g n) ω))

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.blockCylinder
decls.doc: The block cylinder event on the selected coordinates: `{ω | ∀ i, X (k i) ω ∈ C i}`.
decls.statement: def blockCylinder (X : ℕ → Ω → α) {m : ℕ} (k : Fin m → ℕ) (C : Fin m → Set α) : Set Ω

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.mem_blockCylinder
decls.doc:
Membership in the block cylinder: `ω` lies in `blockCylinder X k C` iff every selected
coordinate `X (k i) ω` lies in its set `C i`.
decls.statement:
theorem mem_blockCylinder {X : ℕ → Ω → α} {m : ℕ} {k : Fin m → ℕ} {C : Fin m → Set α} {ω : Ω} :
    ω ∈ blockCylinder X k C ↔ ∀ i, X (k i) ω ∈ C i

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.blockCylinder_eq_preimage_univ_pi
decls.doc:
The block cylinder is the preimage of the rectangle `Set.univ.pi C` under the
selected-coordinate map `ω ↦ (X (k ·) ω)`.
decls.statement:
theorem blockCylinder_eq_preimage_univ_pi (X : ℕ → Ω → α) {m : ℕ} (k : Fin m → ℕ)
    (C : Fin m → Set α) :
    blockCylinder X k C = (fun ω i => X (k i) ω) ⁻¹' Set.univ.pi C

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.measurableSet_blockCylinder
decls.doc:
The block cylinder of a process with measurable selected coordinates on measurable sets is
measurable.

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.blockLaw_blockCylinder
decls.doc:
The block law evaluated on a measurable rectangle is the measure of the block cylinder:
`blockLaw μ X k (Set.univ.pi C) = μ (blockCylinder X k C)`. A `blockCylinder`-named restatement of
the merged `blockLaw_apply_rectangle`.

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.blockIndicatorProd
decls.doc: The product of the selected coordinate indicators, `∏ i, 𝟙_{C i}(X (k i) ω)`.
decls.statement: def blockIndicatorProd (X : ℕ → Ω → α) {m : ℕ} (k : Fin m → ℕ) (C : Fin m → Set α) : Ω → ℝ

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.blockIndicatorProd_apply
decls.doc: Pointwise value of the indicator product: the product of the selected coordinate indicators.
decls.statement:
theorem blockIndicatorProd_apply (X : ℕ → Ω → α) {m : ℕ} (k : Fin m → ℕ) (C : Fin m → Set α)
    (ω : Ω) :
    blockIndicatorProd X k C ω = ∏ i, (C i).indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) (X (k i) ω)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.blockIndicatorProd_eq_indicator
decls.doc: The indicator product is the indicator of the block cylinder.
decls.statement:
theorem blockIndicatorProd_eq_indicator (X : ℕ → Ω → α) {m : ℕ} (k : Fin m → ℕ)
    (C : Fin m → Set α) :
    blockIndicatorProd X k C = (blockCylinder X k C).indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ))

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.blockIndicatorProd_empty
decls.doc: The empty (zero-coordinate) indicator product is the constant-one function.
decls.statement:
theorem blockIndicatorProd_empty (X : ℕ → Ω → α) (k : Fin 0 → ℕ) (C : Fin 0 → Set α) :
    blockIndicatorProd X k C = fun _ => 1

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.blockIndicatorProd_succ_eq_indicator_inter
decls.doc:
**Successor split of the indicator product.** Splitting off the last selected coordinate, the
length-`r+1` indicator product equals the indicator of the length-`r` prefix cylinder intersected
with the last coordinate's preimage. The `Fin 0` companion is `blockIndicatorProd_empty`.
decls.title: Successor split of the indicator product
decls.statement:
theorem blockIndicatorProd_succ_eq_indicator_inter (X : ℕ → Ω → α) {r : ℕ} (k : Fin (r + 1) → ℕ)
    (C : Fin (r + 1) → Set α) :
    blockIndicatorProd X k C
      = (blockCylinder X (fun i : Fin r => k i.castSucc) (fun j => C j.castSucc)
          ∩ X (k (Fin.last r)) ⁻¹' C (Fin.last r)).indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ))

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.nullMeasurableSet_blockCylinder
decls.doc: The block cylinder is null-measurable when the selected coordinates are a.e. measurable.

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.integrable_blockIndicatorProd
decls.doc: The indicator product is integrable under a finite measure (a.e.-measurable coordinates).

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.lintegral_blockCylinder_indicator
decls.doc:
**The block law of a rectangle is the lintegral of the block-cylinder indicator.** For
a.e.-measurable selected coordinates,
`∫⁻ ω, 𝟙_{blockCylinder X k C}(ω) ∂μ = blockLaw μ X k (∏ᵢ C i)`. Being an `ℝ≥0∞` lintegral, this is
the honest identity for an **arbitrary** measure (no finiteness needed).
decls.title: The block law of a rectangle is the lintegral of the block-cylinder indicator
decls.statement:
theorem lintegral_blockCylinder_indicator {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α} {m : ℕ}
    {k : Fin m → ℕ} {C : Fin m → Set α} (hX : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X (k i)) μ)
    (hC : ∀ i, MeasurableSet (C i)) :
    ∫⁻ ω, (blockCylinder X k C).indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ≥0∞)) ω ∂μ
      = blockLaw μ X k (Set.univ.pi C)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.integral_blockIndicatorProd
decls.doc:
The real (Bochner) integral of the indicator product is the block law of the rectangle:
`∫ ω, ∏ i, 𝟙_{C i}(X (k i) ω) ∂μ = (blockLaw μ X k (∏ᵢ C i)).toReal` — the real (`toReal`) form of
the `ℝ≥0∞` identity `lintegral_blockCylinder_indicator` (integrability under a finite measure is
`integrable_blockIndicatorProd`).
decls.statement:
theorem integral_blockIndicatorProd {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α} {m : ℕ}
    {k : Fin m → ℕ} {C : Fin m → Set α} (hX : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X (k i)) μ)
    (hC : ∀ i, MeasurableSet (C i)) :
    ∫ ω, blockIndicatorProd X k C ω ∂μ = (blockLaw μ X k (Set.univ.pi C)).toReal

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.ExchangeableAt.blockLaw_eq_prefixLaw_of_injective
decls.doc:
An exchangeable `n`-prefix has the prefix law on every injective `m`-subselection inside
that prefix.
decls.statement:
theorem blockLaw_eq_prefixLaw_of_injective {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α} {m n : ℕ}
    (h : ExchangeableAt μ X n) (k : Fin m → Fin n) (hk : Function.Injective k)
    (hX : ∀ i : Fin n, AEMeasurable (X i.val) μ) :
    blockLaw μ X (fun i : Fin m => (k i).val) = prefixLaw μ X m

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.ExchangeableAt.of_le
decls.doc: Finite exchangeability at length `n` descends to every shorter prefix length `m ≤ n`.
decls.statement:
theorem of_le {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α} {m n : ℕ}
    (h : ExchangeableAt μ X n) (hmn : m ≤ n)
    (hX : ∀ i : Fin n, AEMeasurable (X i.val) μ) :
    ExchangeableAt μ X m

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.ExchangeableAt.of_lt
decls.doc: Finite exchangeability at length `n` descends to any strictly shorter prefix length.
decls.statement:
theorem of_lt {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α} {m n : ℕ}
    (h : ExchangeableAt μ X n) (hmn : m < n)
    (hX : ∀ i : Fin n, AEMeasurable (X i.val) μ) :
    ExchangeableAt μ X m

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.ExchangeableAt.pred
decls.doc: Exchangeability at `n + 1` descends to exchangeability at `n`.
decls.statement:
theorem pred {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α} {n : ℕ}
    (h : ExchangeableAt μ X (n + 1))
    (hX : ∀ i : Fin (n + 1), AEMeasurable (X i.val) μ) :
    ExchangeableAt μ X n

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.ExchangeableFamily
decls.doc:
A family is exchangeable when its law is unchanged after replacing any finite injective
selection of indices by another of the same size.
decls.statement: def ExchangeableFamily (μ : Measure Ω) (X : ι → Ω → α) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.ExchangeableFamily.intro
decls.doc: Constructor for exchangeability of an arbitrary family.
decls.statement:
theorem ExchangeableFamily.intro {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ι → Ω → α}
    (h : ∀ (m : ℕ) (k l : Fin m → ι), Function.Injective k → Function.Injective l →
      blockLaw μ X k = blockLaw μ X l) :
    ExchangeableFamily μ X

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.exchangeableFamily_iff
decls.doc: Simp normal form for exchangeability of an arbitrary family.
decls.statement:
theorem exchangeableFamily_iff {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ι → Ω → α} :
    ExchangeableFamily μ X ↔
      ∀ (m : ℕ) (k l : Fin m → ι), Function.Injective k → Function.Injective l →
        blockLaw μ X k = blockLaw μ X l

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.ExchangeableFamily.blockLaw_eq
decls.doc: The finite-block law equality defining an exchangeable family.
decls.statement:
theorem ExchangeableFamily.blockLaw_eq {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ι → Ω → α}
    (h : ExchangeableFamily μ X) {m : ℕ} (k l : Fin m → ι)
    (hk : Function.Injective k) (hl : Function.Injective l) :
    blockLaw μ X k = blockLaw μ X l

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.ConditionallyIIDWith.exchangeableFamily
decls.doc: A conditionally i.i.d. family with a named directing measure is exchangeable.

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.ConditionallyIID.exchangeableFamily
decls.doc: A conditionally i.i.d. family is exchangeable.
decls.statement:
theorem ConditionallyIID.exchangeableFamily
    {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ι → Ω → α} (h : ConditionallyIID μ X) :
    ExchangeableFamily μ X

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.ExchangeableFamily.comp_injective
decls.doc: Exchangeability is preserved by reindexing a family along an injection.

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.ExchangeableFamily.exchangeable
decls.doc: An exchangeable family indexed by `ℕ` is an exchangeable sequence.
decls.statement:
theorem ExchangeableFamily.exchangeable {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α}
    (h : ExchangeableFamily μ X) : Exchangeable μ X

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.Exchangeable.exchangeableFamily
decls.doc:
An exchangeable sequence with a.e. measurable coordinates is exchangeable as an
`ℕ`-indexed family.
decls.statement:
theorem Exchangeable.exchangeableFamily {μ : Measure Ω} [IsFiniteMeasure μ]
    {X : ℕ → Ω → α} (h : Exchangeable μ X) (hX : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ) :
    ExchangeableFamily μ X

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.exchangeableFamily_iff_exchangeable
decls.doc:
For a finite measure and a.e. measurable coordinates, exchangeability as an `ℕ`-indexed family
is equivalent to the existing sequence predicate.
decls.statement:
theorem exchangeableFamily_iff_exchangeable {μ : Measure Ω} [IsFiniteMeasure μ]
    {X : ℕ → Ω → α} (hX : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ) :
    ExchangeableFamily μ X ↔ Exchangeable μ X

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.finsetRestrict_eq_comp_prefixProj
decls.doc:
The restriction to a finite index set `I ⊆ {0, …, n-1}` factors through the prefix projection
to the first `n` coordinates.
decls.statement:
theorem finsetRestrict_eq_comp_prefixProj (I : Finset ℕ) {n : ℕ}
    (hn : ∀ i ∈ I, i < n) :
    (Finset.restrict I : (ℕ → α) → ((i : I) → α)) =
      (fun y : Fin n → α => fun i : I => y ⟨i.1, hn i.1 i.2⟩) ∘ prefixProj α n

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.measure_eq_of_prefixProj_map_eq
decls.doc:
**Finite-marginal uniqueness.** Two measures on `ℕ → α`, with `μ` finite, that have the same
law under every finite prefix projection `prefixProj α n` are equal. (Finiteness of `ν` is not
needed: projective-limit uniqueness only requires the prefix-marginal family, supplied by `μ`, to
be finite.)
decls.title: Finite-marginal uniqueness
decls.statement:
theorem measure_eq_of_prefixProj_map_eq {μ ν : Measure (ℕ → α)} [IsFiniteMeasure μ]
    (h : ∀ n, μ.map (prefixProj α n) = ν.map (prefixProj α n)) : μ = ν

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.measure_eq_of_fin_marginals_eq
decls.doc:
**Finite-marginal uniqueness, setwise form** (the roadmap-named milestone): two measures on
`ℕ → α`, with `μ` finite, agreeing on every measurable prefix-cylinder are equal. It assumes only
`μ` is finite; `ν`'s finiteness is forced by the conclusion.
decls.title: Finite-marginal uniqueness, setwise form
decls.statement:
theorem measure_eq_of_fin_marginals_eq {μ ν : Measure (ℕ → α)} [IsFiniteMeasure μ]
    (h : ∀ (n : ℕ) (S : Set (Fin n → α)), MeasurableSet S →
      μ.map (prefixProj α n) S = ν.map (prefixProj α n) S) : μ = ν

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.map_reindex_prefixProj
decls.doc:
The first-`n` prefix marginal of the `π`-reindexed path law is the block law along the
selection `j ↦ π j`.
decls.statement:
theorem map_reindex_prefixProj {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α}
    (hX_meas : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ) (π : Equiv.Perm ℕ) (n : ℕ) :
    (μ.map fun ω i => X (π i) ω).map (prefixProj α n)
      = blockLaw μ X (fun j : Fin n => π j.val)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.FullyExchangeable.exchangeableAt
decls.doc: **Full exchangeability implies finite exchangeability at each dimension `n`.**
decls.title: Full exchangeability implies finite exchangeability at each dimension `n`

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.FullyExchangeable.exchangeable
decls.doc: **Full exchangeability implies finite exchangeability.**
decls.title: Full exchangeability implies finite exchangeability
decls.statement:
theorem FullyExchangeable.exchangeable {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α}
    (hX : FullyExchangeable μ X) (hX_meas : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ) : Exchangeable μ X

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.Exchangeable.fullyExchangeable
decls.doc:
**Finite exchangeability implies full exchangeability** for a finite law with a.e. measurable
coordinates: the path law is invariant under every permutation of `ℕ`.
decls.title: Finite exchangeability implies full exchangeability
decls.statement:
theorem Exchangeable.fullyExchangeable {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α} [IsFiniteMeasure μ]
    (hX : Exchangeable μ X) (hX_meas : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ) : FullyExchangeable μ X

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.exchangeable_iff_fullyExchangeable
decls.doc:
**Finite exchangeability ↔ full exchangeability** for a process with a.e. measurable
coordinates under a finite measure.
decls.title: Finite exchangeability ↔ full exchangeability
decls.statement:
theorem exchangeable_iff_fullyExchangeable {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α} [IsFiniteMeasure μ]
    (hX_meas : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ) : Exchangeable μ X ↔ FullyExchangeable μ X

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.FullyExchangeable.measurePreserving_shift
decls.doc:
**A fully exchangeable process has a shift-invariant path law** — the Layer 0 shift-preservation
bridge.
decls.title: A fully exchangeable process has a shift-invariant path law

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.map_permReindex_pathLaw
decls.doc: Reindexing a path law by a time permutation gives the path law of the permuted process.
decls.statement:
theorem map_permReindex_pathLaw (μ : Measure Ω) {X : ℕ → Ω → α}
    (hX : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ) (π : Equiv.Perm ℕ) :
    (pathLaw μ X).map (permReindex (α := α) π) =
      pathLaw μ (fun k ω => X (π k) ω)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.fullyExchangeable_iff_forall_map_permReindex_pathLaw
decls.doc: Full exchangeability is exactly invariance of the path law under every time permutation.
decls.statement:
theorem fullyExchangeable_iff_forall_map_permReindex_pathLaw
    (μ : Measure Ω) {X : ℕ → Ω → α} (hX : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ) :
    FullyExchangeable μ X ↔
      ∀ π : Equiv.Perm ℕ,
        (pathLaw μ X).map (permReindex (α := α) π) = pathLaw μ X

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.FullyExchangeable.map_permReindex_pathLaw
decls.doc: A fully exchangeable process has path law invariant under any time permutation.
decls.statement:
theorem FullyExchangeable.map_permReindex_pathLaw {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α}
    (h : FullyExchangeable μ X) (hX : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ)
    (π : Equiv.Perm ℕ) :
    (pathLaw μ X).map (permReindex (α := α) π) = pathLaw μ X

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.FullyExchangeable.measurePreserving_permReindex
decls.doc:
Reindexing path space by any time permutation preserves the path law of a fully
exchangeable process.

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.fullyExchangeable_iff_forall_measurePreserving_permReindex
decls.doc:
Full exchangeability is exactly preservation of the path law by every time-permutation
reindexing map.
decls.statement:
theorem fullyExchangeable_iff_forall_measurePreserving_permReindex
    (μ : Measure Ω) {X : ℕ → Ω → α} (hX : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ) :
    FullyExchangeable μ X ↔
      ∀ π : Equiv.Perm ℕ,
        MeasurePreserving (permReindex (α := α) π) (pathLaw μ X) (pathLaw μ X)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.fullyExchangeable_of_forall_map_permReindex_pathLaw
decls.doc: If every time permutation preserves the path law, then the process is fully exchangeable.
decls.statement:
theorem fullyExchangeable_of_forall_map_permReindex_pathLaw
    {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α} (hX : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ)
    (h : ∀ π : Equiv.Perm ℕ,
      (pathLaw μ X).map (permReindex (α := α) π) = pathLaw μ X) :
    FullyExchangeable μ X

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.fullyExchangeable_of_forall_measurePreserving_permReindex
decls.doc:
A measure-preserving form of the path-law bridge: if every time permutation preserves the
path law, then the process is fully exchangeable.
decls.statement:
theorem fullyExchangeable_of_forall_measurePreserving_permReindex
    {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α} (hX : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ)
    (h : ∀ π : Equiv.Perm ℕ,
      MeasurePreserving (permReindex (α := α) π) (pathLaw μ X) (pathLaw μ X)) :
    FullyExchangeable μ X

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.MixedIIDWith.of_iIndepFun_identDistrib
decls.doc:
**An i.i.d. sequence is mixed i.i.d.**, with the constant mixing representative
`ω ↦ μ.map (X 0)` (the common law of the coordinates). For independent, identically
distributed coordinates, the law of an injective finite block is the product of
that common law, which is precisely the mixture against the constant mixing representative.
decls.title: An i.i.d. sequence is mixed i.i.d
decls.statement:
theorem MixedIIDWith.of_iIndepFun_identDistrib {μ : Measure Ω}
    {X : ℕ → Ω → α} (hindep : iIndepFun X μ)
    (hident : ∀ i, IdentDistrib (X i) (X 0) μ μ) :
    haveI

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.MixedIID.of_iIndepFun_identDistrib
decls.doc: **An i.i.d. sequence is mixed i.i.d.** (existential mixing-representative form).
decls.title: An i.i.d. sequence is mixed i.i.d
decls.statement:
theorem MixedIID.of_iIndepFun_identDistrib {μ : Measure Ω}
    {X : ℕ → Ω → α} (hindep : iIndepFun X μ)
    (hident : ∀ i, IdentDistrib (X i) (X 0) μ μ) :
    MixedIID μ X

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.Exchangeable.of_iIndepFun_identDistrib
decls.doc: **An i.i.d. sequence is exchangeable.**
decls.title: An i.i.d. sequence is exchangeable
decls.statement:
theorem Exchangeable.of_iIndepFun_identDistrib {μ : Measure Ω}
    {X : ℕ → Ω → α} (hindep : iIndepFun X μ)
    (hident : ∀ i, IdentDistrib (X i) (X 0) μ μ) :
    Exchangeable μ X

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.Contractable.of_iIndepFun_identDistrib
decls.doc: **An i.i.d. sequence is contractable.**
decls.title: An i.i.d. sequence is contractable
decls.statement:
theorem Contractable.of_iIndepFun_identDistrib {μ : Measure Ω}
    {X : ℕ → Ω → α} (hindep : iIndepFun X μ)
    (hident : ∀ i, IdentDistrib (X i) (X 0) μ μ) :
    Contractable μ X

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.blockAverage
decls.doc:
The **block average** of a real-valued process `X` over a finite selection `k : Fin n → ℕ`:
the empirical mean `n⁻¹ • ∑ i, X (k i)` of the block `(X (k i))ᵢ`.
decls.statement: def blockAverage (X : ℕ → Ω → ℝ) {n : ℕ} (k : Fin n → ℕ) : Ω → ℝ

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.blockAverage_apply
decls.statement:
theorem blockAverage_apply {n : ℕ} (k : Fin n → ℕ) (ω : Ω) :
    blockAverage X k ω = (n : ℝ)⁻¹ * ∑ i, X (k i) ω

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.blockAverage_eq_sum
decls.doc: A block average as a real-scaled finite sum.
decls.statement:
theorem blockAverage_eq_sum {n : ℕ} (k : Fin n → ℕ) :
    blockAverage X k = (n : ℝ)⁻¹ • ∑ i, X (k i)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.memLp_blockAverage
decls.doc: A block average of `L²` coordinates is itself `L²`.
decls.statement:
theorem memLp_blockAverage {n : ℕ} (k : Fin n → ℕ) (hX_L2 : ∀ i, MemLp (X (k i)) 2 μ) :
    MemLp (blockAverage X k) 2 μ

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.sum_sum_cov_eq
decls.doc:
The double sum of block covariances splits along the diagonal into the common variance and
the common off-diagonal covariance of a contractable `L²` sequence.
decls.statement:
theorem sum_sum_cov_eq (hX : Contractable μ X)
    (hmeas : ∀ m, AEMeasurable (X m) μ) {n : ℕ} {k : Fin n → ℕ} (hk : Function.Injective k) :
    ∑ i, ∑ j, cov[X (k i), X (k j); μ]
      = (n : ℝ) ^ 2 * cov[X 0, X 1; μ] + n * (Var[X 0; μ] - cov[X 0, X 1; μ])

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.Contractable.variance_blockAverage
decls.doc:
**The variance of a block average of a contractable L² sequence.** For a contractable
real-valued process with `L²` coordinates and an injective selection `k : Fin n → ℕ` (`0 < n`),
the block average has the closed-form variance `(v - c) / n + c`, where `v = Var[X 0]` is the
common coordinate variance and `c = cov[X 0, X 1]` is the common off-diagonal covariance.
decls.title: The variance of a block average of a contractable L² sequence
decls.statement:
theorem Contractable.variance_blockAverage [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (hX : Contractable μ X)
    (hX_L2 : ∀ n, MemLp (X n) 2 μ) {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) {k : Fin n → ℕ}
    (hk : Function.Injective k) :
    Var[blockAverage X k; μ] = (Var[X 0; μ] - cov[X 0, X 1; μ]) / n + cov[X 0, X 1; μ]

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.Contractable.integral_blockAverage
decls.doc:
**The mean of a block average of a contractable process.** A block average over any
selection of length `0 < n` has the common coordinate mean `μ[X 0]`.
decls.title: The mean of a block average of a contractable process
decls.statement:
theorem Contractable.integral_blockAverage (hX : Contractable μ X)
    (hint0 : Integrable (X 0) μ) {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) {k : Fin n → ℕ}
    (hint : ∀ i, Integrable (X (k i)) μ) :
    μ[blockAverage X k] = μ[X 0]

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.Contractable.covariance_blockAverage_of_disjoint
decls.doc:
**The covariance of two disjoint block averages of a contractable L² sequence.** Two block
averages over selections `k : Fin n → ℕ` and `k' : Fin m → ℕ` with disjoint ranges
(`0 < n`, `0 < m`) have covariance exactly the common off-diagonal covariance `c = cov[X 0, X 1]`,
regardless of the two block lengths.
decls.title: The covariance of two disjoint block averages of a contractable L² sequence
decls.statement:
theorem Contractable.covariance_blockAverage_of_disjoint [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (hX : Contractable μ X)
    (hX_L2 : ∀ n, MemLp (X n) 2 μ) {n m : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (hm : 0 < m) {k : Fin n → ℕ}
    {k' : Fin m → ℕ} (hdisj : ∀ i j, k i ≠ k' j) :
    cov[blockAverage X k, blockAverage X k'; μ] = cov[X 0, X 1; μ]

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.Contractable.variance_blockAverage_sub_of_disjoint
decls.doc:
**The two-window L² bound for block averages.** For a contractable real-valued process with
`L²` coordinates, two block averages over injective selections `k : Fin n → ℕ` and
`k' : Fin m → ℕ` with disjoint ranges (`0 < n`, `0 < m`) satisfy

```text
Var[blockAverage X k - blockAverage X k'] = (v - c) / n + (v - c) / m,
```

where `v = Var[X 0]` and `c = cov[X 0, X 1]`. The bound vanishes as the block lengths grow, which
is the analytic core of the L² route to de Finetti's theorem.
decls.title: The two-window L² bound for block averages
decls.statement:
theorem Contractable.variance_blockAverage_sub_of_disjoint [IsFiniteMeasure μ]
    (hX : Contractable μ X) (hX_L2 : ∀ n, MemLp (X n) 2 μ) {n m : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (hm : 0 < m)
    {k : Fin n → ℕ} {k' : Fin m → ℕ}
    (hk : Function.Injective k) (hk' : Function.Injective k') (hdisj : ∀ i j, k i ≠ k' j) :
    Var[blockAverage X k - blockAverage X k'; μ]
      = (Var[X 0; μ] - cov[X 0, X 1; μ]) / n + (Var[X 0; μ] - cov[X 0, X 1; μ]) / m

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.Contractable.integral_sq_blockAverage_sub_of_disjoint
decls.doc:
**The two-window L² distance for block averages.** Since two disjoint block averages of a
contractable process share the common mean `μ[X 0]`, the two-window variance bound is the
squared `L²` distance between them:

```text
∫ (blockAverage X k - blockAverage X k')² dμ = (v - c) / n + (v - c) / m.
```
decls.title: The two-window L² distance for block averages
decls.statement:
theorem Contractable.integral_sq_blockAverage_sub_of_disjoint [IsFiniteMeasure μ]
    (hX : Contractable μ X) (hX_L2 : ∀ n, MemLp (X n) 2 μ) {n m : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (hm : 0 < m)
    {k : Fin n → ℕ} {k' : Fin m → ℕ}
    (hk : Function.Injective k) (hk' : Function.Injective k') (hdisj : ∀ i j, k i ≠ k' j) :
    ∫ ω, (blockAverage X k ω - blockAverage X k' ω) ^ 2 ∂μ
      = (Var[X 0; μ] - cov[X 0, X 1; μ]) / n + (Var[X 0; μ] - cov[X 0, X 1; μ]) / m

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.Contractable.covariance_structure_comp
decls.doc:
A measurable real-valued observable with square-integrable coordinates, applied coordinatewise
to a contractable process, gives uniform means, variances, and off-diagonal covariances: the means
agree across all coordinates, so do the variances, and every covariance of two distinct coordinates
takes the same value.
decls.statement:
theorem Contractable.covariance_structure_comp {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α}
    (hX_contractable : Contractable μ X) (hX_meas : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ) {f : α → ℝ}
    (hf : Measurable f) (hL2 : ∀ i, MemLp (fun ω => f (X i ω)) 2 μ) :
    (∀ i j, μ[fun ω => f (X i ω)] = μ[fun ω => f (X j ω)]) ∧
      (∀ i j, Var[fun ω => f (X i ω); μ] = Var[fun ω => f (X j ω); μ]) ∧
      (∀ i j k l, i ≠ j → k ≠ l →
        cov[fun ω => f (X i ω), fun ω => f (X j ω); μ] =
          cov[fun ω => f (X k ω), fun ω => f (X l ω); μ])

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.Contractable.covariance_structure_comp_of_bound
decls.doc:
A bounded measurable real-valued observable of a contractable process has uniform means,
variances, and off-diagonal covariances.  On a finite measure space the square-integrability of the
mapped coordinates is automatic, so only an a.e. bound on each coordinate is required.
decls.statement:
theorem Contractable.covariance_structure_comp_of_bound {μ : Measure Ω} [IsFiniteMeasure μ]
    {X : ℕ → Ω → α} (hX_contractable : Contractable μ X) (hX_meas : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ)
    {f : α → ℝ} (hf : Measurable f) (C : ℝ) (hf_bound : ∀ i, ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, |f (X i ω)| ≤ C) :
    (∀ i j, μ[fun ω => f (X i ω)] = μ[fun ω => f (X j ω)]) ∧
      (∀ i j, Var[fun ω => f (X i ω); μ] = Var[fun ω => f (X j ω); μ]) ∧
      (∀ i j k l, i ≠ j → k ≠ l →
        cov[fun ω => f (X i ω), fun ω => f (X j ω); μ] =
          cov[fun ω => f (X k ω), fun ω => f (X l ω); μ])

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.dist_toLp_sq_eq_integral_sq
decls.doc:
The square of the distance between two `L²` representatives is the integral of the square
of their pointwise difference.

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.dist_blockAverage_toLp_le_of_disjoint
decls.doc: Bound the `L²` distance from a block average to a longer disjoint block average.
decls.statement:
theorem dist_blockAverage_toLp_le_of_disjoint {μ : Measure Ω}
    [IsFiniteMeasure μ] {Y : ℕ → Ω → ℝ} (hY : Contractable μ Y)
    (hY_L2 : ∀ i, MemLp (Y i) 2 μ)
    (hD : 0 ≤ Var[Y 0; μ] - cov[Y 0, Y 1; μ]) {n l : ℕ}
    (hn : 0 < n) (hl : 0 < l) {k : Fin n → ℕ} {k₀ : Fin l → ℕ}
    (hk : Function.Injective k) (hk₀ : Function.Injective k₀)
    (hdisj : ∀ i j, k i ≠ k₀ j) (hnl : n ≤ l) :
    dist
        ((memLp_blockAverage k fun i => hY_L2 (k i)).toLp (blockAverage Y k))
        ((memLp_blockAverage k₀ fun i => hY_L2 (k₀ i)).toLp (blockAverage Y k₀)) ≤
      Real.sqrt (2 * (Var[Y 0; μ] - cov[Y 0, Y 1; μ]) / n)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.dist_blockAverages_toLp_le_via_disjoint
decls.doc: Compare two block averages in `L²` through a longer block disjoint from both.
decls.statement:
theorem dist_blockAverages_toLp_le_via_disjoint {μ : Measure Ω}
    [IsFiniteMeasure μ] {Y : ℕ → Ω → ℝ} (hY : Contractable μ Y)
    (hY_L2 : ∀ i, MemLp (Y i) 2 μ)
    (hD : 0 ≤ Var[Y 0; μ] - cov[Y 0, Y 1; μ]) {n m l : ℕ}
    (hn : 0 < n) (hm : 0 < m) (hl : 0 < l)
