    {k : Fin n → ℕ} {k' : Fin m → ℕ} {k₀ : Fin l → ℕ}
    (hk : Function.Injective k) (hk' : Function.Injective k')
    (hk₀ : Function.Injective k₀) (hdisj : ∀ i j, k i ≠ k₀ j)
    (hdisj' : ∀ i j, k' i ≠ k₀ j) (hnl : n ≤ l) (hml : m ≤ l) :
    dist
        ((memLp_blockAverage k fun i => hY_L2 (k i)).toLp (blockAverage Y k))
        ((memLp_blockAverage k' fun i => hY_L2 (k' i)).toLp (blockAverage Y k')) ≤
      Real.sqrt (2 * (Var[Y 0; μ] - cov[Y 0, Y 1; μ]) / n) +
        Real.sqrt (2 * (Var[Y 0; μ] - cov[Y 0, Y 1; μ]) / m)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.zero_le_variance_sub_covariance_of_contractable
decls.doc: For a contractable `L²` sequence the lag-one covariance never exceeds the variance.
decls.statement:
theorem zero_le_variance_sub_covariance_of_contractable {μ : Measure Ω} [IsFiniteMeasure μ]
    {Y : ℕ → Ω → ℝ} (hY : Contractable μ Y) (hY_L2 : ∀ i, MemLp (Y i) 2 μ) :
    0 ≤ Var[Y 0; μ] - cov[Y 0, Y 1; μ]

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.cauchySeq_blockAverage_prefix_toLp
decls.doc: The prefix block averages of a contractable `L²` sequence are Cauchy in `L²`.
decls.statement:
theorem cauchySeq_blockAverage_prefix_toLp {μ : Measure Ω} [IsFiniteMeasure μ]
    {Y : ℕ → Ω → ℝ} (hY : Contractable μ Y) (hY_L2 : ∀ i, MemLp (Y i) 2 μ) :
    CauchySeq fun m : ℕ =>
      (memLp_blockAverage (fun i : Fin (m + 1) => (i : ℕ)) fun i => hY_L2 i).toLp
        (blockAverage Y fun i : Fin (m + 1) => (i : ℕ))

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.tendsto_dist_blockAverage_window_prefix_toLp
decls.doc: Every fixed-start window approaches the prefix of the same length in `L²`.
decls.statement:
theorem tendsto_dist_blockAverage_window_prefix_toLp {μ : Measure Ω}
    [IsFiniteMeasure μ] {Y : ℕ → Ω → ℝ} (hY : Contractable μ Y)
    (hY_L2 : ∀ i, MemLp (Y i) 2 μ) (r : ℕ) :
    Tendsto (fun m : ℕ =>
        dist ((memLp_blockAverage (fun j : Fin (m + 1) => r + j) fun j => hY_L2 (r + j)).toLp
            (blockAverage Y fun j : Fin (m + 1) => r + j))
          ((memLp_blockAverage (fun i : Fin (m + 1) => (i : ℕ)) fun i => hY_L2 i).toLp
            (blockAverage Y fun i : Fin (m + 1) => (i : ℕ))))
      atTop (𝓝 0)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.tendsto_integral_abs_sub_of_tendsto_eLpNorm_two
decls.doc:
On a finite measure space, `L²` convergence to a limit gives `L¹` convergence of the
integrated absolute difference.

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.weighted_sums_converge_L1_of_memLp
decls.doc:
A measurable observable of a contractable process whose composite with a *single* coordinate is
square-integrable has fixed-start Cesàro averages converging in `L¹` to one common measurable limit.

The start `r` is fixed while the window length `m + 1` tends to infinity. The successor in the
length avoids assigning any special meaning to an empty average.

Contractability makes the mapped coordinates identically distributed, so square-integrability at
coordinate `0` carries to all of them.
decls.statement:
theorem weighted_sums_converge_L1_of_memLp {μ : Measure Ω} [IsFiniteMeasure μ]
    {X : ℕ → Ω → α} (hX : Contractable μ X) (hX_ae : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ)
    {f : α → ℝ} (hf : Measurable f) (hf_L2 : MemLp (fun ω => f (X 0 ω)) 2 μ) :
    ∃ a : Ω → ℝ, Measurable a ∧ MemLp a 1 μ ∧
      ∀ r : ℕ,
        Tendsto
          (fun m => ∫ ω,
            |blockAverage (fun i ω => f (X i ω)) (fun j : Fin (m + 1) => r + j) ω - a ω| ∂μ)
          atTop (𝓝 0)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.weighted_sums_converge_L1
decls.doc:
**Bounded-observable form**, the shape the Layer 3 roadmap names and the determining-class stage
consumes. A uniform bound on `f` gives square-integrability of the composite on a finite measure
space, so this is the direct entry point for bounded observables.
decls.title: Bounded-observable form
decls.statement:
theorem weighted_sums_converge_L1 {μ : Measure Ω} [IsFiniteMeasure μ]
    {X : ℕ → Ω → α} (hX : Contractable μ X) (hX_ae : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ)
    {f : α → ℝ} (hf : Measurable f) (hf_bdd : ∃ C, ∀ x, ‖f x‖ ≤ C) :
    ∃ a : Ω → ℝ, Measurable a ∧ MemLp a 1 μ ∧
      ∀ r : ℕ,
        Tendsto
          (fun m => ∫ ω,
            |blockAverage (fun i ω => f (X i ω)) (fun j : Fin (m + 1) => r + j) ω - a ω| ∂μ)
          atTop (𝓝 0)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.Contractable.integral_coord_eq
decls.doc:
**Equal means from contractability.** For a contractable process with values in a normed
real vector space, all coordinate expectations agree.
decls.title: Equal means from contractability
decls.statement:
theorem Contractable.integral_coord_eq (hZ : Contractable μ Z)
    {i j : ℕ} (hi_meas : AEMeasurable (Z i) μ) (hj_meas : AEMeasurable (Z j) μ) :
    μ[Z i] = μ[Z j]

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.Contractable.variance_coord_eq
decls.doc:
**Equal variances from contractability.** For a contractable real-valued process, all
coordinate variances agree.
decls.title: Equal variances from contractability
decls.statement:
theorem Contractable.variance_coord_eq (hX : Contractable μ X)
    {i j : ℕ} (hi_meas : AEMeasurable (X i) μ) (hj_meas : AEMeasurable (X j) μ) :
    Var[X i; μ] = Var[X j; μ]

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.Contractable.covariance_eq_of_lt
decls.doc:
**Uniform covariances from contractability.** For a contractable real-valued process with
a.e. measurable coordinates, any two off-diagonal covariances agree:
`cov[X i, X j; μ] = cov[X k, X l; μ]` whenever `i < j` and `k < l`.
decls.title: Uniform covariances from contractability
decls.statement:
theorem Contractable.covariance_eq_of_lt (hX : Contractable μ X)
    {i j k l : ℕ} (hi_meas : AEMeasurable (X i) μ) (hj_meas : AEMeasurable (X j) μ)
    (hk_meas : AEMeasurable (X k) μ) (hl_meas : AEMeasurable (X l) μ)
    (hij : i < j) (hkl : k < l) :
    cov[X i, X j; μ] = cov[X k, X l; μ]

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.Contractable.covariance_eq_of_ne
decls.doc:
**Uniform off-diagonal covariances from contractability.** For a contractable real-valued
process with a.e. measurable coordinates, any two off-diagonal covariances agree:
`cov[X i, X j; μ] = cov[X k, X l; μ]` whenever `i ≠ j` and `k ≠ l`.
decls.title: Uniform off-diagonal covariances from contractability
decls.statement:
theorem Contractable.covariance_eq_of_ne (hX : Contractable μ X)
    {i j k l : ℕ} (hi_meas : AEMeasurable (X i) μ) (hj_meas : AEMeasurable (X j) μ)
    (hk_meas : AEMeasurable (X k) μ) (hl_meas : AEMeasurable (X l) μ)
    (hij : i ≠ j) (hkl : k ≠ l) :
    cov[X i, X j; μ] = cov[X k, X l; μ]

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.contractable_covariance_structure
decls.doc:
**The uniform covariance structure of a contractable L² sequence.** A contractable
real-valued process with `L²` coordinates has constant coordinate means and variances, and a
single common off-diagonal covariance: any two unequal-index pairs have equal covariance. This
is the seed of the Layer 3 L² route to de Finetti.
decls.title: The uniform covariance structure of a contractable L² sequence
decls.statement:
theorem contractable_covariance_structure (hX : Contractable μ X) (hX_L2 : ∀ n, MemLp (X n) 2 μ) :
    (∀ i j, μ[X i] = μ[X j]) ∧ (∀ i j, Var[X i; μ] = Var[X j; μ]) ∧
      (∀ i j k l, i ≠ j → k ≠ l → cov[X i, X j; μ] = cov[X k, X l; μ])

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.prefixAverage
decls.doc: The average of the first `n` coordinates of a real-valued process.
decls.statement: def prefixAverage (X : ℕ → Ω → ℝ) (n : ℕ) : Ω → ℝ

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.followingAverage
decls.doc: The average of the `n` coordinates immediately following the first `n` coordinates.
decls.statement: def followingAverage (X : ℕ → Ω → ℝ) (n : ℕ) : Ω → ℝ

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.prefixAverage_apply
decls.statement:
theorem prefixAverage_apply (n : ℕ) (ω : Ω) :
    prefixAverage X n ω = (n : ℝ)⁻¹ * ∑ i : Fin n, X i ω

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.followingAverage_apply
decls.statement:
theorem followingAverage_apply (n : ℕ) (ω : Ω) :
    followingAverage X n ω = (n : ℝ)⁻¹ * ∑ i : Fin n, X (n + i) ω

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.prefixSelection_injective
decls.doc: The prefix selection is injective.
decls.statement:
theorem prefixSelection_injective (n : ℕ) :
    Function.Injective (fun i : Fin n => (i : ℕ))

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.followingSelection_injective
decls.doc: The following-block selection is injective.
decls.statement:
theorem followingSelection_injective (n : ℕ) :
    Function.Injective (fun i : Fin n => n + (i : ℕ))

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.prefix_ne_following
decls.doc: The prefix and following-block selections have disjoint ranges.
decls.statement:
theorem prefix_ne_following (n : ℕ) (i j : Fin n) :
    (i : ℕ) ≠ n + (j : ℕ)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.memLp_prefixAverage
decls.doc: A prefix average of `L²` coordinates is itself `L²`.
decls.statement:
theorem memLp_prefixAverage (n : ℕ) (hX_L2 : ∀ i : Fin n, MemLp (X i) 2 μ) :
    MemLp (prefixAverage X n) 2 μ

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.memLp_followingAverage
decls.doc: A following tail average of `L²` coordinates is itself `L²`.
decls.statement:
theorem memLp_followingAverage (n : ℕ) (hX_L2 : ∀ i : Fin n, MemLp (X (n + i)) 2 μ) :
    MemLp (followingAverage X n) 2 μ

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.Contractable.integral_sq_prefixAverage_sub_followingAverage
decls.doc:
**The exact long-average versus tail-average `L²` bound.** For a contractable process,
the squared `L²` distance between the average of the first `n` coordinates and the average of
the following `n` coordinates is `2 * (v - c) / n`.
decls.title: The exact long-average versus tail-average `L²` bound
decls.statement:
theorem Contractable.integral_sq_prefixAverage_sub_followingAverage [IsFiniteMeasure μ]
    (hX : Contractable μ X) (hX_L2 : ∀ i, MemLp (X i) 2 μ) {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) :
    ∫ ω, (prefixAverage X n ω - followingAverage X n ω) ^ 2 ∂μ =
      2 * (Var[X 0; μ] - cov[X 0, X 1; μ]) / n

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.Contractable.tendsto_integral_sq_prefixAverage_sub_followingAverage
decls.doc:
The long-average versus tail-average squared `L²` distance tends to zero.  The use of
blocks of length `n + 1` avoids a separate convention for the empty average.
decls.statement:
theorem Contractable.tendsto_integral_sq_prefixAverage_sub_followingAverage
    [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (hX : Contractable μ X) (hX_L2 : ∀ i, MemLp (X i) 2 μ) :
    Tendsto
      (fun n => ∫ ω, (prefixAverage X (n + 1) ω - followingAverage X (n + 1) ω) ^ 2 ∂μ)
      atTop (𝓝 0)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.ExchangeableAt.map_values
decls.doc:
Finite exchangeability at a fixed length is preserved by a coordinatewise measurable
map of the value space.
decls.statement:
theorem ExchangeableAt.map_values {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α} {n : ℕ}
    (h : ExchangeableAt μ X n) {f : α → β} (hf : Measurable f)
    (hX : ∀ i : Fin n, AEMeasurable (X i.val) μ) :
    ExchangeableAt μ (fun n ω => f (X n ω)) n

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.Exchangeable.map_values
decls.doc:
Finite exchangeability is preserved by a coordinatewise measurable map of the value
space.
decls.statement:
theorem Exchangeable.map_values {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α} (h : Exchangeable μ X)
    {f : α → β} (hf : Measurable f) (hX : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ) :
    Exchangeable μ (fun n ω => f (X n ω))

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.FullyExchangeable.map_values
decls.doc:

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.measure_eq_of_forall_univ_pi
decls.doc:
Implementation helper for the rectangle characterization: two measures on a finite product
space are equal if they agree on all measurable rectangles `Set.univ.pi B`. Only the first measure
is assumed finite.
decls.statement:
theorem measure_eq_of_forall_univ_pi {ι : Type*} [Finite ι] {α : ι → Type*}
    [∀ i, MeasurableSpace (α i)] {μ ν : Measure (∀ i, α i)} [IsFiniteMeasure μ]
    (h : ∀ B : ∀ i, Set (α i), (∀ i, MeasurableSet (B i)) →
      μ (Set.univ.pi B) = ν (Set.univ.pi B)) :

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.MixedIIDWith
decls.doc:
Mixed i.i.d.-ness with a specified mixing representative `ν`: the random
measure `ν` is measurable, and along every finite selection `k` of **distinct** coordinates
the block law is the `ν`-mixture of the product measure
`ProbabilityMeasure.pi (fun _ => ν ω)`. Distinctness (`Function.Injective k`) is what product
laws need, in contrast with the order condition `StrictMono` of `Contractable`.
decls.statement:
def MixedIIDWith (μ : Measure Ω) (X : ℕ → Ω → α) (ν : Ω → ProbabilityMeasure α) :
    Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.MixedIIDWith.intro
decls.doc:
Constructor: a measurable mixing representative together with the finite-block mixture
identity.
decls.statement:
theorem MixedIIDWith.intro {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α} {ν : Ω → ProbabilityMeasure α}
    (hν : Measurable ν)
    (h : ∀ (m : ℕ) (k : Fin m → ℕ), Function.Injective k →
      blockLaw μ X k = μ.bind fun ω => (ProbabilityMeasure.pi fun _ : Fin m => ν ω).toMeasure) :
    MixedIIDWith μ X ν

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.mixedIIDWith_iff
decls.doc: Simp normal form for `MixedIIDWith`.
decls.statement:
theorem mixedIIDWith_iff {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α} {ν : Ω → ProbabilityMeasure α} :
    MixedIIDWith μ X ν ↔
      Measurable ν ∧
        ∀ (m : ℕ) (k : Fin m → ℕ), Function.Injective k →
          blockLaw μ X k = μ.bind fun ω => (ProbabilityMeasure.pi fun _ : Fin m => ν ω).toMeasure

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.MixedIID
decls.doc: Mixed i.i.d.-ness: existence of a mixing representative.
decls.statement: def MixedIID (μ : Measure Ω) (X : ℕ → Ω → α) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.MixedIID.of_mixingRepresentative

decls.statement:
theorem MixedIID.of_mixingRepresentative {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α}

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.mixedIID_iff
decls.doc: Simp normal form for the existential wrapper `MixedIID`.
decls.statement:
theorem mixedIID_iff {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α} :
    MixedIID μ X ↔ ∃ ν : Ω → ProbabilityMeasure α, MixedIIDWith μ X ν

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.MixedIIDWith.measurable_mixingRepresentative

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.MixedIIDWith.blockLaw_eq_mixture
decls.doc:
The defining finite-block mixture identity of a `MixedIIDWith` witness: along an injective
selection the block law is the `ν`-mixture of the product measure. The prefix specialization is
`MixedIIDWith.prefixLaw_eq_mixture`.
decls.statement:
theorem MixedIIDWith.blockLaw_eq_mixture {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α}
    {ν : Ω → ProbabilityMeasure α} (h : MixedIIDWith μ X ν)
    {m : ℕ} (k : Fin m → ℕ) (hk : Function.Injective k) :
    blockLaw μ X k = μ.bind fun ω => (ProbabilityMeasure.pi fun _ : Fin m => ν ω).toMeasure

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.MixedIID.exists_mixingRepresentative
decls.doc: A `MixedIID` process has a mixing representative.

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.mixedIIDWith_of_forall_rectangles
decls.doc:
A process is `MixedIIDWith μ X ν` once every injective finite block has the same
rectangle values as the corresponding random product-measure mixture.
decls.statement:
theorem mixedIIDWith_of_forall_rectangles {μ : Measure Ω} [IsFiniteMeasure μ]
    {X : ℕ → Ω → α} {ν : Ω → ProbabilityMeasure α} (hν : Measurable ν)
    (h_rect : ∀ (m : ℕ) (k : Fin m → ℕ), Function.Injective k →
      ∀ B : Fin m → Set α, (∀ i, MeasurableSet (B i)) →
        blockLaw μ X k (Set.univ.pi B) =
          ∫⁻ ω, ∏ i : Fin m, (ν ω : Measure α) (B i) ∂μ) :
    MixedIIDWith μ X ν

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.MixedIIDWith.blockLaw_univ_pi
decls.doc:
A `MixedIIDWith` witness gives the expected rectangle factorization for every injective
finite block.
decls.statement:
theorem MixedIIDWith.blockLaw_univ_pi {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α}
    {ν : Ω → ProbabilityMeasure α} (h : MixedIIDWith μ X ν)
    {m : ℕ} (k : Fin m → ℕ) (hk : Function.Injective k)
    (B : Fin m → Set α) (hB : ∀ i, MeasurableSet (B i)) :
    blockLaw μ X k (Set.univ.pi B) =
      ∫⁻ ω, ∏ i : Fin m, (ν ω : Measure α) (B i) ∂μ

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.mixedIIDWith_iff_forall_rectangles
decls.doc: Rectangle factorization is equivalent to the named `MixedIIDWith` relation.
decls.statement:
theorem mixedIIDWith_iff_forall_rectangles {μ : Measure Ω} [IsFiniteMeasure μ]
    {X : ℕ → Ω → α} {ν : Ω → ProbabilityMeasure α} :
    MixedIIDWith μ X ν ↔
      Measurable ν ∧
        ∀ (m : ℕ) (k : Fin m → ℕ), Function.Injective k →
          ∀ B : Fin m → Set α, (∀ i, MeasurableSet (B i)) →
            blockLaw μ X k (Set.univ.pi B) =
              ∫⁻ ω, ∏ i : Fin m, (ν ω : Measure α) (B i) ∂μ

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.mixedIID_iff_exists_forall_rectangles
decls.doc: Rectangle factorization is equivalent to the existential `MixedIID` relation.
decls.statement:
theorem mixedIID_iff_exists_forall_rectangles {μ : Measure Ω} [IsFiniteMeasure μ]
    {X : ℕ → Ω → α} :
    MixedIID μ X ↔
      ∃ ν : Ω → ProbabilityMeasure α, Measurable ν ∧
        ∀ (m : ℕ) (k : Fin m → ℕ), Function.Injective k →
          ∀ B : Fin m → Set α, (∀ i, MeasurableSet (B i)) →
            blockLaw μ X k (Set.univ.pi B) =
              ∫⁻ ω, ∏ i : Fin m, (ν ω : Measure α) (B i) ∂μ

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.MixedIIDWith.blockLaw_eq_pi_of_const
decls.doc:
A constant mixing representative says exactly that every injective block law is the
corresponding product of `p`.
decls.statement:
theorem MixedIIDWith.blockLaw_eq_pi_of_const {μ : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    {X : ℕ → Ω → α} {p : ProbabilityMeasure α} (h : MixedIIDWith μ X fun _ => p)
    {m : ℕ} (k : Fin m → ℕ) (hk : Function.Injective k) :
    blockLaw μ X k = Measure.pi fun _ : Fin m => (p : Measure α)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.MixedIIDWith.aemeasurable_of_const
decls.doc:
A constant mixing representative already forces the coordinates to be a.e. measurable, so no
such hypothesis is needed alongside it: the singleton block law is the probability measure `p`,
hence nonzero, while `Measure.map` of a non-a.e.-measurable function is `0`.
decls.statement:
theorem MixedIIDWith.aemeasurable_of_const {μ : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    {X : ℕ → Ω → α} {p : ProbabilityMeasure α} (h : MixedIIDWith μ X fun _ => p) (i : ℕ) :
    AEMeasurable (X i) μ

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.MixedIIDWith.map_eq_of_const
decls.doc: Every coordinate of a process with a constant mixing representative `p` has law `p`.

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.MixedIIDWith.iIndepFun_of_const
decls.doc:
The coordinates of a process with a constant mixing representative are independent. Along an
injective selection the block law is a product measure, and `Measure.pi` on a finite index set is
exactly what independence of that finite subfamily means.
decls.statement:
theorem MixedIIDWith.iIndepFun_of_const {μ : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {X : ℕ → Ω → α}
    {p : ProbabilityMeasure α} (h : MixedIIDWith μ X fun _ => p) : iIndepFun X μ

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.mixedIIDWith_const_iff_iIndepFun_and_map_eq
decls.doc:
**A constant mixing representative means plain i.i.d.**: `fun _ => p` witnesses `MixedIIDWith`
exactly when the coordinates are independent and each has law `p`.
decls.title: A constant mixing representative means plain i.i.d
decls.statement:
theorem mixedIIDWith_const_iff_iIndepFun_and_map_eq {μ : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    {X : ℕ → Ω → α} {p : ProbabilityMeasure α} :
    (MixedIIDWith μ X fun _ => p) ↔ iIndepFun X μ ∧ ∀ i, μ.map (X i) = (p : Measure α)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.MixedIIDWith.prefixLaw_eq_mixture
decls.doc:

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.MixedIIDWith.map_values
decls.doc:
Mixed i.i.d.-ness with a named mixing representative is preserved by a coordinatewise
measurable map of the value space: if `X` is mixed i.i.d. with mixing representative `ν`, then
`fun i ω => f (X i ω)` is mixed i.i.d. with mixing representative the coordinatewise
pushforward `fun ω => (ν ω).map f`.
decls.statement:
theorem MixedIIDWith.map_values {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α}
    {ν : Ω → ProbabilityMeasure α} (h : MixedIIDWith μ X ν)
    {f : α → β} (hf : Measurable f) (hX : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ) :
    MixedIIDWith μ (fun i ω => f (X i ω)) fun ω => (ν ω).map hf.aemeasurable

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.MixedIID.map_values
decls.doc: Mixed i.i.d.-ness is preserved by a coordinatewise measurable map of the value space.

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.mixedIID_of_mixedIID_pathLaw
decls.doc:
**Transfer of mixed i.i.d.-ness along the path law.** If the coordinate process on path
space is mixed i.i.d. under `pathLaw μ X`, then `X` is mixed i.i.d. under `μ`.
decls.title: Transfer of mixed i.i.d.-ness along the path law
decls.statement:
theorem mixedIID_of_mixedIID_pathLaw {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α}
    (hX_meas : ∀ n, Measurable (X n))
    (h : MixedIID (pathLaw μ X) fun n p => p n) :
    MixedIID μ X

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.pathLaw_eq_bind_infinitePi_of_mixedIIDWith
decls.doc:
**The mixture representation of a path law.** If `ν` is a mixing representative for `X`, the
path law of `X` is the `μ.map ν`-mixture of the infinite product measures `P^{⊗ℕ}`.
decls.title: The mixture representation of a path law
decls.statement:
theorem pathLaw_eq_bind_infinitePi_of_mixedIIDWith {μ : Measure Ω} [IsFiniteMeasure μ]
    {X : ℕ → Ω → α} (hX : ∀ n, AEMeasurable (X n) μ) {ν : Ω → ProbabilityMeasure α}
    (h : MixedIIDWith μ X ν) :
    pathLaw μ X = (μ.map ν).bind fun P => Measure.infinitePi fun _ : ℕ => (P : Measure α)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.mixedIID_mixingLaw_unique
decls.doc:
**Uniqueness of the mixing law.** Two mixing representatives for the same process induce the
same law on `ProbabilityMeasure α`.

Only the *law* `μ.map ν` is unique, not the witness. For a nondegenerate mixing law an independent
copy of a mixing representative is another one, so no witness-level a.e.-equality theorem can
conclude `ν =ᵐ[μ] ν'` from `MixedIIDWith` alone; a.e. uniqueness of the witness belongs to the
conditional predicate (`conditionallyIID_ae_unique`).

*Finiteness* of `μ` is load-bearing rather than decorative: for an infinite base measure, distinct
mixing measures can produce identical `∞`-valued finite-dimensional mixtures, so mixing-law
uniqueness fails at the hypothesis-light generality the definitions otherwise enjoy.

Normalization, however, is not needed. The roadmap states this target with
`[IsProbabilityMeasure μ]`, but the justification it gives only separates finite from infinite base
measures, and the proof goes through for any finite `μ`.
decls.title: Uniqueness of the mixing law

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.MixedIID.existsUnique_mixingLaw
decls.doc:
**Existence and uniqueness of the mixing law.** A mixed i.i.d. process under a probability
law has a unique probability measure `π` on `ProbabilityMeasure α` such that its path law is
the `π`-mixture of the infinite product measures `P^{⊗ℕ}`.

This identifies the mixing law intrinsically from the path law, rather than merely comparing the
pushforwards of two supplied mixing representatives as `mixedIID_mixingLaw_unique` does.
decls.title: Existence and uniqueness of the mixing law
decls.statement:
theorem MixedIID.existsUnique_mixingLaw {μ : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    {X : ℕ → Ω → α} (h : MixedIID μ X) (hX : ∀ n, AEMeasurable (X n) μ) :
    ∃! π : ProbabilityMeasure (ProbabilityMeasure α),
      pathLaw μ X = (π : Measure (ProbabilityMeasure α)).bind
        fun P => Measure.infinitePi fun _ : ℕ => (P : Measure α)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.ContractableLaw
decls.doc:
A measure on one-sided path space is contractable, or spreadable, if it is invariant under
every strictly increasing reindexing of the time coordinate.
decls.statement: def ContractableLaw (ρ : Measure (ℕ → α)) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.ContractableLaw.intro
decls.doc: Constructor for `ContractableLaw` from the defining map invariance.
decls.statement:
theorem ContractableLaw.intro {ρ : Measure (ℕ → α)}
    (h : ∀ φ : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono φ →
      ρ.map (fun x : ℕ → α => fun k => x (φ k)) = ρ) :
    ContractableLaw ρ

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.contractableLaw_iff
decls.doc: Simp normal form for `ContractableLaw`.
decls.statement:
theorem contractableLaw_iff {ρ : Measure (ℕ → α)} :
    ContractableLaw ρ ↔
      ∀ φ : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono φ →
        ρ.map (fun x : ℕ → α => fun k => x (φ k)) = ρ

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.ContractableLaw.map_reindex
decls.doc: The defining invariance of a contractable path law.
decls.statement:
theorem ContractableLaw.map_reindex {ρ : Measure (ℕ → α)}
    (hρ : ContractableLaw ρ)
    {φ : ℕ → ℕ} (hφ : StrictMono φ) :
    ρ.map (fun x : ℕ → α => fun k => x (φ k)) = ρ

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.ContractableLaw.measurePreserving_reindex
decls.doc: A strictly increasing time reindexing preserves a contractable path law.

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.contractableLaw_iff_forall_measurePreserving_reindex
decls.doc:
Path-law contractability is equivalently measure preservation by every strictly increasing
time reindexing.
decls.statement:
theorem contractableLaw_iff_forall_measurePreserving_reindex {ρ : Measure (ℕ → α)} :
    ContractableLaw ρ ↔
      ∀ φ : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono φ →
        MeasurePreserving (fun x : ℕ → α => fun k => x (φ k)) ρ ρ

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.ContractableLaw.map_prefixProj_of_strictMono
decls.doc:
The finite marginal of a contractable path law along any strictly increasing selection
`k : Fin n → ℕ` equals its first-`n` prefix marginal.
decls.statement:
theorem ContractableLaw.map_prefixProj_of_strictMono {ρ : Measure (ℕ → α)}
    (hρ : ContractableLaw ρ) {n : ℕ} {k : Fin n → ℕ} (hk : StrictMono k) :
    ρ.map (fun x : ℕ → α => fun i : Fin n => x (k i)) =
      ρ.map (prefixProj α n)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.contractableLaw_iff_forall_map_prefixProj_of_strictMono
decls.doc:
For finite path laws, contractability is equivalently invariance of every finite-dimensional
marginal under strictly increasing finite selections.
decls.statement:
theorem contractableLaw_iff_forall_map_prefixProj_of_strictMono {ρ : Measure (ℕ → α)}
    [IsFiniteMeasure ρ] :
    ContractableLaw ρ ↔
      ∀ n (k : Fin n → ℕ), StrictMono k →
        ρ.map (fun x : ℕ → α => fun i : Fin n => x (k i)) =
          ρ.map (prefixProj α n)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.exchangeableSigma
decls.doc:
The exchangeable σ-algebra on path space: ambient-measurable events invariant under every
finitely supported permutation of the time coordinate.
decls.statement: def exchangeableSigma (α : Type*) [MeasurableSpace α] : MeasurableSpace (ℕ → α)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.mem_exchangeableSigma_iff
decls.doc:
A set is measurable for `exchangeableSigma` iff it is ambient-measurable and fixed by every
finitely supported time permutation.
decls.statement:
theorem mem_exchangeableSigma_iff {s : Set (ℕ → α)} :
    MeasurableSet[exchangeableSigma α] s ↔
      MeasurableSet s ∧
        ∀ π : Equiv.Perm ℕ, (MulAction.fixedBy ℕ π)ᶜ.Finite →
          permReindex (α := α) π ⁻¹' s = s

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.exchangeableSigma_le
decls.doc: The exchangeable σ-algebra is a sub-σ-algebra of the ambient path-space σ-algebra.
decls.statement:
theorem exchangeableSigma_le :
    exchangeableSigma α ≤ (inferInstance : MeasurableSpace (ℕ → α))

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.MeasurableSet.ambient_of_exchangeableSigma
decls.doc: An `exchangeableSigma`-measurable set is ambient-measurable.
decls.statement:
theorem MeasurableSet.ambient_of_exchangeableSigma {s : Set (ℕ → α)}
    (hs : MeasurableSet[exchangeableSigma α] s) : MeasurableSet s

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.measurableSet_exchangeableSigma_of_forall_permReindex
decls.doc:
An ambient-measurable event fixed by every finitely supported time permutation is measurable
for the exchangeable σ-algebra.
decls.statement:
theorem measurableSet_exchangeableSigma_of_forall_permReindex {s : Set (ℕ → α)}
    (hs_meas : MeasurableSet s)
    (hs_inv : ∀ π : Equiv.Perm ℕ, (MulAction.fixedBy ℕ π)ᶜ.Finite →
      permReindex (α := α) π ⁻¹' s = s) :
    MeasurableSet[exchangeableSigma α] s

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.MeasurableSet.preimage_permReindex_eq_of_exchangeableSigma
decls.doc: An exchangeable event is fixed by any finitely supported time permutation.

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.measurable_permReindex_exchangeableSigma
decls.doc: Reindexing by any permutation is measurable as an endomap of the exchangeable σ-algebra.

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.measurable_exchangeableSigma_of_comp_permReindex_eq
decls.doc:
An ambient-measurable observable fixed by every finitely supported reindexing is measurable
with respect to the exchangeable σ-algebra.
decls.statement:
theorem measurable_exchangeableSigma_of_comp_permReindex_eq [MeasurableSpace β]
    {g : (ℕ → α) → β} (hg : Measurable g)
    (hg_perm : ∀ π : Equiv.Perm ℕ, (MulAction.fixedBy ℕ π)ᶜ.Finite →
      g ∘ permReindex (α := α) π = g) :
    @Measurable (ℕ → α) β (exchangeableSigma α) inferInstance g

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.comp_permReindex_eq_of_measurable_exchangeableSigma
decls.doc:
For a target with measurable singletons, a function measurable with respect to the
exchangeable σ-algebra is fixed by every finitely supported reindexing.
decls.statement:
theorem comp_permReindex_eq_of_measurable_exchangeableSigma [MeasurableSpace β]
    [MeasurableSingletonClass β] {g : (ℕ → α) → β}
    (hg : @Measurable (ℕ → α) β (exchangeableSigma α) inferInstance g)
    {π : Equiv.Perm ℕ} (hπ : (MulAction.fixedBy ℕ π)ᶜ.Finite) :
    g ∘ permReindex (α := α) π = g

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.preimage_permReindex_eq_of_measurable_tailFamily
decls.doc:
If a set belongs to the future path σ-algebra from time `N` onward and `π` fixes every index
`k ≥ N`, then reindexing paths by `π` leaves the set fixed.
decls.statement:
theorem preimage_permReindex_eq_of_measurable_tailFamily
    {s : Set (ℕ → α)} {π : Equiv.Perm ℕ} {N : ℕ}
    (hs : MeasurableSet[tailFamily (fun k (x : ℕ → α) => x k) N] s)
    (hπ : ∀ k, N ≤ k → π k = k) :
    permReindex (α := α) π ⁻¹' s = s

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.pathTail_le_exchangeableSigma
decls.doc:
The path-space tail σ-algebra is contained in the exchangeable σ-algebra: tail events are
fixed by every finitely supported permutation of the time coordinate.
decls.statement:
theorem pathTail_le_exchangeableSigma :
    pathTail α ≤ exchangeableSigma α

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.tail_le_exchangeableSigma
decls.doc: The path-space tail σ-algebra is contained in the exchangeable σ-algebra.
decls.statement:
theorem tail_le_exchangeableSigma :
    pathTail α ≤ exchangeableSigma α

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.ExchangeableLaw.contractableLaw
decls.doc:
An exchangeable finite path law is contractable: invariance under all permutations implies
invariance under every strictly increasing time reindexing.
decls.statement:
theorem ExchangeableLaw.contractableLaw {ρ : Measure (ℕ → α)} [IsFiniteMeasure ρ]
    (hρ : ExchangeableLaw ρ) :
    ContractableLaw ρ

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.blockSwap
decls.doc:
The finitely supported permutation of `ℕ` that swaps the block `[0, N)` with `[N, 2N)`
pointwise and fixes everything from `2 * N` on: Mathlib's half-swap `finAddFlip` on `Fin (N + N)`,
transported to `ℕ` along the value embedding.
decls.statement: def blockSwap (N : ℕ) : Equiv.Perm ℕ

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.blockSwap_apply_of_lt
decls.statement: theorem blockSwap_apply_of_lt {N i : ℕ} (hi : i < N) : blockSwap N i = N + i

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.blockSwap_apply_of_le
decls.statement: theorem blockSwap_apply_of_le {N n : ℕ} (hn : N + N ≤ n) : blockSwap N n = n

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.disjoint_map_blockSwap
decls.doc:
`blockSwap N` carries any index block inside `[0, N)` off itself: the moved copy lands in
`[N, 2N)`. This is the disjointness the independence step consumes.
decls.statement:
theorem disjoint_map_blockSwap {N : ℕ} {F : Finset ℕ} (hF : F ⊆ Finset.range N) :
    Disjoint F (F.map (Equiv.toEmbedding (blockSwap N)))

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.blockSwap_finite_support
decls.statement:
theorem blockSwap_finite_support (N : ℕ) :
    (MulAction.fixedBy ℕ (blockSwap N))ᶜ.Finite

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.pullMoved
decls.doc:
Read a block indexed by the moved index set `F.map π` back onto `F`, along `π`. This is the
change of variables that turns a `π`-reindexed cylinder over `F` into a cylinder over `F.map π`.
decls.statement:
def pullMoved (π : Equiv.Perm ℕ) (F : Finset ℕ) (α : Type*)
    (g : ∀ _j : F.map (Equiv.toEmbedding π), α) : ∀ _i : F, α

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.pullMoved_apply
decls.statement:
theorem pullMoved_apply (π : Equiv.Perm ℕ) (F : Finset ℕ)
    (g : ∀ _j : F.map (Equiv.toEmbedding π), α) (i : F) :
    pullMoved π F α g i = g ⟨π ↑i, Finset.mem_map_of_mem _ i.2⟩

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.preimage_permReindex_cylinder
decls.doc:
Reindexing a cylinder over `F` by `π` is a cylinder over the moved index set `F.map π`: both
sides say that the coordinates `p (π i)`, for `i ∈ F`, lie in `S`.
decls.statement:
theorem preimage_permReindex_cylinder (π : Equiv.Perm ℕ) (F : Finset ℕ)
    (S : Set (∀ _i : F, α)) :
    permReindex (α := α) π ⁻¹' cylinder F S
      = cylinder (F.map (Equiv.toEmbedding π)) (pullMoved π F α ⁻¹' S)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.measurable_pullMoved
decls.statement:
theorem measurable_pullMoved [MeasurableSpace α] (π : Equiv.Perm ℕ) (F : Finset ℕ) :
    Measurable (pullMoved π F α)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.exists_cylinder_measure_symmDiff_lt
decls.doc:
Every measurable path-space event is approximated, in measure, by a measurable cylinder over a
finite index set.
decls.statement:
theorem exists_cylinder_measure_symmDiff_lt [MeasurableSpace α] {ρ : Measure (ℕ → α)}
    [IsFiniteMeasure ρ] {s : Set (ℕ → α)} (hs : MeasurableSet s) {ε : ℝ≥0∞} (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ (F : Finset ℕ) (S : Set (∀ _i : F, α)),
      MeasurableSet S ∧ ρ (symmDiff (cylinder F S) s) < ε

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.measure_pathLaw_inter_cylinder_of_disjoint
decls.doc:
Cylinders over **disjoint** index blocks are independent events under the path law of an
independent family. This is the step that turns the disjointness produced by `blockSwap` into a
product formula.
decls.statement:
theorem measure_pathLaw_inter_cylinder_of_disjoint {μ : Measure Ω}
    {X : ℕ → Ω → α} (hX : ∀ n, AEMeasurable (X n) μ)
    (h_indep : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun X μ)
    {F G : Finset ℕ} (hFG : Disjoint F G)
    {S : Set (∀ _i : F, α)} (hS : MeasurableSet S)
    {T : Set (∀ _j : G, α)} (hT : MeasurableSet T) :
    pathLaw μ X (cylinder F S ∩ cylinder G T)
      = pathLaw μ X (cylinder F S) * pathLaw μ X (cylinder G T)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.symmDiff_inter_subset
decls.statement:
theorem symmDiff_inter_subset {Ω : Type*} {t t' s : Set Ω} :
    symmDiff (t ∩ t') s ⊆ symmDiff t s ∪ symmDiff t' s

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.measure_symmDiff_preimage_permReindex
decls.doc:
**A measure-preserving reindexing does not change how well a set approximates an invariant
event.** If `s` is fixed by the reindexing, then `π⁻¹(t)` differs from `s` by exactly the
`π`-preimage of `t ∆ s`, whose measure is unchanged.

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.abs_mul_sub_mul_self_lt
decls.doc:
**A product estimate.** If `x` and `y` each lie within `e` of `q`, with `y` and `q` in
`[0, 1]`, then `x · y` lies within `2e` of `q²`: the error splits as `(x - q)·y + q·(y - q)`.
decls.title: A product estimate
decls.statement:
lemma abs_mul_sub_mul_self_lt {x y q e : ℝ} (hx : |x - q| < e) (hy : |y - q| < e)
    (hy1 : y ≤ 1) (hy0 : 0 ≤ y) (hq0 : 0 ≤ q) (hq1 : q ≤ 1) : |x * y - q * q| < 2 * e

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.abs_measureReal_inter_sub_lt
decls.doc:
**Two close sets have a close intersection**, since `(A ∩ B) ∆ s` sits inside the union of
the two symmetric differences.
decls.title: Two close sets have a close intersection
decls.statement:
lemma abs_measureReal_inter_sub_lt {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {ρ : Measure Ω}
    [IsFiniteMeasure ρ] {A B s : Set Ω} (hA : NullMeasurableSet A ρ) (hB : NullMeasurableSet B ρ)
    (hs : NullMeasurableSet s ρ)
    {e : ℝ} (h1 : ρ.real (symmDiff A s) < e) (h2 : ρ.real (symmDiff B s) < e) :
    |ρ.real (A ∩ B) - ρ.real s| < 2 * e

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.abs_sub_mul_self_lt_of_close
decls.doc:
**Closing the gap.** If `q` and `q²` are each within `e` of a common value `z`, they are
within `2e` of each other.
decls.title: Closing the gap
decls.statement:
lemma abs_sub_mul_self_lt_of_close {q z e : ℝ} (h1 : |q - z| < e) (h2 : |z - q * q| < e) :
    |q - q * q| < 2 * e

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.abs_measureReal_sub_mul_self_lt_of_symmDiff_lt
decls.doc:
**The approximation squeeze.** Suppose `t` and `t'` each approximate `s` to within `e` in
symmetric difference, and the measure of their intersection factors as the product of their
measures. Then `ρ.real s` lies within `4e` of its own square.

Two estimates meet at the factorization: `t ∩ t'` is within `2e` of `s`, while the product
`ρ.real t * ρ.real t'` is within `2e` of `(ρ.real s)²`. Nothing here concerns exchangeability or
cylinders — it is the arithmetic half of `measureReal_sq_of_exchangeableSigma`, and holds on any
probability space.
decls.title: The approximation squeeze
decls.statement:
lemma abs_measureReal_sub_mul_self_lt_of_symmDiff_lt {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω]
    {ρ : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure ρ] {t t' s : Set Ω}
    (ht : NullMeasurableSet t ρ) (ht' : NullMeasurableSet t' ρ) (hs : NullMeasurableSet s ρ)
    {e : ℝ} (h1 : ρ.real (symmDiff t s) < e) (h2 : ρ.real (symmDiff t' s) < e)
    (hinter : ρ.real (t ∩ t') = ρ.real t * ρ.real t') :
    |ρ.real s - ρ.real s * ρ.real s| < 4 * e

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.measureReal_sq_of_exchangeableSigma
decls.doc:
**The squaring identity.** Under an exchangeable path law in which cylinders over disjoint
index blocks are independent, an exchangeable event has measure equal to its own square.

The mechanism is the classical one: approximate the event by a cylinder over `[0, N)`, move that
cylinder onto the disjoint block `[N, 2N)` by `blockSwap N` — which fixes the event, being
exchangeable, and preserves the law — and let independence factor the two copies.
decls.title: The squaring identity
decls.statement:
theorem measureReal_sq_of_exchangeableSigma {ρ : Measure (ℕ → α)} [IsProbabilityMeasure ρ]
    (hexch : ExchangeableLaw ρ)
    (hprod : ∀ {F G : Finset ℕ}, Disjoint F G → ∀ {S : Set (∀ _i : F, α)}, MeasurableSet S →
      ∀ {T : Set (∀ _j : G, α)}, MeasurableSet T →
      ρ (cylinder (α := fun _ : ℕ => α) F S ∩ cylinder (α := fun _ : ℕ => α) G T)
        = ρ (cylinder (α := fun _ : ℕ => α) F S) * ρ (cylinder (α := fun _ : ℕ => α) G T))
    {s : Set (ℕ → α)} (hs : MeasurableSet[exchangeableSigma α] s) :
    ρ.real s = ρ.real s * ρ.real s

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.measure_eq_zero_or_one_of_exchangeableSigma
decls.doc:
**Zero-one law for exchangeable events**, abstract form: an exchangeable path law in which
cylinders over disjoint index blocks are independent gives every exchangeable event measure `0`
or `1`.
decls.title: Zero-one law for exchangeable events
decls.statement:
theorem measure_eq_zero_or_one_of_exchangeableSigma {ρ : Measure (ℕ → α)} [IsProbabilityMeasure ρ]
    (hexch : ExchangeableLaw ρ)
    (hprod : ∀ {F G : Finset ℕ}, Disjoint F G → ∀ {S : Set (∀ _i : F, α)}, MeasurableSet S →
      ∀ {T : Set (∀ _j : G, α)}, MeasurableSet T →
      ρ (cylinder (α := fun _ : ℕ => α) F S ∩ cylinder (α := fun _ : ℕ => α) G T)
        = ρ (cylinder (α := fun _ : ℕ => α) F S) * ρ (cylinder (α := fun _ : ℕ => α) G T))
    {s : Set (ℕ → α)} (hs : MeasurableSet[exchangeableSigma α] s) :
    ρ s = 0 ∨ ρ s = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.hewittSavage_trivial_of_iIndep
decls.doc:
**The Hewitt–Savage zero-one law.** For an i.i.d. sequence, the exchangeable (symmetric)
σ-algebra on path space is trivial: every exchangeable event has probability `0` or `1`.

Kolmogorov's tail zero-one law does not subsume this: tail triviality needs only independence,
whereas the symmetric σ-algebra can contain non-tail events — for measurable `B` with `B ≠ ∅` and
`B ≠ Set.univ`, the event `{p | ∃ n, p n ∈ B}` is permutation-invariant but not a tail event
(see the module docstring). Identical distribution is used here to obtain exchangeability of the
path law, which is what the argument consumes; it is not claimed to be necessary for the
conclusion — `measure_eq_zero_or_one_of_exchangeableSigma` assumes exchangeability directly.
decls.title: The Hewitt–Savage zero-one law
decls.statement:
theorem hewittSavage_trivial_of_iIndep {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α}
    (h_indep : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun X μ)
    (hident : ∀ i, ProbabilityTheory.IdentDistrib (X i) (X 0) μ μ)
    {s : Set (ℕ → α)} (hs : MeasurableSet[exchangeableSigma α] s) :
    pathLaw μ X s = 0 ∨ pathLaw μ X s = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.tailFamily_coord_eq_comap_shift_iterate
decls.doc:
The future path σ-algebra from time `n` onward is the σ-algebra generated by the `n`-fold
shift: an event depends only on the coordinates `n, n + 1, …` exactly when it is the preimage of an
ambient-measurable event under `(shift α)^[n]`.
decls.statement:
theorem tailFamily_coord_eq_comap_shift_iterate (n : ℕ) :
    tailFamily (fun k (x : ℕ → α) => x k) n =
      MeasurableSpace.comap ((shift α)^[n]) inferInstance

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.pathTail_eq_iInf_comap_shift_iterate
decls.doc:
The path tail σ-algebra is the intersection of the σ-algebras generated by the iterated
shifts.
decls.statement:
theorem pathTail_eq_iInf_comap_shift_iterate :
    pathTail α = ⨅ n : ℕ, MeasurableSpace.comap ((shift α)^[n]) inferInstance

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.measurableSet_tailFamily_of_preimage_shift_iterate_eq
decls.doc:
An ambient-measurable event fixed by the `n`-fold shift lies in the future path σ-algebra from
time `n` onward.

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.invariants_shift_le_pathTail
decls.doc:
**A shift-invariant event is a tail event.**  A shift-invariant event is fixed by every iterate
of the one-sided shift, hence for each `n` it is the preimage under `(shift α)^[n]` of an
ambient-measurable event, so it depends only on the coordinates from time `n` onward.
decls.title: A shift-invariant event is a tail event
decls.statement:
theorem invariants_shift_le_pathTail :
    MeasurableSpace.invariants (shift α) ≤ pathTail α

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.invariants_shift_le_exchangeableSigma
decls.doc:
A shift-invariant event is an exchangeable event: it is a tail event, and tail events are fixed
by every finitely supported permutation of the time coordinate.
decls.statement:
theorem invariants_shift_le_exchangeableSigma :
    MeasurableSpace.invariants (shift α) ≤ exchangeableSigma α

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.trueFrequentlyAtEvenTimes
decls.doc:
The path-space event that a `Bool`-valued path takes the value `true` at infinitely many even
times.  It is a tail event which the one-sided shift does not preserve.
decls.statement: def trueFrequentlyAtEvenTimes : Set (ℕ → Bool)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.mem_trueFrequentlyAtEvenTimes
decls.doc:
Membership in `trueFrequentlyAtEvenTimes` says that `true` occurs at arbitrarily late even
times.
decls.statement:
theorem mem_trueFrequentlyAtEvenTimes {x : ℕ → Bool} :
    x ∈ trueFrequentlyAtEvenTimes ↔ ∀ N, ∃ n, N ≤ n ∧ x (2 * n) = true

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.trueFrequentlyAtEvenTimes_eq_iInter_iUnion
decls.doc:
`trueFrequentlyAtEvenTimes` can be written using only the even times beyond any prescribed
cutoff `r`; this is what makes it measurable for every future σ-algebra.

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.measurableSet_tailFamily_trueFrequentlyAtEvenTimes
decls.doc: `trueFrequentlyAtEvenTimes` belongs to every future path σ-algebra.
decls.statement:
theorem measurableSet_tailFamily_trueFrequentlyAtEvenTimes (r : ℕ) :
    MeasurableSet[tailFamily (fun k (x : ℕ → Bool) => x k) r] trueFrequentlyAtEvenTimes

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.measurableSet_pathTail_trueFrequentlyAtEvenTimes
decls.doc: `trueFrequentlyAtEvenTimes` is a tail event.
decls.statement:
theorem measurableSet_pathTail_trueFrequentlyAtEvenTimes :
    MeasurableSet[pathTail Bool] trueFrequentlyAtEvenTimes

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.preimage_shift_trueFrequentlyAtEvenTimes_ne
decls.doc:
The one-sided shift does not preserve `trueFrequentlyAtEvenTimes`: the alternating path lies
in the event, while its shift, which is `true` exactly at the odd times, does not.
decls.statement:
theorem preimage_shift_trueFrequentlyAtEvenTimes_ne :
    shift Bool ⁻¹' trueFrequentlyAtEvenTimes ≠ trueFrequentlyAtEvenTimes

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.not_pathTail_le_invariants_shift
decls.doc:
**The path tail σ-algebra is not contained in the shift-invariant σ-algebra**: for `Bool`-valued
paths, the tail event "the value `true` occurs at infinitely many even times" is not fixed by the
one-sided shift, which carries the even times onto the odd ones.
decls.title: The path tail σ-algebra is not contained in the shift-invariant σ-algebra
decls.statement:
theorem not_pathTail_le_invariants_shift :
    ¬ pathTail Bool ≤ MeasurableSpace.invariants (shift Bool)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.invariants_shift_lt_pathTail
decls.doc:
For `Bool`-valued paths the inclusion `invariants_shift_le_pathTail` is strict: the
shift-invariant σ-algebra is a proper sub-σ-algebra of the path tail σ-algebra.
decls.statement:
theorem invariants_shift_lt_pathTail :
    MeasurableSpace.invariants (shift Bool) < pathTail Bool

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.invariants_shift_lt_exchangeableSigma
decls.doc:
For `Bool`-valued paths the shift-invariant σ-algebra is a proper sub-σ-algebra of the
exchangeable σ-algebra.
decls.statement:
theorem invariants_shift_lt_exchangeableSigma :
    MeasurableSpace.invariants (shift Bool) < exchangeableSigma Bool

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.ExchangeableLaw
decls.doc:
A measure on one-sided path space is exchangeable if it is invariant under every
permutation of the time coordinate.
decls.statement: def ExchangeableLaw (ρ : Measure (ℕ → α)) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.ExchangeableLaw.intro
decls.doc: Constructor for `ExchangeableLaw` from the defining map invariance.

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.exchangeableLaw_iff
decls.doc: Simp normal form for `ExchangeableLaw`.
decls.statement:
theorem exchangeableLaw_iff {ρ : Measure (ℕ → α)} :
    ExchangeableLaw ρ ↔ ∀ π : Equiv.Perm ℕ, ρ.map (permReindex (α := α) π) = ρ

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.ExchangeableLaw.map_permReindex
decls.doc: The defining invariance of an exchangeable path law.
decls.statement:
theorem ExchangeableLaw.map_permReindex {ρ : Measure (ℕ → α)} (hρ : ExchangeableLaw ρ)
    (π : Equiv.Perm ℕ) :
    ρ.map (permReindex (α := α) π) = ρ

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.ExchangeableLaw.measurePreserving_permReindex
decls.doc: Reindexing by a time permutation preserves an exchangeable path law.

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.exchangeableLaw_iff_forall_measurePreserving_permReindex
decls.doc: Path-law exchangeability is equivalently measure preservation by every time permutation.
decls.statement:
theorem exchangeableLaw_iff_forall_measurePreserving_permReindex {ρ : Measure (ℕ → α)} :
    ExchangeableLaw ρ ↔
      ∀ π : Equiv.Perm ℕ, MeasurePreserving (permReindex (α := α) π) ρ ρ

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.map_reindex_prefixProj
decls.doc:
The first-`n` prefix marginal of a path-space measure reindexed by `φ : ℕ → ℕ` is its
finite coordinate marginal along `i ↦ φ i`. This only uses coordinate reindexing, so it holds
for an arbitrary function `φ`, not just a permutation.
decls.statement:
theorem map_reindex_prefixProj (ρ : Measure (ℕ → α)) (φ : ℕ → ℕ) (n : ℕ) :
    (ρ.map (fun x : ℕ → α => fun k => x (φ k))).map (prefixProj α n) =
      ρ.map (fun x : ℕ → α => fun i : Fin n => x (φ i.val))

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.ExchangeableLaw.map_prefixProj_of_injective
decls.doc:
The finite marginal of an exchangeable path law along any injective selection
`k : Fin n → ℕ` equals its first-`n` prefix marginal: an exchangeable law has the same
finite-dimensional distribution along every injective finite selection of coordinates.
decls.statement:
theorem ExchangeableLaw.map_prefixProj_of_injective {ρ : Measure (ℕ → α)}
    (hρ : ExchangeableLaw ρ) {n : ℕ} (k : Fin n → ℕ) (hk : Function.Injective k) :
    ρ.map (fun x : ℕ → α => fun i : Fin n => x (k i)) =
      ρ.map (prefixProj α n)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.ExchangeableLaw.map_prefixProj_perm
decls.doc:
The prefix marginal of an exchangeable path law is invariant under permutations of the
finite prefix, the special case of `ExchangeableLaw.map_prefixProj_of_injective` along the
injective selection `i ↦ (σ i).val`.
decls.statement:
theorem ExchangeableLaw.map_prefixProj_perm {ρ : Measure (ℕ → α)} (hρ : ExchangeableLaw ρ)
    (n : ℕ) (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) :
    ρ.map (fun x : ℕ → α => fun i : Fin n => x (σ i).val) =
      ρ.map (prefixProj α n)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.FullyExchangeable.exchangeableLaw_pathLaw
decls.doc: A fully exchangeable process has an exchangeable path law.

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.fullyExchangeable_iff_exchangeableLaw_pathLaw
decls.doc: A process is fully exchangeable iff its path law is an exchangeable path-space measure.

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.exchangeable_iff_exchangeableLaw_pathLaw
decls.doc:
For finite laws, finite exchangeability of a process is equivalent to exchangeability of
its path law.

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.fullyExchangeable_of_exchangeableLaw_pathLaw
decls.doc: A process whose path law is exchangeable is fully exchangeable.

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.exchangeable_of_exchangeableLaw_pathLaw
decls.doc: A process whose path law is exchangeable is finitely exchangeable under a finite base law.
decls.statement:
theorem exchangeable_of_exchangeableLaw_pathLaw {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α}
    [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (hX_meas : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ)
    (hρ : ExchangeableLaw (pathLaw μ X)) :
    Exchangeable μ X

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.Contractable.contractableLaw_pathLaw
decls.doc: A contractable process has a contractable path law.

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.contractable_iff_contractableLaw_pathLaw
decls.doc: Contractability of a process is equivalent to contractability of its path law.

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.contractable_of_contractableLaw_pathLaw
decls.doc: If a process has a contractable path law, then the process is contractable.
decls.statement:
theorem contractable_of_contractableLaw_pathLaw {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α}
    [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (hX_meas : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ)
    (hρ : ContractableLaw (pathLaw μ X)) :
    Contractable μ X

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.Contractable.coordinate_pathLaw
decls.doc:
**The coordinate process under a contractable process's path law is contractable.** This is the
form path-space arguments need: transfer the hypothesis to `pathLaw μ X`, work there — path space
being standard Borel whenever the state space is — and carry the conclusion back.
decls.title: The coordinate process under a contractable process's path law is contractable

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.processShift
decls.doc:
The shifted random path of a process, as the `m`-fold path-space shift `(shift α)^[m]` of the
process's path (reusing the merged path shift): `ω ↦ (n ↦ X (m + n) ω)`.
decls.statement: def processShift (X : ℕ → Ω → α) (m : ℕ) : Ω → (ℕ → α)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.processShift_apply
decls.doc: Coordinate equation for `processShift`: its `n`th coordinate is `X (m + n)`.
decls.statement:
theorem processShift_apply (X : ℕ → Ω → α) (m n : ℕ) (ω : Ω) :
    processShift X m ω n = X (m + n) ω

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.measurable_processShift
decls.doc: The shifted process is measurable when its tail coordinates `X (m + ·)` are.
decls.statement:
theorem measurable_processShift {X : ℕ → Ω → α} {m : ℕ} (hX : ∀ n, Measurable (X (m + n))) :
    Measurable (processShift X m)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.processShift_eq_shift_iterate
decls.doc: `processShift X m` is the `m`-fold path shift `(shift α)^[m]` composed with the process path.
decls.statement:
theorem processShift_eq_shift_iterate (X : ℕ → Ω → α) (m : ℕ) :
    processShift X m = (shift α)^[m] ∘ fun ω n => X n ω

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.map_processShift
decls.doc:
Measure-level bridge: the law of the shifted process is the pushforward of the path law by the
`m`-fold path shift `(shift α)^[m]`.
decls.statement:
theorem map_processShift (μ : Measure Ω) {X : ℕ → Ω → α} (hX : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ) (m : ℕ) :
    μ.map (processShift X m) = (pathLaw μ X).map ((shift α)^[m])

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.shift_iterate_apply
decls.doc: Iterating the one-sided shift by `n` drops the first `n` coordinates.
decls.statement:
theorem shift_iterate_apply (n k : ℕ) (x : ℕ → α) :
    (shift α)^[n] x k = x (k + n)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.shift_iterate_eq_reindex
decls.doc: The `n`th shift iterate is the coordinate reindexing `k ↦ k + n`.
decls.statement:
theorem shift_iterate_eq_reindex (n : ℕ) :
    (shift α)^[n] = fun x : ℕ → α => fun k => x (k + n)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.measurable_shift_iterate
decls.doc: Every iterate of the one-sided path-space shift is measurable.
decls.statement: theorem measurable_shift_iterate (n : ℕ) : Measurable ((shift α)^[n])

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.aemeasurable_shift_iterate
decls.doc:
Every iterate of the one-sided path-space shift is a.e.-measurable with respect to any
measure on path space.
decls.statement:
theorem aemeasurable_shift_iterate (n : ℕ) (μ : Measure (ℕ → α)) :
    AEMeasurable ((shift α)^[n]) μ

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.prefixProj_shift_iterate
decls.doc: A finite prefix after `n` shifts is the block of coordinates `n, …, n + m - 1`.
decls.statement:
theorem prefixProj_shift_iterate (n m : ℕ) (x : ℕ → α) :
    prefixProj α m ((shift α)^[n] x) = fun i : Fin m => x (i.val + n)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.measurable_prefixProj_shift_iterate
decls.doc: The prefix projection after an `n`-fold shift is measurable.
decls.statement:
theorem measurable_prefixProj_shift_iterate (n m : ℕ) :
    Measurable (fun x : ℕ → α => prefixProj α m ((shift α)^[n] x))

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.map_shift_iterate_pathLaw
decls.doc:
Shifting the path law by `n` gives the path law of the reindexed process
`k ↦ X (k + n)`.

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.map_prefixProj_shift_iterate_pathLaw
decls.doc:
The first `m` coordinates of the path law after `n` shifts are the block law along
`i ↦ i + n`.
decls.statement:
theorem map_prefixProj_shift_iterate_pathLaw (μ : Measure Ω) {X : ℕ → Ω → α}
    (hX : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ) (n m : ℕ) :
    ((pathLaw μ X).map ((shift α)^[n])).map (prefixProj α m) =
      blockLaw μ X (fun i : Fin m => i.val + n)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.map_prefixProj_shift_iterate_pathLaw_apply
decls.doc: The setwise form of `map_prefixProj_shift_iterate_pathLaw`.
decls.statement:
theorem map_prefixProj_shift_iterate_pathLaw_apply (μ : Measure Ω) {X : ℕ → Ω → α}
    (hX : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ) (n m : ℕ) (s : Set (Fin m → α)) :
    ((pathLaw μ X).map ((shift α)^[n])).map (prefixProj α m) s =
      blockLaw μ X (fun i : Fin m => i.val + n) s

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.exists_strictMono_nat_extending_fin
decls.doc:
A strictly monotone finite selection `k : Fin m → ℕ` extends to a strictly increasing
self-map of `ℕ` that agrees with `k` on the first `m` inputs.
decls.statement:
theorem exists_strictMono_nat_extending_fin {m : ℕ} {k : Fin m → ℕ} (hk : StrictMono k) :
    ∃ φ : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono φ ∧ ∀ i : Fin m, φ i.val = k i

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.Contractable.measurePreserving_shift_iterate
decls.doc: Every iterate of the one-sided shift preserves the path law of a contractable process.
decls.statement:
theorem Contractable.measurePreserving_shift_iterate {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α}
    [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (hX : Contractable μ X) (hX_meas : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ)
    (n : ℕ) :
    MeasurePreserving ((shift α)^[n]) (pathLaw μ X) (pathLaw μ X)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.Contractable.map_shift_iterate_pathLaw
decls.doc: Iterating the one-sided shift leaves the path law of a contractable process unchanged.
decls.statement:
theorem Contractable.map_shift_iterate_pathLaw {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α}
    [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (hX : Contractable μ X) (hX_meas : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ)
    (n : ℕ) :
    (pathLaw μ X).map ((shift α)^[n]) = pathLaw μ X

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.Contractable.pathLaw_preimage_shift_iterate
decls.doc: Setwise stationarity for every shift iterate of a contractable process.
decls.statement:
theorem Contractable.pathLaw_preimage_shift_iterate {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α}
    [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (hX : Contractable μ X) (hX_meas : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ)
    (n : ℕ) {s : Set (ℕ → α)} (hs : NullMeasurableSet s (pathLaw μ X)) :
    pathLaw μ X (((shift α)^[n]) ⁻¹' s) = pathLaw μ X s

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.Contractable.map_processShift_eq_pathLaw
decls.doc: The law of the `n`-step shifted process of a contractable process is the original path law.
decls.statement:
theorem Contractable.map_processShift_eq_pathLaw {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α}
    [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (hX : Contractable μ X) (hX_meas : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ)
    (n : ℕ) :
    μ.map (processShift X n) = pathLaw μ X

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.Contractable.map_prefixProj_shift_iterate_pathLaw_eq_prefixLaw
decls.doc: Prefix laws are unchanged after shifting a contractable process by any finite amount.
decls.statement:
theorem Contractable.map_prefixProj_shift_iterate_pathLaw_eq_prefixLaw {μ : Measure Ω}
    {X : ℕ → Ω → α} (hX : Contractable μ X)
    (hX_meas : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ) (n m : ℕ) :
    ((pathLaw μ X).map ((shift α)^[n])).map (prefixProj α m) = prefixLaw μ X m

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.Exchangeable.measurePreserving_shift
decls.doc: **An exchangeable process has a shift-invariant path law.**
decls.title: An exchangeable process has a shift-invariant path law

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.Exchangeable.measurePreserving_shift_iterate
decls.doc: Every iterate of the one-sided shift preserves the path law of an exchangeable process.
decls.statement:
theorem Exchangeable.measurePreserving_shift_iterate {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α}
    [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (hX : Exchangeable μ X) (hX_meas : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ)
    (n : ℕ) :
    MeasurePreserving ((shift α)^[n]) (pathLaw μ X) (pathLaw μ X)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.Exchangeable.map_shift_iterate_pathLaw
decls.doc: Iterating the one-sided shift leaves the path law of an exchangeable process unchanged.
decls.statement:
theorem Exchangeable.map_shift_iterate_pathLaw {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α}
    [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (hX : Exchangeable μ X) (hX_meas : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ)
    (n : ℕ) :
    (pathLaw μ X).map ((shift α)^[n]) = pathLaw μ X

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.Exchangeable.pathLaw_preimage_shift_iterate
decls.doc: Setwise stationarity for every shift iterate.
decls.statement:
theorem Exchangeable.pathLaw_preimage_shift_iterate {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α}
    [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (hX : Exchangeable μ X) (hX_meas : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ)
    (n : ℕ) {s : Set (ℕ → α)} (hs : NullMeasurableSet s (pathLaw μ X)) :
    pathLaw μ X (((shift α)^[n]) ⁻¹' s) = pathLaw μ X s

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.Exchangeable.map_processShift_eq_pathLaw
decls.doc: The law of the `n`-step shifted process of an exchangeable process is the original path law.
decls.statement:
theorem Exchangeable.map_processShift_eq_pathLaw {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α}
    [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (hX : Exchangeable μ X) (hX_meas : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ)
    (n : ℕ) :
    μ.map (processShift X n) = pathLaw μ X

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.Exchangeable.map_prefixProj_shift_iterate_pathLaw_eq_prefixLaw
decls.doc: Prefix laws are unchanged after shifting an exchangeable process by any finite amount.
decls.statement:
theorem Exchangeable.map_prefixProj_shift_iterate_pathLaw_eq_prefixLaw {μ : Measure Ω}
    {X : ℕ → Ω → α} (hX : Exchangeable μ X)
    (hX_meas : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ) (n m : ℕ) :
    ((pathLaw μ X).map ((shift α)^[n])).map (prefixProj α m) = prefixLaw μ X m

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.threeCycle
decls.doc:
The deterministic 3-cycle process on `ZMod 3`: from state `ω`, the `n`-th coordinate is the
`n`-fold rotation `ω + n`.
decls.statement: abbrev threeCycle : ℕ → ZMod 3 → ZMod 3

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.threeCycle_apply
decls.statement: theorem threeCycle_apply (n : ℕ) (ω : ZMod 3) : threeCycle n ω = ω + (n : ZMod 3)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.threeCycleMeasure
decls.doc:
The uniform probability law on `ZMod 3`, the stationary law of the 3-cycle. This is a `def`
(not an `abbrev`) so that the `IsAddRightInvariant` instance below keys on `threeCycleMeasure`
and stays scoped to this example, rather than leaking to the general `uniformOn Set.univ`.
decls.statement: def threeCycleMeasure : Measure (ZMod 3)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.threeCycleMeasure_def
decls.doc: The stationary measure of the 3-cycle is the uniform law on `ZMod 3`.
decls.statement: theorem threeCycleMeasure_def : threeCycleMeasure = uniformOn Set.univ

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.instIsAddRightInvariantZModOfNatNatThreeCycleMeasure
decls.doc:
The uniform law on `ZMod 3` is invariant under right addition, supplying the translation
invariance used in the shift-stationarity proof.
decls.statement: instance : threeCycleMeasure.IsAddRightInvariant

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.threeCycleMeasure_singleton
decls.doc: The uniform law gives mass `3⁻¹` to each singleton.
decls.statement: theorem threeCycleMeasure_singleton (a : ZMod 3) : threeCycleMeasure {a} = 3⁻¹

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.threeCycle_measurePreserving_shift
decls.doc:
**The 3-cycle is stationary.** Its path law is preserved by the one-sided shift: shifting the
sample path of `ω` yields the sample path of `ω + 1`, and the uniform law is translation
invariant.
decls.title: The 3-cycle is stationary
decls.statement:
theorem threeCycle_measurePreserving_shift :
    MeasurePreserving (shift (ZMod 3)) (pathLaw threeCycleMeasure threeCycle)
      (pathLaw threeCycleMeasure threeCycle)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.threeCycle_straight_event
decls.doc:
The straight two-coordinate event `{X₀ = 0, X₁ = 1}` is realized only from the start state
`0`.

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.threeCycle_spread_event
decls.doc:
The spread event `{X₀ = 0, X₂ = 1}` is unrealizable: it would need `ω = 0` and `ω + 2 = 1`
simultaneously.
decls.statement:
theorem threeCycle_spread_event :
    {ω : ZMod 3 | ∀ i : Fin 2,
        threeCycle ((![0, 2] : Fin 2 → ℕ) i) ω ∈
          (![{0}, {1}] : Fin 2 → Set (ZMod 3)) i} = ∅

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.threeCycle_not_contractable
decls.doc:
**The 3-cycle is not contractable.** The pair law `(X₀, X₂)` along the strictly increasing
selection `0 < 2` differs from the prefix pair law `(X₀, X₁)`: on the rectangle `{X₀ = 0, X₁ = 1}`
the prefix law has mass `3⁻¹` while the spread law has mass `0`.
decls.title: The 3-cycle is not contractable
decls.statement: theorem threeCycle_not_contractable : ¬ Contractable threeCycleMeasure threeCycle

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.threeCycle_not_exchangeable
decls.doc:
**The 3-cycle is not exchangeable.** Its two-coordinate prefix law already fails the finite
exchangeability symmetry: the pair `(X₀, X₁) = (ω, ω + 1)` ranges over
`{(0, 1), (1, 2), (2, 0)}`, so the law of `(X₀, X₁)` differs from that of `(X₁, X₀)`.
decls.title: The 3-cycle is not exchangeable
decls.statement: theorem threeCycle_not_exchangeable : ¬ Exchangeable threeCycleMeasure threeCycle

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.condIndep_of_indicator_condExp_eq
decls.doc:
**Conditional independence from the drop-information criterion.** If conditioning `𝟙_H` on
`mF ⊔ mG` is a.e. the same as conditioning on `mG` (for every `mH`-measurable `H`), then `mF` and
`mH` are conditionally independent given `mG`.
decls.title: Conditional independence from the drop-information criterion
decls.statement:
theorem condIndep_of_indicator_condExp_eq {Ω : Type*} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω}
    [StandardBorelSpace Ω] {μ : Measure Ω} [IsFiniteMeasure μ] {mF mG mH : MeasurableSpace Ω}
    (hmF : mF ≤ mΩ) (hmG : mG ≤ mΩ) (hmH : mH ≤ mΩ)
    (h : ∀ H, MeasurableSet[mH] H →
      μ[H.indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) | mF ⊔ mG]
        =ᵐ[μ] μ[H.indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) | mG]) :
    CondIndep mG mF mH hmG μ

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.mul_indicator_one_eq_indicator
decls.doc:
Pointwise product with the constant-`1` indicator of `s` restricts a function to the
indicator of `s`. Lets indicator products be rewritten without pointwise case splits.
decls.statement:
lemma mul_indicator_one_eq_indicator {Ω : Type*} (s : Set Ω) (φ : Ω → ℝ) :
    φ * s.indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) = s.indicator φ

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.setIntegral_condExp_indicator_eq_on_rectangle
decls.doc:
Rectangle step for `condExp_indicator_sup_eq_of_condIndep`: over a rectangle `tF ∩ tG` (`tF`
`mF`-measurable, `tG` `mG`-measurable), the conditional expectation given `mG` of an
`mH`-measurable indicator integrates to the same value as the indicator itself.
decls.statement:
lemma setIntegral_condExp_indicator_eq_on_rectangle {Ω : Type*} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω}
    [StandardBorelSpace Ω] {μ : @Measure Ω mΩ} [IsFiniteMeasure μ]
    {mF mG mH : MeasurableSpace Ω}
    (hmF : mF ≤ mΩ) (hmG : mG ≤ mΩ) (hmH : mH ≤ mΩ)
    (hCI : CondIndep mG mF mH hmG μ)
    {H : Set Ω} (hH : MeasurableSet[mH] H)
    {tF tG : Set Ω} (htF : MeasurableSet[mF] tF) (htG : MeasurableSet[mG] tG) :
    ∫ x in tF ∩ tG, (μ[H.indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) | mG]) x ∂μ
      = ∫ x in tF ∩ tG, H.indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) x ∂μ

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.isPiSystem_inter_measurableSet
decls.doc:
The sets `tF ∩ tG`, with `tF` being `mF`-measurable and `tG` being `mG`-measurable, form a
π-system.

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.sup_eq_generateFrom_inter_measurableSet
decls.doc:
The join `mF ⊔ mG` is generated by the sets `tF ∩ tG` with `tF` being `mF`-measurable and
`tG` being `mG`-measurable.

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.setIntegral_condExp_indicator_eq_of_measurableSet_sup
decls.doc:
Under conditional independence, the conditional expectation `μ[𝟙_H | mG]` has the same
integral as `𝟙_H` over every `mF ⊔ mG`-measurable set.
decls.statement:
lemma setIntegral_condExp_indicator_eq_of_measurableSet_sup {Ω : Type*}
    {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} [StandardBorelSpace Ω] {μ : @Measure Ω mΩ} [IsFiniteMeasure μ]
    {mF mG mH : MeasurableSpace Ω} (hmF : mF ≤ mΩ) (hmG : mG ≤ mΩ) (hmH : mH ≤ mΩ)
    (hCI : CondIndep mG mF mH hmG μ) {H : Set Ω} (hH : MeasurableSet[mH] H)
    {s : Set Ω} (hs : MeasurableSet[mF ⊔ mG] s) :
    ∫ x in s, (μ[H.indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) | mG]) x ∂μ
      = ∫ x in s, H.indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) x ∂μ

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.condExp_indicator_sup_eq_of_condIndep
decls.doc:
**Projection from conditional independence.** If `mF` and `mH` are conditionally independent
given `mG` (in the sense of Mathlib's `ProbabilityTheory.CondIndep`), then conditioning the
indicator of an `mH`-measurable set `H` on the join `mF ⊔ mG` collapses to conditioning on `mG`.
This is the converse of `condIndep_of_indicator_condExp_eq`.
decls.title: Projection from conditional independence
decls.statement:
theorem condExp_indicator_sup_eq_of_condIndep {Ω : Type*} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω}
    [StandardBorelSpace Ω] {μ : @Measure Ω mΩ} [IsFiniteMeasure μ]
    {mF mG mH : MeasurableSpace Ω}
    (hmF : mF ≤ mΩ) (hmG : mG ≤ mΩ) (hmH : mH ≤ mΩ)
    (hCI : CondIndep mG mF mH hmG μ)
    {H : Set Ω} (hH : MeasurableSet[mH] H) :
    μ[H.indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) | mF ⊔ mG]
      =ᵐ[μ]
    μ[H.indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) | mG]

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.marginal_law_eq_of_pair_law
decls.doc: From the pair-law equality `(X, W) =ᵈ (X, W')`, extract the marginal `W =ᵈ W'`.
decls.statement:
lemma marginal_law_eq_of_pair_law (X : Ω → α) (W W' : Ω → γ)
    (hX : Measurable X) (hW : Measurable W) (hW' : Measurable W')
    (h_law : Measure.map (fun ω => (X ω, W ω)) μ = Measure.map (fun ω => (X ω, W' ω)) μ) :
    Measure.map W μ = Measure.map W' μ

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.setIntegral_indicator_preimage_eq_of_pair_law
decls.doc:
If the pair laws agree, `(X, W) =ᵈ (X, W')`, the indicator of `X ⁻¹' A` has the same integral
over `W ⁻¹' B` as over `W' ⁻¹' B`.
decls.statement:
lemma setIntegral_indicator_preimage_eq_of_pair_law
    (X : Ω → α) (W W' : Ω → γ)
    (hX : Measurable X) (hW : Measurable W) (hW' : Measurable W')
    (h_law : Measure.map (fun ω => (X ω, W ω)) μ = Measure.map (fun ω => (X ω, W' ω)) μ)
    {A : Set α} (hA : MeasurableSet A) {B : Set γ} (hB : MeasurableSet B) :
    ∫ ω in W ⁻¹' B, (X ⁻¹' A).indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) ω ∂μ
      = ∫ ω in W' ⁻¹' B, (X ⁻¹' A).indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) ω ∂μ

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.setIntegral_map_eq_setIntegral_preimage_of_condExp_comp
decls.doc:
Set-integral of a Doob–Dynkin factor: if `g ∘ W` represents `μ[φ | comap W]`, the integral of
`g` over `B` against `Measure.map W μ` equals the integral of `φ` over `W ⁻¹' B`.
decls.statement:
lemma setIntegral_map_eq_setIntegral_preimage_of_condExp_comp
    {W : Ω → γ} (hW : Measurable W) [SigmaFinite (μ.trim (measurable_iff_comap_le.mp hW))]
    {g : γ → ℝ} (hg : AEStronglyMeasurable g (Measure.map W μ))
    {φ : Ω → ℝ} (hφ_int : Integrable φ μ)
    (hg_eq : μ[φ | MeasurableSpace.comap W inferInstance] = g ∘ W)
    {B : Set γ} (hB : MeasurableSet B) :
    ∫ y in B, g y ∂(Measure.map W μ) = ∫ ω in W ⁻¹' B, φ ω ∂μ

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.integral_sq_condExp_eq_of_pair_law
decls.doc: Helper for Kallenberg 1.3: the square-integrals of the two conditional expectations agree.
decls.statement:
lemma integral_sq_condExp_eq_of_pair_law [IsFiniteMeasure μ]
    (X : Ω → α) (W W' : Ω → γ)
    (hX : Measurable X) (hW : Measurable W) (hW' : Measurable W')
    (h_law : Measure.map (fun ω => (X ω, W ω)) μ = Measure.map (fun ω => (X ω, W' ω)) μ)
    {A : Set α} (hA : MeasurableSet A) :
    ∫ ω, (μ[(X ⁻¹' A).indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ))
            | MeasurableSpace.comap W inferInstance]) ω
        * (μ[(X ⁻¹' A).indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ))
            | MeasurableSpace.comap W inferInstance]) ω ∂μ
      = ∫ ω, (μ[(X ⁻¹' A).indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ))
              | MeasurableSpace.comap W' inferInstance]) ω
          * (μ[(X ⁻¹' A).indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ))
              | MeasurableSpace.comap W' inferInstance]) ω ∂μ

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.ae_eq_of_integral_mul_eq_of_integral_sq_eq
decls.doc:
Two real functions with equal integrals of their squares (`∫ g₁² = ∫ g₂²`) and matching cross
integral (`∫ g₂ g₁ = ∫ g₁²`) are a.e. equal: the `L²` distance polarises to
`∫ (g₂ - g₁)² = ∫ g₂² - 2 ∫ g₂ g₁ + ∫ g₁² = 0`. The products `g₁²`, `g₂²`, `g₂ g₁` are assumed
integrable.
decls.statement:
lemma ae_eq_of_integral_mul_eq_of_integral_sq_eq {Ω : Type*} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω}
    {μ : Measure Ω} {g₁ g₂ : Ω → ℝ}
    (hg₁sq : Integrable (fun ω => g₁ ω * g₁ ω) μ)
    (hg₂sq : Integrable (fun ω => g₂ ω * g₂ ω) μ)
    (hg₂g₁ : Integrable (fun ω => g₂ ω * g₁ ω) μ)
    (h_cross : ∫ ω, g₂ ω * g₁ ω ∂μ = ∫ ω, g₁ ω * g₁ ω ∂μ)
    (h_sq : ∫ ω, g₁ ω * g₁ ω ∂μ = ∫ ω, g₂ ω * g₂ ω ∂μ) :
    g₁ =ᵐ[μ] g₂

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.ae_norm_condExp_indicator_le_one
decls.doc:
The conditional expectation of a `0/1` indicator is bounded by `1` in norm almost everywhere,
on any sub-σ-algebra: the indicator itself is, and conditioning does not increase the bound.

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.condExp_indicator_eq_of_law_eq_of_comap_le
decls.doc:
**Kallenberg Lemma 1.3 (contraction-independence).** If `(X, W) =ᵈ (X, W')` and
`σ(W) ≤ σ(W')` (so `W` is a contraction of `W'`), then conditioning the indicator of `X` on the
finer `σ(W')` equals conditioning on the coarser `σ(W)`, almost everywhere.
decls.title: Kallenberg Lemma 1.3 (contraction-independence)
decls.statement:
theorem condExp_indicator_eq_of_law_eq_of_comap_le [IsFiniteMeasure μ]
    (X : Ω → α) (W W' : Ω → γ)
    (hX : Measurable X) (hW : Measurable W) (hW' : Measurable W')
    (h_law : Measure.map (fun ω => (X ω, W ω)) μ = Measure.map (fun ω => (X ω, W' ω)) μ)
    (h_le : MeasurableSpace.comap W inferInstance ≤ MeasurableSpace.comap W' inferInstance)
    {A : Set α} (hA : MeasurableSet A) :
    μ[(X ⁻¹' A).indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) | MeasurableSpace.comap W' inferInstance]
      =ᵐ[μ]
    μ[(X ⁻¹' A).indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) | MeasurableSpace.comap W inferInstance]

decls.name: MeasureTheory.ae_upcrossings_condExp_lt_top
decls.doc:
Reverse-martingale upcrossing bound: for real `a < b`, the expected number of upcrossings of
`n ↦ μ[f | 𝔽 n]` on `[a, b]` is finite, so the upcrossings are a.e. finite.
decls.statement:
lemma ae_upcrossings_condExp_lt_top
    [IsFiniteMeasure μ] {𝔽 : ℕ → MeasurableSpace Ω}
    (h_antitone : Antitone 𝔽) (h_le : ∀ n, 𝔽 n ≤ (inferInstance : MeasurableSpace Ω))
    (f : Ω → ℝ) (hf : Integrable f μ) {a b : ℝ} (hab : a < b) :
    ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, upcrossings a b (fun n => μ[f | 𝔽 n]) ω < ⊤

decls.name: MeasureTheory.exists_integrable_tendsto_ae_condExp_of_antitone
decls.doc:
A.S. existence of the limit of `μ[f | 𝔽 n]` for integrable `f` along an antitone filtration —
the L¹ reverse-martingale (Lévy downward) limit.
decls.statement:
lemma exists_integrable_tendsto_ae_condExp_of_antitone
    [IsFiniteMeasure μ] {𝔽 : ℕ → MeasurableSpace Ω}
    (h_antitone : Antitone 𝔽) (h_le : ∀ n, 𝔽 n ≤ (inferInstance : MeasurableSpace Ω))
    (f : Ω → ℝ) (hf : Integrable f μ) :
    ∃ Xlim, (Integrable Xlim μ ∧
           ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Tendsto (fun n => μ[f | 𝔽 n] ω) atTop (𝓝 (Xlim ω)))

decls.name: MeasureTheory.condExp_exists_ae_limit_antitone
decls.doc:
Roadmap Layer 4 target name (`TauCetiRoadmap/Exchangeability`) for
`exists_integrable_tendsto_ae_condExp_of_antitone`.
decls.statement: alias condExp_exists_ae_limit_antitone

decls.name: MeasureTheory.condExp_iInf_ae_eq_of_tendsto_ae_of_tendsto_eLpNorm
decls.doc:
**Identification of the reverse-martingale limit.** If `μ[f | 𝔽 n]` converges to `Xlim` both
almost everywhere and in `L¹`, along an antitone filtration, then `Xlim` is the conditional
expectation of `f` on the tail σ-algebra `⨅ n, 𝔽 n`.

The proof uses the a.e. convergence to make `Xlim` measurable for `⨅ n, 𝔽 n`, and the `L¹`
convergence to transport the tower property `μ[μ[f | 𝔽 n] | ⨅ n, 𝔽 n] =ᵐ μ[f | ⨅ n, 𝔽 n]` to the
limit.
decls.title: Identification of the reverse-martingale limit
decls.statement:
lemma condExp_iInf_ae_eq_of_tendsto_ae_of_tendsto_eLpNorm
    [IsFiniteMeasure μ] {𝔽 : ℕ → MeasurableSpace Ω} {f Xlim : Ω → ℝ}
    (h_filtration : Antitone 𝔽)
    (h_le0 : 𝔽 0 ≤ (inferInstance : MeasurableSpace Ω))
    (hXlimint : Integrable Xlim μ)
    (h_tendsto : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Tendsto (fun n => μ[f | 𝔽 n] ω) atTop (𝓝 (Xlim ω)))
    (hL1_conv : Tendsto (fun n => eLpNorm (μ[f | 𝔽 n] - Xlim) 1 μ) atTop (𝓝 0)) :
    μ[f | ⨅ n, 𝔽 n] =ᵐ[μ] Xlim

decls.name: MeasureTheory.tendsto_ae_and_eLpNorm_condExp_iInf
decls.doc:
Lévy's downward theorem, proving the almost-everywhere and `L¹` forms together.

The `L¹` convergence is not an afterthought of the a.e. convergence: the Vitali step that upgrades
a.e. convergence of the uniformly integrable family `μ[f | 𝔽ₙ]` to `L¹` convergence is what
identifies the a.e. limit as `μ[f | ⨅ₙ 𝔽ₙ]` in the first place. Proving the two conclusions in one
pass avoids running that step twice; the public `tendsto_ae_condExp_iInf` and
`tendsto_eLpNorm_condExp_iInf` are its two projections.
decls.statement:
theorem tendsto_ae_and_eLpNorm_condExp_iInf
    [IsFiniteMeasure μ]
    {𝔽 : ℕ → MeasurableSpace Ω}
    (h_filtration : Antitone 𝔽)
    (h_le0 : 𝔽 0 ≤ (inferInstance : MeasurableSpace Ω))
    (f : Ω → ℝ) :
    (∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Tendsto
        (fun n => μ[f | 𝔽 n] ω)
        atTop
        (𝓝 (μ[f | ⨅ n, 𝔽 n] ω))) ∧
      Tendsto (fun n => eLpNorm (μ[f | 𝔽 n] - μ[f | ⨅ n, 𝔽 n]) 1 μ) atTop (𝓝 0)

decls.name: MeasureTheory.tendsto_ae_condExp_iInf
decls.doc:
**Conditional expectation converges along a decreasing filtration (Lévy's downward theorem).**

For a decreasing filtration `𝔽ₙ`, the sequence `μ[f | 𝔽ₙ]` converges almost surely to
`μ[f | ⨅ₙ 𝔽ₙ]` — the reverse-martingale (Lévy downward) limit. As in Mathlib's upward
`MeasureTheory.tendsto_ae_condExp`, no integrability hypothesis is needed: `condExp` vanishes on
non-integrable arguments, so the statement is trivial there.
decls.title: Conditional expectation converges along a decreasing filtration (Lévy's downward theorem)
decls.statement:
theorem tendsto_ae_condExp_iInf
    [IsFiniteMeasure μ]
    {𝔽 : ℕ → MeasurableSpace Ω}
    (h_filtration : Antitone 𝔽)
    (h_le0 : 𝔽 0 ≤ (inferInstance : MeasurableSpace Ω))
    (f : Ω → ℝ) :
    ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Tendsto
      (fun n => μ[f | 𝔽 n] ω)
      atTop
      (𝓝 (μ[f | ⨅ n, 𝔽 n] ω))

decls.name: MeasureTheory.tendsto_eLpNorm_condExp_iInf
decls.doc:
**Conditional expectation converges in `L¹` along a decreasing filtration (Lévy's downward
theorem, `L¹` form).**

For a decreasing filtration `𝔽ₙ`, the sequence `μ[f | 𝔽ₙ]` converges in `L¹` to `μ[f | ⨅ₙ 𝔽ₙ]`.
This upgrades the almost-everywhere statement `tendsto_ae_condExp_iInf`: the conditional
expectations `μ[f | 𝔽ₙ]` of a fixed integrable function form a uniformly integrable family, so
their a.e. convergence is convergence in `L¹` by Vitali's theorem. As in Mathlib's upward
`MeasureTheory.tendsto_eLpNorm_condExp`, which this is the downward analogue of, no integrability
hypothesis is needed: `condExp` vanishes on non-integrable arguments, so the statement is trivial
there.
decls.statement:
theorem tendsto_eLpNorm_condExp_iInf
    [IsFiniteMeasure μ]
    {𝔽 : ℕ → MeasurableSpace Ω}
    (h_filtration : Antitone 𝔽)
    (h_le0 : 𝔽 0 ≤ (inferInstance : MeasurableSpace Ω))
    (f : Ω → ℝ) :
    Tendsto (fun n => eLpNorm (μ[f | 𝔽 n] - μ[f | ⨅ n, 𝔽 n]) 1 μ) atTop (𝓝 0)

decls.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_pos_part_revCEFinite_le
decls.doc:
Positive-part L¹ bound for the reversed conditional-expectation process: for integrable `f`,
the integral of `(revCEFinite f 𝔽 N M · - a)⁺` is bounded by `‖f‖₁ + |a| · μ(univ)`,
uniformly in the horizon `N` and the time `M`.
decls.statement:
lemma lintegral_pos_part_revCEFinite_le
    (f : Ω → ℝ) (hf : Integrable f μ) (a : ℝ) (N M : ℕ) :
    ∫⁻ ω, ENNReal.ofReal ((revCEFinite (μ := μ) f 𝔽 N M ω - a)⁺) ∂μ
      ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (eLpNorm f 1 μ).toReal + ENNReal.ofReal |a| * μ Set.univ

decls.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_upcrossings_revCEFinite_bdd
decls.doc:
Surrogate bound (kept private): uniform (in `N`) bound on upcrossings for the reversed
conditional-expectation process.

For an integrable `f` and the process obtained by reversing an antitone filtration, the expected
number of upcrossings is uniformly bounded, independent of the time horizon `N`, by Doob's
upcrossing inequality. The public `upcrossings_bdd_uniform` transfers this surrogate bound to the
genuine antitone sequence `n ↦ μ[f | 𝔽 n]`.
decls.statement:
lemma lintegral_upcrossings_revCEFinite_bdd
    [IsFiniteMeasure μ]
    (h_antitone : Antitone 𝔽) (h_le : ∀ n, 𝔽 n ≤ (inferInstance : MeasurableSpace Ω))
    (f : Ω → ℝ) (hf : Integrable f μ) (a b : ℝ) (hab : a < b) :
    ∃ C : ENNReal, C < ⊤ ∧ ∀ N,
      ∫⁻ ω, (upcrossings (↑a) (↑b) (fun n => revCEFinite (μ := μ) f 𝔽 N n) ω) ∂μ ≤ C

decls.name: MeasureTheory.upcrossingsBefore_condExp_le_upcrossings_neg_revCEFinite
decls.doc:
Pathwise comparison: the upcrossings of `n ↦ μ[f | 𝔽 n]` on `[a, b]` before time `N` are
bounded by the total upcrossings on `[-b, -a]` of the negated finite-horizon reverse process.
decls.statement:
lemma upcrossingsBefore_condExp_le_upcrossings_neg_revCEFinite
    (f : Ω → ℝ) {a b : ℝ} (hab : a < b) (N : ℕ) (ω : Ω) :
    ↑(upcrossingsBefore a b (fun n => μ[f | 𝔽 n]) N ω)
