      ≤ upcrossings (-b) (-a) (-(fun n => revCEFinite (μ := μ) f 𝔽 N n)) ω

decls.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_upcrossings_neg_revCEFinite_eq
decls.doc:
Finite-horizon integral step: negating commutes a.e. with the reverse conditional-expectation
process (via `condExp_neg`), so the upcrossing integrals of the negated process and of the reverse
process of `-f` agree.
decls.statement:
lemma lintegral_upcrossings_neg_revCEFinite_eq
    (f : Ω → ℝ) (a b : ℝ) (N : ℕ) :
    ∫⁻ ω, upcrossings (-b) (-a)
        (-(fun n => revCEFinite (μ := μ) f 𝔽 N n)) ω ∂μ
      = ∫⁻ ω, upcrossings (-b) (-a)
          (fun n => revCEFinite (μ := μ) (fun x => -f x) 𝔽 N n) ω ∂μ

decls.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_upcrossings_le_of_forall_lintegral_upcrossingsBefore_le
decls.doc:
Upgrade a uniform-in-`N` bound on the per-horizon `upcrossingsBefore` integrals to a bound on
the total `upcrossings` integral, by monotone convergence in the horizon `N`. The adapted process
`g` supplies the measurability of each `upcrossingsBefore` count.

decls.name: MeasureTheory.exists_lintegral_upcrossings_condExp_le
decls.doc:
Uniform crossing bound for the antitone conditional-expectation sequence.

For an antitone filtration `𝔽` and integrable `f`, the expected number of upcrossings of the
conditional-expectation process `n ↦ μ[f | 𝔽 n]` on any interval `[a, b]` is finite — the L¹
reverse-martingale upcrossing bound. This is the crossing bound consumed by the antitone-limit
(Lévy downward) argument.
decls.statement:
theorem exists_lintegral_upcrossings_condExp_le [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (h_antitone : Antitone 𝔽)
    (h_le : ∀ n, 𝔽 n ≤ (inferInstance : MeasurableSpace Ω)) (f : Ω → ℝ) (hf : Integrable f μ)
    (a b : ℝ) (hab : a < b) :
    ∃ C : ENNReal, C < ⊤ ∧ ∫⁻ ω, upcrossings (↑a) (↑b) (fun n => μ[f | 𝔽 n]) ω ∂μ ≤ C

decls.name: MeasureTheory.upcrossings_bdd_uniform
decls.doc:
Roadmap Layer 4 target name (`TauCetiRoadmap/Exchangeability`) for the uniform upcrossing bound
`exists_lintegral_upcrossings_condExp_le`.
decls.statement: alias upcrossings_bdd_uniform

decls.name: MeasureTheory.hitting_congr
decls.doc: Helper: hitting respects pointwise equality on `[n, m]`.

decls.name: MeasureTheory.upperCrossingTime_congr
decls.doc: Helper: `upperCrossingTime` respects pointwise equality on `[0, N]`.
decls.statement:
lemma upperCrossingTime_congr {Ω ι : Type*} [Preorder ι] [OrderBot ι] [InfSet ι]
    {a b : ℝ} {f g : ι → Ω → ℝ} {N : ι} {ω : Ω} (h : ∀ n ≤ N, f n ω = g n ω) :
    ∀ k, upperCrossingTime a b f N k ω = upperCrossingTime a b g N k ω

decls.name: MeasureTheory.upcrossingsBefore_congr
decls.doc: Helper: `upcrossingsBefore` is invariant under pointwise equality on `[0, N]`.
decls.statement:
lemma upcrossingsBefore_congr {Ω ι : Type*} [Preorder ι] [OrderBot ι] [InfSet ι]
    {a b : ℝ} {f g : ι → Ω → ℝ} {N : ι} {ω : Ω} (h : ∀ n ≤ N, f n ω = g n ω) :
    upcrossingsBefore a b f N ω = upcrossingsBefore a b g N ω

decls.name: MeasureTheory.hittingBtwn_succ_congr
decls.doc:
Free-boundary hitting congruence: at horizon `N + 1`, agreement of `u` and `v` on `[n, N]`
already forces equal hitting times. A hit at the free top index `N + 1` yields the horizon value
`N + 1`, exactly as the no-hit default does, so the value at `N + 1` never matters.

decls.name: MeasureTheory.upperCrossingTime_succ_congr
decls.doc: Helper: `upperCrossingTime` at horizon `N + 1` respects pointwise equality on `[0, N]`.

decls.name: MeasureTheory.upcrossingsBefore_succ_congr
decls.doc:
Helper: `upcrossingsBefore` at horizon `N + 1` is invariant under pointwise equality on
`[0, N]`. The extra index `N + 1` is a "free boundary" that never affects the crossing count.

decls.name: MeasureTheory.upcrossingsBefore_le_upcrossingsBefore_neg_revProcess_succ
decls.doc:
Reversed-crossing bound: the upcrossings of `X` on `[a, b]` before time `N` are bounded by the
upcrossings of the negated time-reversed process `-(revProcess X N)` on `[-b, -a]` before time
`N + 1`. The extra `N + 1` horizon on the reversed side is what makes crossings completing exactly
at time `N` count.
decls.statement:
lemma upcrossingsBefore_le_upcrossingsBefore_neg_revProcess_succ
    {Ω : Type*} (X : ℕ → Ω → ℝ) (a b : ℝ) (hab : a < b) (N : ℕ) (ω : Ω) :
    upcrossingsBefore a b X N ω
      ≤ upcrossingsBefore (-b) (-a) (-(revProcess X N)) (N + 1) ω

decls.name: MeasureTheory.revProcess
decls.doc:
Time reversal of a stochastic process up to time `N`, using Mathlib's horizon reversal
`Polynomial.revAt`. For `n ≤ N` this is `X (N - n)`; see `revProcess_apply_of_le`.
decls.statement: def revProcess {Ω α : Type*} (X : ℕ → Ω → α) (N : ℕ) : ℕ → Ω → α

decls.name: MeasureTheory.revProcess_apply
decls.doc: Defining equation for `revProcess` (whose body is deliberately not `@[expose]`d).
decls.statement:
lemma revProcess_apply {Ω α : Type*} (X : ℕ → Ω → α) (N n : ℕ) (ω : Ω) :
    revProcess X N n ω = X (Polynomial.revAt N n) ω

decls.name: MeasureTheory.revProcess_apply_of_le
decls.doc: Below the horizon, `Polynomial.revAt N` is genuine subtraction, so `revProcess` reverses.
decls.statement:
lemma revProcess_apply_of_le {Ω α : Type*} (X : ℕ → Ω → α) {N n : ℕ} (h : n ≤ N) (ω : Ω) :
    revProcess X N n ω = X (N - n) ω

decls.name: MeasureTheory.upperCrossingTime_neg_revProcess_succ_le
decls.statement:
lemma upperCrossingTime_neg_revProcess_succ_le
    {Ω : Type*} (X : ℕ → Ω → ℝ) (a b : ℝ) (hab : a < b) (N m' i : ℕ) (ω : Ω)
    (hσ_lt_N : upperCrossingTime a b X N (i + 1) ω < N)
    (ih' : upperCrossingTime (-b) (-a) (-(revProcess X N)) (N + 1) m' ω
      ≤ N - lowerCrossingTime a b X N (i + 1) ω) :
    upperCrossingTime (-b) (-a) (-(revProcess X N)) (N + 1) (m' + 1) ω
      ≤ N - lowerCrossingTime a b X N i ω

decls.name: MeasureTheory.upperCrossingTime_neg_revProcess_le_strong
decls.doc:
Strong version tracking the bijection explicitly.

For `m ≤ k` with `X`'s `k`-th crossing completing before `N`:
  `upperCrossingTime Y (N + 1) m ≤ N - lowerCrossingTime X (k - m)`.

This captures that `Y`'s `m`-th crossing corresponds to `X`'s `(k - m + 1)`-th crossing (reversed
order), with `Y`'s crossing ending at time `N - τ` where `τ` is the start of `X`'s crossing.
decls.statement:
lemma upperCrossingTime_neg_revProcess_le_strong
    {Ω : Type*} (X : ℕ → Ω → ℝ) (a b : ℝ) (hab : a < b) (N k m : ℕ) (ω : Ω)
    (hm : m ≤ k)
    (h_k : upperCrossingTime a b X N k ω < N) :
    upperCrossingTime (-b) (-a) (-(revProcess X N)) (N + 1) m ω
      ≤ N - lowerCrossingTime a b X N (k - m) ω

decls.name: MeasureTheory.upperCrossingTime_neg_revProcess_le
decls.doc:
**Time-reversal crossing bound.**

For a process `X` with `k` upcrossings `[a→b]` completing before time `N`, the time-reversed
negated process `-(revProcess X N)` has its `k`-th upcrossing `[-b→-a]` completing at
time `≤ N`.
decls.title: Time-reversal crossing bound
decls.statement:
lemma upperCrossingTime_neg_revProcess_le
    {Ω : Type*} (X : ℕ → Ω → ℝ) (a b : ℝ) (hab : a < b) (N k : ℕ) (ω : Ω)
    (h_k : upperCrossingTime a b X N k ω < N) :
    upperCrossingTime (-b) (-a) (-(revProcess X N)) (N + 1) k ω ≤ N

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.iInf_measurableSpace_eq_of_antitone_of_eventually_const
decls.doc:
The intersection of an antitone filtration that is constant from index `N` on collapses to
the stabilized σ-algebra `𝔽 N`. This is the order fact behind the Lévy-downward specialization.

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.condExp_eq_of_eventually_const
decls.doc:
Past the stabilization index the conditional expectations are literally equal: for `N ≤ n`
the σ-algebras `𝔽 n` and `𝔽 N` coincide, so `μ[f | 𝔽 n]` and `μ[f | 𝔽 N]` are the same term.

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.tendsto_condExp_of_eventually_const
decls.doc:
**Elementary convergence.** Along a filtration constant from index `N` on, the conditional
expectations `μ[f | 𝔽 n]` reach `μ[f | 𝔽 N]` exactly and stay there, so they converge to it at
every point. No integrability of `f` or finiteness of `μ` is needed: the sequence is eventually
constant.
decls.title: Elementary convergence

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.condExp_iInf_eq_of_eventually_const
decls.doc:
**The Lévy downward limit collapses.** For an antitone filtration constant from index `N`
on, the reverse-martingale limit `μ[f | ⨅ n, 𝔽 n]` produced by `tendsto_ae_condExp_iInf` is the
conditional expectation onto the stabilized σ-algebra `𝔽 N`.
decls.title: The Lévy downward limit collapses
decls.statement:
theorem condExp_iInf_eq_of_eventually_const
    (h_anti : Antitone 𝔽) {N : ℕ} (h_const : ∀ n, N ≤ n → 𝔽 n = 𝔽 N) (f : Ω → ℝ) :
    μ[f | ⨅ n, 𝔽 n] = μ[f | 𝔽 N]

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.tendsto_ae_condExp_of_eventually_const
decls.doc:
**Lévy's downward theorem specializes correctly to an eventually constant filtration.**

Run the flagship `MeasureTheory.tendsto_ae_condExp_iInf` on an antitone filtration that is
constant from index `N` on, then collapse its limit through
`condExp_iInf_eq_of_eventually_const`. The a.e. limit it delivers is `μ[f | 𝔽 N]` — exactly the
value the sequence already reaches by the elementary
`tendsto_condExp_of_eventually_const`. The general and elementary computations agree.
decls.title: Lévy's downward theorem specializes correctly to an eventually constant filtration
decls.statement:
theorem tendsto_ae_condExp_of_eventually_const [IsFiniteMeasure μ]
    (h_anti : Antitone 𝔽) (h_le0 : 𝔽 0 ≤ (inferInstance : MeasurableSpace Ω))
    {N : ℕ} (h_const : ∀ n, N ≤ n → 𝔽 n = 𝔽 N)
    (f : Ω → ℝ) :
    ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Tendsto (fun n => μ[f | 𝔽 n] ω) atTop (𝓝 (μ[f | 𝔽 N] ω))

decls.name: MeasureTheory.revFiltration
decls.doc:
Reverse filtration on a finite horizon `N`: its level `n` is `𝔽 (N - n)`. Used for
finite-horizon time reversal of an antitone family `𝔽`.

decls.name: MeasureTheory.revCEFinite
decls.doc:
Reverse conditional-expectation process at finite horizon `N`: for `n ≤ N` this is
`μ[f | 𝔽 (N - n)]`, for a Banach-space-valued `f`.
decls.statement:
def revCEFinite (f : Ω → E) (𝔽 : ℕ → MeasurableSpace Ω) (N n : ℕ) :
    Ω → E

decls.name: MeasureTheory.revCEFinite_apply
decls.doc: Defining equation for `revCEFinite` (whose body is deliberately not `@[expose]`d).
decls.statement:
lemma revCEFinite_apply (f : Ω → E) (𝔽 : ℕ → MeasurableSpace Ω) (N n : ℕ) :
    revCEFinite (μ := μ) f 𝔽 N n = μ[f | 𝔽 (N - n)]

decls.name: MeasureTheory.revFiltration_apply
decls.doc: Levels of the reverse filtration: `revFiltration 𝔽 … N` at `n` is `𝔽 (N - n)`.
decls.statement:
lemma revFiltration_apply (𝔽 : ℕ → MeasurableSpace Ω) (h_antitone : Antitone 𝔽)
    (h_le : ∀ n, 𝔽 n ≤ m0) (N n : ℕ) :
    (revFiltration 𝔽 h_antitone h_le N) n = 𝔽 (N - n)

decls.name: MeasureTheory.revCEFinite_martingale
decls.doc:
Finite-horizon reversal adapter for Mathlib's `martingale_condExp`: the reversed
conditional-expectation process `revCEFinite … N` is a genuine (forward) martingale for the forward
filtration `revFiltration 𝔽 … N`.
decls.statement:
theorem revCEFinite_martingale (h_antitone : Antitone 𝔽) (h_le : ∀ n, 𝔽 n ≤ m0) (f : Ω → E)
    (N : ℕ) [SigmaFiniteFiltration μ (revFiltration 𝔽 h_antitone h_le N)] :
    Martingale (fun n => revCEFinite (μ := μ) f 𝔽 N n) (revFiltration 𝔽 h_antitone h_le N) μ

decls.name: TauCeti.coordFun
decls.doc: The `i`-th coordinate, as a continuous function on a subset of `ι → ℝ`.
decls.statement: def coordFun (K : Set (ι → ℝ)) (i : ι) : C(K, ℝ)

decls.name: TauCeti.coordBCF
decls.doc: The `i`-th coordinate as a bounded continuous function, using compactness of `K`.
decls.statement: def coordBCF (K : Set (ι → ℝ)) [CompactSpace K] (i : ι) : K →ᵇ ℝ

decls.name: TauCeti.coordBCF_apply
decls.statement:
theorem coordBCF_apply [CompactSpace K] (i : ι) (x : K) :
    coordBCF K i x = (x : ι → ℝ) i

decls.name: TauCeti.coordAlgebra
decls.doc:
The subalgebra of `K →ᵇ ℝ` generated by the coordinate functions. Its elements are exactly the
polynomial functions of the coordinates.

It is packaged as a `StarSubalgebra` because that is what
`MeasureTheory.ext_of_forall_mem_subalgebra_integral_eq_of_polish` consumes; the star condition
holds trivially, as `star` is the identity on real-valued functions.
decls.statement: def coordAlgebra (K : Set (ι → ℝ)) [CompactSpace K] : StarSubalgebra ℝ (K →ᵇ ℝ)

decls.name: TauCeti.coordAlgebra_separatesPoints
decls.doc:
Distinct points of `K` differ in some coordinate, so the coordinate functions separate
points.
decls.statement:
theorem coordAlgebra_separatesPoints (K : Set (ι → ℝ)) [CompactSpace K] :
    ((coordAlgebra K).map (toContinuousMapStarₐ ℝ)).SeparatesPoints

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_monomial_of_mem_closure
decls.doc:
Every element of the multiplicative closure of the coordinate functions is a mixed monomial.
`Submonoid.exists_of_mem_closure_range` supplies the exponent vector; this only transports the
resulting equation of bounded continuous functions to its pointwise form.

decls.name: TauCeti.integral_eq_of_mem_coordAlgebra
decls.doc:
Integrals against `μ` and `ν` agree on the whole coordinate subalgebra, given agreement on
mixed monomials. The monomials are the multiplicative closure of the coordinates, so this is a
span induction; the multiplicative step is unavailable, since integral agreement is not closed
under products.
decls.statement:
theorem integral_eq_of_mem_coordAlgebra [Fintype ι] [CompactSpace K] [MeasurableSpace K]
    [BorelSpace K] {μ ν : Measure K} [IsFiniteMeasure μ] [IsFiniteMeasure ν]
    (hmom : ∀ n : ι → ℕ, ∫ x, ∏ i, (x : ι → ℝ) i ^ n i ∂μ
      = ∫ x, ∏ i, (x : ι → ℝ) i ^ n i ∂ν)
    {g : K →ᵇ ℝ} (hg : g ∈ coordAlgebra K) :
    ∫ x, g x ∂μ = ∫ x, g x ∂ν

decls.name: TauCeti.Measure.ext_of_forall_integral_monomial_eq
decls.doc:
**Multivariate moment determinacy on a compact set.** Two finite Borel measures on a compact
subset `K` of `ι → ℝ` that assign the same integral to every mixed monomial
`x ↦ ∏ i, x i ^ n i` are equal.

Compactness is what makes the monomials suffice: it bounds the coordinates, so the polynomial
functions are dense in `C(K, ℝ)` by Stone–Weierstrass. Without it the conclusion fails, as the
classical lognormal counterexample on `ℝ` shows.
decls.title: Multivariate moment determinacy on a compact set
decls.statement:
theorem Measure.ext_of_forall_integral_monomial_eq [Fintype ι] [CompactSpace K] [MeasurableSpace K]
    [BorelSpace K] {μ ν : Measure K} [IsFiniteMeasure μ] [IsFiniteMeasure ν]
    (hmom : ∀ n : ι → ℕ, ∫ x, ∏ i, (x : ι → ℝ) i ^ n i ∂μ
      = ∫ x, ∏ i, (x : ι → ℝ) i ^ n i ∂ν) :
    μ = ν

decls.name: TauCeti.Measure.ext_of_forall_integral_monomial_eq_of_support
decls.doc:
**Multivariate moment determinacy, ambient form.** Two finite Borel measures on `ι → ℝ`
that are both supported on a common compact set `K` and assign the same integral to every mixed
monomial are equal.

Both support hypotheses are required *by this proof*, which restricts to the compact subtype: that
route establishes only `μ.restrict K = ν.restrict K`, and each support hypothesis is what identifies
one restriction with the original measure.

`hν` cannot simply be dropped. Classically, a compactly supported finite measure is
moment-determinate among all finite measures *whose moments exist*. But `hmom` is stated with
Bochner integrals, and `MeasureTheory.integral_undef` makes `∫ f ∂ν = 0` when `f` is not
`ν`-integrable, so `hmom` asserts nothing where `ν`'s moments diverge. Taking `μ` a Dirac mass and
`ν` a Cauchy measure satisfies every hypothesis with `hν` deleted, since each side of `hmom` is `0`
for `n ≠ 0` — on the left because `0 ^ n = 0`, on the right because the integral is undefined. So
`hν` is what forces `ν`'s moments to exist at all.

The strengthening that *is* available replaces `hν` by moment-integrability of `ν`, which compact
support implies: with genuine moments, a Markov bound on `x i ^ (2 * m)` confines `ν` to the same
box. That is left to a follow-up; the Layer 6 consumer already has both mixing laws on a common
compact box.
decls.title: Multivariate moment determinacy, ambient form
decls.statement:
theorem Measure.ext_of_forall_integral_monomial_eq_of_support [Fintype ι] (hK : IsCompact K)
    {μ ν : Measure (ι → ℝ)} [IsFiniteMeasure μ] [IsFiniteMeasure ν]
    (hμ : μ Kᶜ = 0) (hν : ν Kᶜ = 0)
    (hmom : ∀ n : ι → ℕ, ∫ x, ∏ i, x i ^ n i ∂μ = ∫ x, ∏ i, x i ^ n i ∂ν) :
    μ = ν

decls.name: TauCeti.iteratedDeriv_complexMGF_id_zero
decls.doc:
The `n`-th derivative at `0` of the complex moment-generating function of `μ` is the `n`-th
complex moment `↑(∫ xⁿ dμ)`.  Immediate from `iteratedDeriv_complexMGF` at `z = 0`, where the
exponential factor is `1`.
decls.statement:
lemma iteratedDeriv_complexMGF_id_zero
    (hμ : (0 : ℝ) ∈ interior (integrableExpSet id μ)) (n : ℕ) :
    iteratedDeriv n (complexMGF id μ) 0 = ((∫ x, x ^ n ∂μ : ℝ) : ℂ)

decls.name: TauCeti.charFun_eq_of_forall_integral_pow_eq
decls.doc:
**Moment determinacy at the level of characteristic functions.** If two measures on `ℝ` have
finite exponential moments near `0` (so their complex moment-generating functions are analytic on a
strip about the imaginary axis) and agree on every polynomial moment `∫ xⁿ`, then their
characteristic functions coincide.
decls.title: Moment determinacy at the level of characteristic functions
decls.statement:
theorem charFun_eq_of_forall_integral_pow_eq
    (hμ : (0 : ℝ) ∈ interior (integrableExpSet id μ))
    (hν : (0 : ℝ) ∈ interior (integrableExpSet id ν))
    (hmom : ∀ n, ∫ x, x ^ n ∂μ = ∫ x, x ^ n ∂ν) :
    charFun μ = charFun ν

decls.name: TauCeti.Measure.ext_of_forall_integral_pow_eq
decls.doc:
**Moment determinacy for finite measures on `ℝ`.** A finite measure on `ℝ` with finite
exponential moments near `0` is determined by its polynomial moments `∫ xⁿ`.  Combines
`charFun_eq_of_forall_integral_pow_eq` with `MeasureTheory.Measure.ext_of_charFun`.
decls.title: Moment determinacy for finite measures on `ℝ`
decls.statement:
theorem Measure.ext_of_forall_integral_pow_eq [IsFiniteMeasure μ] [IsFiniteMeasure ν]
    (hμ : (0 : ℝ) ∈ interior (integrableExpSet id μ))
    (hν : (0 : ℝ) ∈ interior (integrableExpSet id ν))
    (hmom : ∀ n, ∫ x, x ^ n ∂μ = ∫ x, x ^ n ∂ν) :
    μ = ν

decls.name: TauCeti.zero_mem_interior_integrableExpSet_id_of_exists_integrable_exp
decls.doc:
If `∫ e^{a|x|} dμ` is finite for a single `a > 0`, then `0` lies in the interior of the
integrability set `integrableExpSet id μ`: for `|t| ≤ a` the exponential `e^{tx}` is dominated by
`e^{a|x|}`, so the open interval `(-a, a)` is contained in `integrableExpSet id μ`.
decls.statement:
lemma zero_mem_interior_integrableExpSet_id_of_exists_integrable_exp
    (h : ∃ a : ℝ, 0 < a ∧ Integrable (fun x => Real.exp (a * |x|)) μ) :
    (0 : ℝ) ∈ interior (integrableExpSet id μ)

decls.name: TauCeti.Measure.ext_of_forall_integral_pow_eq_of_exists_integrable_exp
decls.doc:
**Moment determinacy, exponential-moment form (the roadmap's B1 hypothesis).** A finite measure
on `ℝ` for which some exponential moment `∫ e^{a|x|} dμ` with `a > 0` is finite is determined by its
polynomial moments.  This is the form the completeness argument consumes: the hypothesis holds for
Gaussian decay and automatically for compactly supported measures.
decls.title: Moment determinacy, exponential-moment form (the roadmap's B1 hypothesis)
decls.statement:
theorem Measure.ext_of_forall_integral_pow_eq_of_exists_integrable_exp
    [IsFiniteMeasure μ] [IsFiniteMeasure ν]
    (hμ : ∃ a : ℝ, 0 < a ∧ Integrable (fun x => Real.exp (a * |x|)) μ)
    (hν : ∃ a : ℝ, 0 < a ∧ Integrable (fun x => Real.exp (a * |x|)) ν)
    (hmom : ∀ n, ∫ x, x ^ n ∂μ = ∫ x, x ^ n ∂ν) :
    μ = ν

decls.name: TauCeti.expNeg
decls.doc: The substitution `x ↦ e^{-x}`, which turns Laplace transforms into moments.
decls.statement: def expNeg (x : ℝ≥0) : ℝ

decls.name: TauCeti.expNeg_apply
decls.statement: theorem expNeg_apply (x : ℝ≥0) : expNeg x = Real.exp (-(x : ℝ))

decls.name: TauCeti.measurable_expNeg
decls.statement: theorem measurable_expNeg : Measurable expNeg

decls.name: TauCeti.injective_expNeg
decls.statement: theorem injective_expNeg : Function.Injective expNeg

decls.name: TauCeti.measurableEmbedding_expNeg
decls.statement: theorem measurableEmbedding_expNeg : MeasurableEmbedding expNeg

decls.name: TauCeti.abs_expNeg_le_one
decls.statement: theorem abs_expNeg_le_one (x : ℝ≥0) : |expNeg x| ≤ 1

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_integrable_exp_map_expNeg
decls.doc:
The pushforward under `x ↦ e^{-x}` has a finite exponential moment: it is carried by `(0, 1]`,
so `e^{|y|}` is bounded on it. This is the hypothesis
`Measure.ext_of_forall_integral_pow_eq_of_exists_integrable_exp` consumes.
decls.statement:
theorem exists_integrable_exp_map_expNeg (μ : Measure ℝ≥0) [IsFiniteMeasure μ] :
    ∃ a : ℝ, 0 < a ∧ Integrable (fun y => Real.exp (a * |y|)) (μ.map expNeg)

decls.name: TauCeti.Measure.ext_of_forall_integral_exp_neg_natCast_mul_eq
decls.doc:
**A finite measure on `ℝ≥0` is determined by its Laplace transform at the natural numbers.**

Substituting `y = e^{-x}` turns the value at `n` into the `n`-th moment of the pushforward, which is
carried by `(0, 1]` and so is moment-determinate.
decls.title: A finite measure on `ℝ≥0` is determined by its Laplace transform at the natural numbers
decls.statement:
theorem Measure.ext_of_forall_integral_exp_neg_natCast_mul_eq {μ ν : Measure ℝ≥0}
    [IsFiniteMeasure μ] [IsFiniteMeasure ν]
    (h : ∀ n : ℕ, ∫ x, Real.exp (-(n : ℝ) * (x : ℝ)) ∂μ
      = ∫ x, Real.exp (-(n : ℝ) * (x : ℝ)) ∂ν) :
    μ = ν

decls.name: TauCeti.Measure.ext_of_forall_integral_exp_neg_mul_eq
decls.doc:
**A finite measure on `ℝ≥0` is determined by its Laplace transform.** The convenience form
taking the hypothesis at every nonnegative real; the proof needs only the natural numbers, so
`Measure.ext_of_forall_integral_exp_neg_natCast_mul_eq` is the sharper statement.
decls.title: A finite measure on `ℝ≥0` is determined by its Laplace transform
decls.statement:
theorem Measure.ext_of_forall_integral_exp_neg_mul_eq {μ ν : Measure ℝ≥0}
    [IsFiniteMeasure μ] [IsFiniteMeasure ν]
    (h : ∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t →
      ∫ x, Real.exp (-t * (x : ℝ)) ∂μ = ∫ x, Real.exp (-t * (x : ℝ)) ∂ν) :
    μ = ν

decls.name: TauCeti.integrable_pow_of_exp_moment
decls.doc:
**One finite exponential moment makes every polynomial moment finite.**

The two-sided moment hypothesis of `ProbabilityTheory.integrable_pow_of_integrable_exp_mul` is
what a *single* symmetric moment `e^{a|x|} ∈ L¹(ν)` supplies: `±x ≤ |x|` makes `e^{a|x|}`
dominate both `e^{ax}` and `e^{-ax}`.

This is the bridge to the family-agnostic polynomial interface of
`TauCeti.MeasureTheory.Function.PolynomialMemLp`, whose hypothesis is exactly "every polynomial
moment is finite"; the `MemLp` statements of
`TauCeti.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.PolynomialCompleteness` are that interface applied through
this.
decls.title: One finite exponential moment makes every polynomial moment finite
decls.statement:
theorem integrable_pow_of_exp_moment
    (hexp : ∃ a : ℝ, 0 < a ∧ Integrable (fun x : ℝ => Real.exp (a * |x|)) ν) (k : ℕ) :
    Integrable (fun x : ℝ => x ^ k) ν

decls.name: TauCeti.integrable_toReal_ofReal_smul_pow
decls.doc:
Shared step for the positive and negative parts. If the truncation `f⁺` is pointwise dominated
by `|g|` and `e^{a|x|}·g` is integrable, every polynomial moment of the density `ofReal ∘ f` is
integrable. Applied below to `f = g` and `f = -g`.
decls.statement:
theorem integrable_toReal_ofReal_smul_pow (ha : 0 < a)
    (hexp : Integrable (fun x : ℝ => Real.exp (a * |x|) * g x) ν)
    (hfm : AEMeasurable (fun x : ℝ => ENNReal.ofReal (f x)) ν)
    (hle : ∀ x, |max (f x) 0| ≤ |g x|) (n : ℕ) :
    Integrable (fun x : ℝ => (ENNReal.ofReal (f x)).toReal • x ^ n) ν

decls.name: TauCeti.integrable_exp_withDensity_ofReal
decls.doc: Shared step: the density measure `(ofReal ∘ f) · ν` inherits the finite exponential moment.
decls.statement:
theorem integrable_exp_withDensity_ofReal
    (hexp : Integrable (fun x : ℝ => Real.exp (a * |x|) * g x) ν)
    (hfm : AEMeasurable (fun x : ℝ => ENNReal.ofReal (f x)) ν)
    (hlt : ∀ᵐ x ∂ν, ENNReal.ofReal (f x) < ⊤)
    (hle : ∀ x, |max (f x) 0| ≤ |g x|) :
    Integrable (fun x : ℝ => Real.exp (a * |x|))
      (ν.withDensity fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (f x))

decls.name: TauCeti.integrable_of_integrable_exp_mul_abs_mul
decls.doc:
An exponentially-weighted product bounds the function itself: since `e^{a|x|} ≥ 1` for
`a ≥ 0`, integrability of `e^{a|x|} · g` already gives integrability of `g`.
decls.statement:
theorem integrable_of_integrable_exp_mul_abs_mul (ha : 0 ≤ a)
    (hexp : Integrable (fun x : ℝ => Real.exp (a * |x|) * g x) ν) : Integrable g ν

decls.name: TauCeti.integral_pow_withDensity_ofReal_eq
decls.doc:
If `∫ xⁿ g` vanishes then the two truncations `g⁺` and `g⁻`, taken as densities against `ν`,
have the same `n`-th moment: their difference is `g` pointwise.
decls.statement:
theorem integral_pow_withDensity_ofReal_eq {n : ℕ}
    (hmeasp : AEMeasurable (fun x : ℝ => ENNReal.ofReal (g x)) ν)
    (hmeasn : AEMeasurable (fun x : ℝ => ENNReal.ofReal (-g x)) ν)
    (hintp : Integrable (fun x : ℝ => (ENNReal.ofReal (g x)).toReal • x ^ n) ν)
    (hintn : Integrable (fun x : ℝ => (ENNReal.ofReal (-g x)).toReal • x ^ n) ν)
    (hmom : ∫ x : ℝ, x ^ n * g x ∂ν = 0) :
    ∫ x, x ^ n ∂(ν.withDensity fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (g x))
      = ∫ x, x ^ n ∂(ν.withDensity fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (-g x))

decls.name: TauCeti.ae_eq_zero_of_forall_moment_eq_zero
decls.doc:
**Roadmap B1 (function level).** A real function on `ℝ` whose exponentially-weighted product
`e^{a|x|} · g` is integrable for some `a > 0`, and all of whose polynomial moments `∫ xⁿ g` vanish,
is a.e. zero.

This is the internal transfer step, not the form the completeness step consumes — that is the
measure-level `ae_eq_zero_of_forall_moment_eq_zero_of_exists_integrable_exp` below, which wraps this
one. `Measure.ext_of_forall_integral_pow_eq_of_exists_integrable_exp` in
`TauCeti.Probability.Moments.Determinacy` pins down a *measure* from its moments, and this transfers
that to a *function* by applying it to the positive and negative parts of `g` as densities
against `ν`.

The exponential hypothesis is the existential `∃ a > 0`, matching the engine's convention; a caller
holding a bound at every rate supplies it at any single one.

The reference measure is arbitrary, not just `volume`, and carries no σ-finiteness hypothesis: the
argument splits `g` into `g⁺`/`g⁻` as densities, and integrability of `g` already bounds the
positive density's lintegral, which is what lets equality of the two `withDensity` measures be read
back as equality of the densities. That generality is what lets weighted orthogonal families against
a measure other than Lebesgue (Hermite against a Gaussian, Chebyshev against `(1-x²)^{-1/2}` on
`[-1,1]`) reach the completeness step, through the measure-level form below.
decls.title: Roadmap B1 (function level)
decls.statement:
theorem ae_eq_zero_of_forall_moment_eq_zero (g : ℝ → ℝ)
    (hexp : ∃ a : ℝ, 0 < a ∧ Integrable (fun x : ℝ => Real.exp (a * |x|) * g x) ν)
    (hmom : ∀ n : ℕ, ∫ x : ℝ, x ^ n * g x ∂ν = 0) :
    g =ᵐ[ν] 0

decls.name: TauCeti.isFiniteMeasure_of_integrable_exp_mul_abs
decls.doc:
A measure carrying an integrable weight `e^{a|x|}` at a rate `a ≥ 0` is finite: that weight
dominates the constant `1`.
decls.statement:
theorem isFiniteMeasure_of_integrable_exp_mul_abs {a : ℝ} (ha : 0 ≤ a)
    (hexp : Integrable (fun x : ℝ => Real.exp (a * |x|)) ν) : IsFiniteMeasure ν

decls.name: TauCeti.memLp_two_algebraMap_pow_of_integrable_exp_mul_abs
decls.doc:
Every monomial, cast into `𝕜`, is square-integrable against a measure carrying an integrable
weight `e^{b|x|}` at a positive rate: that weight dominates `e^{±bx}`, which makes every polynomial
moment finite.
decls.statement:
theorem memLp_two_algebraMap_pow_of_integrable_exp_mul_abs {b : ℝ} (hb : 0 < b)
    (hexp : Integrable (fun x : ℝ => Real.exp (b * |x|)) ν) (n : ℕ) :
    MemLp (fun x : ℝ => (algebraMap ℝ 𝕜 x) ^ n) 2 ν

decls.name: TauCeti.integral_pow_mul_clm_eq_zero
decls.doc:
A real-linear functional passes through a vanishing monomial moment.  The monomial `xⁿ` is
real, so `L` commutes with multiplication by it, and `∫ xⁿ · L(g)` is `L` applied to the moment.
decls.statement:
theorem integral_pow_mul_clm_eq_zero (L : 𝕜 →L[ℝ] ℝ) {g : ℝ → 𝕜} {n : ℕ}
    (hint : Integrable (fun x : ℝ => (algebraMap ℝ 𝕜 x) ^ n * g x) ν)
    (hmom : ∫ x, (algebraMap ℝ 𝕜 x) ^ n * g x ∂ν = 0) :
    ∫ x : ℝ, x ^ n * L (g x) ∂ν = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.ae_eq_zero_of_forall_moment_eq_zero_of_exists_integrable_exp
decls.doc:
**Roadmap B1, measure level.** A measure `ν` on `ℝ` carrying one finite exponential moment is
moment-determinate, so a `g ∈ L²(ν)` orthogonal to every monomial is a.e. `0`.

The rate is existential, matching the convention of the engine this wraps and of the function-level
form above; a caller holding a bound at every rate supplies it at any single one.  Requiring it at
*every* rate would exclude exponentially-tailed weights such as `e^{-|x|}`, for which
`∫ e^{a|x|} dν` is finite only for `a < 1`, even though they are moment-determinate all the same.
The `_of_exists_integrable_exp` suffix names the hypothesis exactly — *existence* of one positive
rate with `e^{a|x|}` integrable — and matches the adjacent determinacy API
(`Measure.ext_of_forall_integral_pow_eq_of_exists_integrable_exp`).  The roadmap name
`_of_finite_expMoments`, with the matching *all-rates* hypothesis, wraps this one immediately below.

Finiteness of `ν` is not a separate hypothesis: `e^{a|x|} ≥ 1`.
decls.title: Roadmap B1, measure level
decls.statement:
theorem ae_eq_zero_of_forall_moment_eq_zero_of_exists_integrable_exp
    (hexp : ∃ a : ℝ, 0 < a ∧ Integrable (fun x : ℝ => Real.exp (a * |x|)) ν)
    {g : ℝ → 𝕜} (hg : MemLp g 2 ν)
    (hmom : ∀ n : ℕ, ∫ x, (algebraMap ℝ 𝕜 x) ^ n * g x ∂ν = 0) :
    g =ᵐ[ν] 0

decls.name: TauCeti.ae_eq_zero_of_forall_moment_eq_zero_of_finite_expMoments
decls.doc:
**Roadmap B1, measure level** (roadmap-specified API name).  The name `_of_finite_expMoments`
is accurate here: the hypothesis is that *every* exponential moment is finite -- `e^{a|x|}` is
integrable at every rate `a ≥ 0` -- which is the roadmap signature.  This is strictly stronger than
the primary `_of_exists_integrable_exp`, and follows from it immediately by using the moment at any
single positive rate.
decls.title: Roadmap B1, measure level
decls.statement:
theorem ae_eq_zero_of_forall_moment_eq_zero_of_finite_expMoments
    (hexp : ∀ a : ℝ, 0 ≤ a → Integrable (fun x : ℝ => Real.exp (a * |x|)) ν)
    {g : ℝ → 𝕜} (hg : MemLp g 2 ν)
    (hmom : ∀ n : ℕ, ∫ x, (algebraMap ℝ 𝕜 x) ^ n * g x ∂ν = 0) :
    g =ᵐ[ν] 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.tailFamily
decls.doc: The σ-algebra generated by the future coordinates `X k` with `n ≤ k`.
decls.statement: def tailFamily (X : (k : ℕ) → Ω → β k) (n : ℕ) : MeasurableSpace Ω

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.tailProcess
decls.doc: The tail σ-algebra of a process, expressed as Mathlib's `limsup` tail σ-algebra.
decls.statement: def tailProcess (X : (k : ℕ) → Ω → β k) : MeasurableSpace Ω

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.tailFamily_eq_iSup_comap
decls.doc: Normal form for the future σ-algebra generated by coordinates from `n` onward.
decls.statement:
theorem tailFamily_eq_iSup_comap (X : (k : ℕ) → Ω → β k) (n : ℕ) :
    tailFamily X n =
      ⨆ k : {k : ℕ // n ≤ k}, MeasurableSpace.comap (X k.1) inferInstance

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.tailProcess_eq_limsup
decls.doc: The process-relative tail σ-algebra is Mathlib's `limsup` tail σ-algebra.
decls.statement:
theorem tailProcess_eq_limsup (X : (k : ℕ) → Ω → β k) :
    tailProcess X = limsup (fun k => MeasurableSpace.comap (X k) inferInstance) atTop

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.tailProcess_eq_iInf_tailFamily
decls.doc: Normal form for the process-relative tail σ-algebra.
decls.statement:
theorem tailProcess_eq_iInf_tailFamily (X : (k : ℕ) → Ω → β k) :
    tailProcess X = ⨅ n : ℕ, tailFamily X n

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.measurable_tailFamily_of_le
decls.doc: A future coordinate is measurable with respect to the corresponding future σ-algebra.

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.tailFamily_le_iff
decls.doc: Universal property of the future σ-algebra generated by coordinates from `n` onward.
decls.statement:
theorem tailFamily_le_iff {X : (k : ℕ) → Ω → β k} {n : ℕ} {m : MeasurableSpace Ω} :
    tailFamily X n ≤ m ↔ ∀ k, n ≤ k → Measurable[m] (X k)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.tailFamily_antitone
decls.doc: The future σ-algebras of a process form a decreasing family.
decls.statement:
theorem tailFamily_antitone (X : (k : ℕ) → Ω → β k) :
    Antitone (tailFamily X)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.tailProcess_le_tailFamily
decls.doc: The tail σ-algebra is contained in every future σ-algebra.
decls.statement:
theorem tailProcess_le_tailFamily (X : (k : ℕ) → Ω → β k) (n : ℕ) :
    tailProcess X ≤ tailFamily X n

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.tailFamily_eq_comap_shift
decls.doc:
The future σ-algebra `tailFamily X r` is the σ-algebra generated by the `r`-shifted tail
`ω ↦ (X (r + ·) ω)`, viewed as a single (product-valued) random variable.
decls.statement:
theorem tailFamily_eq_comap_shift (X : (k : ℕ) → Ω → β k) (r : ℕ) :
    tailFamily X r = MeasurableSpace.comap (fun ω n => X (r + n) ω) inferInstance

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.tailFamily_le_ambient
decls.doc:
If all coordinates are ambient-measurable, then each future σ-algebra is a sub-σ-algebra of
the ambient one.
decls.statement:
theorem tailFamily_le_ambient {X : (k : ℕ) → Ω → β k} (n : ℕ)
    (hX : ∀ k, n ≤ k → Measurable (X k)) :
    tailFamily X n ≤ (inferInstance : MeasurableSpace Ω)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.tailProcess_le_ambient
decls.doc:
If the coordinates from some cutoff `n` onward are ambient-measurable, then the tail σ-algebra
is a sub-σ-algebra of the ambient one.  The tail does not see the finitely many initial
coordinates, so only eventual measurability is required.
decls.statement:
theorem tailProcess_le_ambient {X : (k : ℕ) → Ω → β k} (n : ℕ)
    (hX : ∀ k, n ≤ k → Measurable (X k)) :
    tailProcess X ≤ (inferInstance : MeasurableSpace Ω)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.pathTail
decls.doc: The path-space tail σ-algebra, i.e. the tail of the coordinate process on `ℕ → α`.
decls.statement: abbrev pathTail (α : Type*) [MeasurableSpace α] : MeasurableSpace (ℕ → α)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.pathTail_eq_tailProcess
decls.doc: Normal form for the path-space tail σ-algebra.
decls.statement:
theorem pathTail_eq_tailProcess :
    pathTail α = tailProcess (fun k (x : ℕ → α) => x k)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.pathTail_le_tailFamily
decls.doc:
The path-space tail σ-algebra is contained in every future path σ-algebra from time `n`
onward.
decls.statement:
theorem pathTail_le_tailFamily (n : ℕ) :
    pathTail α ≤ tailFamily (fun k (x : ℕ → α) => x k) n

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.processCons
decls.doc:
Cons a head random variable onto a sequence-valued one (a pointwise `Stream'.cons`):
`processCons x t = [x, t 0, t 1, …]`.
decls.statement: def processCons (x : Ω → α) (t : Ω → ℕ → α) : Ω → ℕ → α

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.processCons_zero
decls.doc: Leading coordinate of a cons: `processCons x t ω 0 = x ω`.
decls.statement: theorem processCons_zero (x : Ω → α) (t : Ω → ℕ → α) (ω : Ω) : processCons x t ω 0 = x ω

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.processCons_succ
decls.doc: Later coordinates of a cons: `processCons x t ω (n + 1) = t ω n`.
decls.statement:
theorem processCons_succ (x : Ω → α) (t : Ω → ℕ → α) (ω : Ω) (n : ℕ) :
    processCons x t ω (n + 1) = t ω n

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.processTail
decls.doc:
Drop the leading coordinate of a sequence-valued random variable (a pointwise `Stream'.tail`):
`processTail t ω n = t ω (n+1)`.
decls.statement: def processTail (t : Ω → ℕ → α) : Ω → ℕ → α

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.processTail_apply
decls.doc: Coordinate equation for `processTail`: its `n`th coordinate is `t (n + 1)`.
decls.statement: theorem processTail_apply (t : Ω → ℕ → α) (ω : Ω) (n : ℕ) : processTail t ω n = t ω (n + 1)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.processTail_processCons
decls.doc: The tail of a cons recovers the original sequence.
decls.statement:
theorem processTail_processCons (x : Ω → α) (t : Ω → ℕ → α) :
    processTail (processCons x t) = t

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.processCons_processTail
decls.doc: Reconstruct a sequence from its head and tail (the reverse of `processTail_processCons`).
decls.statement:
theorem processCons_processTail (t : Ω → ℕ → α) :
    processCons (fun ω => t ω 0) (processTail t) = t

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.measurable_processCons
decls.doc: Consing a measurable head onto a process is measurable when its coordinates `t (· ·)` are.
decls.statement:
theorem measurable_processCons {x : Ω → α} {t : Ω → ℕ → α} (hx : Measurable x)
    (ht : ∀ n, Measurable fun ω => t ω n) : Measurable (processCons x t)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.measurable_processTail
decls.doc: The tail of a process is measurable when its tail coordinates `t (· + 1)` are.
decls.statement:
theorem measurable_processTail {t : Ω → ℕ → α} (ht : ∀ n, Measurable fun ω => t ω (n + 1)) :
    Measurable (processTail t)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.comap_processTail_le
decls.doc:
The tail of a sequence-valued random variable generates a coarser σ-algebra than the variable
itself.
decls.statement:
theorem comap_processTail_le {t : Ω → ℕ → α} :
    MeasurableSpace.comap (processTail t) inferInstance
      ≤ MeasurableSpace.comap t inferInstance

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.comap_le_comap_processCons
decls.doc:
Consing a head onto a sequence-valued random variable refines its σ-algebra: `σ(t) ≤
σ(processCons x t)`.
decls.statement:
theorem comap_le_comap_processCons (x : Ω → α) (t : Ω → ℕ → α) :
    MeasurableSpace.comap t inferInstance ≤ MeasurableSpace.comap (processCons x t) inferInstance

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.comap_processCons_eq_sup
decls.doc:
Consing a head onto a sequence-valued random variable joins their σ-algebras:
`σ(processCons x t) = σ(x) ⊔ σ(t)`.
decls.statement:
theorem comap_processCons_eq_sup (x : Ω → α) (t : Ω → ℕ → α) :
    MeasurableSpace.comap (processCons x t) inferInstance
      = MeasurableSpace.comap x inferInstance ⊔ MeasurableSpace.comap t inferInstance

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.tailReverseFiltration
decls.doc: Reverse filtration of the process-tail family on the finite horizon `N`.
decls.statement:
def tailReverseFiltration (X : (k : ℕ) → Ω → β k) (hX : ∀ k, Measurable (X k))
    (N : ℕ) : Filtration ℕ (inferInstance : MeasurableSpace Ω)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.tailReverseFiltration_apply
decls.doc: Level equation for the finite-horizon reverse filtration of a process tail.
decls.statement:
theorem tailReverseFiltration_apply (X : (k : ℕ) → Ω → β k)
    (hX : ∀ k, Measurable (X k)) (N n : ℕ) :
    (tailReverseFiltration X hX N) n = tailFamily X (N - n)

decls.name: TauCeti.Probability.tailProcess_eq_iInf_revFiltration
decls.doc:
The process tail is the infimum of the time-zero levels of the finite-horizon reverse
filtrations attached to `tailFamily X`.
decls.statement:
theorem tailProcess_eq_iInf_revFiltration (X : (k : ℕ) → Ω → β k)
    (hX : ∀ k, Measurable (X k)) :
    tailProcess X = ⨅ N : ℕ, (tailReverseFiltration X hX N) 0
